News.title: Body found in month-long search for kayaker, 19, who capsized at sea after family pay tribute to ‘keen sportsman’
News.content:
TRAGIC END Body found in month-long search for kayaker, 19, who capsized at sea after family pay tribute to ‘keen sportsman’

A BODY has been found during a month-long search for a 19-year-old kayaker whose boat capsized.

Michael Henry, from the Rothbury area, was feared dead after his kayak tipped over in the sea near Boulmer, Northumberland, on July 7.

Northumbria Police have been conducting extensive searches for Michael’s body since HM Coastguard called cops about a kayak containing two men capsizing.

One of the men managed to swim from the small boat to a buoy while Michael remained unaccounted for.





The coastguard rescued the man from the buoy and launched a frantic search for Michael.

Following the tragic discovery, a formal identification has taken place and a report has been prepared for the coroner.

Michael’s family, who are being supported by specialist officers, paid tribute to Michael on July 15 when he was reported as presumed dead.

His family said: “We would like to thank everyone for all their love, kindness and support now and throughout Michael’s life; it was that love and kindness that made him the marvellous person he was.



“Michael was a much-loved son, brother, grandson, nephew, team-mate and friend; a keen sportsman who loved the outdoors.

“Michael was preparing to go travelling this summer and hoping to start university next academic year. Michael will be forever in our thoughts, and we will miss him.

“Our thanks go to the emergency services and everyone who is helping to search for Michael.”

At the time police were conducting their searches, Chief Inspector Jon Caisley, of Northumbria Police, said: “This is a tragic update to share, and I would like to extend our deepest sympathies to Michael’s family and friends.



“Despite extensive searches at sea and on the coast, we have been unable to find Michael and he is sadly believed to have died at sea.

“We know the impact this news will have upon his loved ones and the wider community.”

Chief Insp Caisley added: “I would also like to thank all of our officers and partners to their assistance in the search efforts to find Michael.

“We would continue to ask that people respect the family’s privacy at this time.”

News.title: Moment idiot ‘bus surfer’ gets his comeuppance as he falls & faceplants onto road after losing grip on double-decker
News.content:
THIS is the shocking moment a stupid “bus surfer” gets his comeuppance as he falls onto the road having lost his grip on a double-decker.

The idiotic man was seen clinging on to the rear of the Number 297 in London going 30mph.



But he then lost his hold when he tried to get off as the red Routemaster indicated to pull into a bus stop.

He initially put both feet, wearing blue Crocs, on the road surface but then lost his footing.



The man – also wearing shorts and a blue jacket – then face-planted the tarmac.

He then rolled over towards the pavement on the A4088, Neasden Lane North near the junction with Press Road, Neasden, northwest London.



A passenger in a car travelling behind the bus filmed it on their mobile phone.

The idiotic stunt – known as bus surfing – is often done to avoid paying a bus fare.



An adult pay as you go ticket on Transport for London services is just £1.75 per journey.

It happened on July 31.

Local Jamie Lunkin said: “£1.75 by the way.”

Russell Longman said: “Holding on where the engine is ain’t the best place.

“F*****g doughnut.”



Mohsin Khan compared it to a scene from Back to the Future and joked: “When Marty Mcfly forgot his skateboard at home

Lee Hemans said: “He really did that wearing Crocs?

Elinia added: “Why would he do it in Crocs?”

Kabij said: “Wouldn’t happen if he put the Crocs in sport mode.”

Transport for London and the London Ambulance Service have been approached for comment.

The Met Police declined to comment.

In April, two men were spotted bus surfing on the back of the Number 114 on Mollison Way, Burnt Oak, Edgware, North London.

News.title: Two workers killed in Japanese mall blast after boss told them to re-enter earthquake-hit shopping centre to rescue cash
News.content:
TWO workers died in a shopping mall explosion after their boss ordered them back into the earthquake-stricken building to retrieve cash.

The pair were among the 38 people who died in the 7.1 magnitude earthquake at Kumamoto, Japan last week.



Their employer at Habita in the Aeon Mall has apologised for the fatal instruction that resulted in the “loss of two precious lives.”

One of the workers has been identified as 22-year-old Kurumi Otake.



The identity of the other deceased employee has not been made public.

Otake evacuated from the Aeon shopping mall in Kashima following the earthquake on July 28 but was later seen re-entering the building.

Company sales manager Goji Yuse admitted the company had instructed the two workers to put sales proceeds into the safe.

It is understood the store later collapsed following an explosion.



Two company representatives attended Otake’a wake on Sunday and apologised to her family.

They said: “Looking back now it was not worth a life.”

Her mother said: “My daughter is not coming back.

“I wished someone had stopped her.”

Otake’s relative described her as someone with a “strong sense of justice”.



The relative said: “If she hadn’t gone back in side the store at the time, Kurumi would still be with her family today.”

The mall’s operator said it believes the explosion was due to a gas leak.

It occurred after about 3,000 shoppers had been evacuated to a car park following the quake but some employees remained inside.



Seven of the earthquakes total fatalities were from Aeon Mall.

The earthquake has left 114 people injured across Kumamoto, authorities said.

Some 700 homes were destroyed, and more than 11,300 buildings were damaged, according to Kumamoto prefecture.

More than 8,500 people remain at crowded emergency shelters, such as converted community centers, school gyms and classrooms, many of which lack air-conditioning.

Others are sleeping in cars at town hall parking lots and parks, or outside of their homes.



Intense heat and a lack of water supplies have complicated repair efforts.

More than 46,000 households remain without water and many also face fuel shortages as the region suffers the sweltering heat.

One woman has died from heatstroke after she was forced to sleep in her car, the Independent reports.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

The woman, in her 70s, was found on July 30 in a vehicle that had run out of petrol in Kumamoto prefecture.

Japan Meteorological Agency predicted that temperatures would rise close to 40C on Monday.

News.title: My uncle’s twisted abuse left me terrified of summer hols… years later I snared him into shocking Facebook confession
News.content:
SCROLLING through Facebook, Angel Buxton saw a face she recognised and felt instantly sick.

As she read the words about how a “monstrous” paedophile had been jailed for filming himself abusing a child, a rush of guilt came over her.





The man in the image accompanying the news article was her uncle – and he had sexually abused her as a child, too.

Angel was just five years old when the abuse started in 2003, while her dad’s younger brother George Bellwood was 10, and the pair would play together at their nan’s house in the Lake District during the summer holidays.

She recalls how George, now 34, was “trusted to take care” of his little niece, but little did her father or grandmother know of the true horror that was unfolding.

Angel, now 27, says: “They had no clue. If my dad was home, he’d be none the wiser watching TV and Nan always thought I was safe too.

“My first memory is Uncle George kissing me with his tongue. I remember the colour, smell, furniture, everything. He was old enough to know what he was doing. He would force himself on me, putting his hands in my pants.”

Angel says the abuse would continue every time she visited her dad, who lived with his mother, Angel’s nan.

Five years later, when Angel was 10 and George was 15, he would bombard her with gifts and pretend to be her boyfriend.

She says: “He’d ask if I had a boyfriend yet, and if I knew what to do with one.





“He started asking sexual questions and showing me how to do things, pretending to be boyfriend and girlfriend.

“He’d tell me how special I was, that I was his favourite niece and there was no-one like me.

“Every Christmas, Easter, birthday, he’d give me a present in front of the family. I had lots of Barbies and teddy bears. He looked like the perfect, loving uncle.”

As Angel grew older, so did the hold her depraved uncle had over her, as he begged her not to tell anyone.

She says: “He always said I wasn’t allowed to tell anyone or I’d be in trouble and so would he.

“He said the police are bad guys and they’d put him away and that my dad and my nan would never believe me.”

The abuse continued until Angel was 12 years old, when her family moved away and George, then 17, got a girlfriend. However, their paths still crossed, leaving Angel terrified.

She says: “I’d still see him at family occasions and felt a loyalty to him as a niece, but I was scared.”



It was only when Angel became a mum for the first time that she realised just how serious the abuse she had suffered as a child was – and finally felt able to speak up.

In 2019, she sent a group text to her family, telling them how George had spent years abusing her – but he managed to “talk everyone out of it.”

Fearing she would never be believed, Angel knew she had to get George to admit to what he did himself – so messaged him on Facebook.

“I confronted him, telling him he had ruined my childhood and had taken years away from me. I told him how it was eating me alive that our family didn’t know the truth.

“He replied saying he wished he could take it all back, he was sorry and that he hated himself. He begged me not to tell anyone.

“I took screenshots and sent it to my family and I also went to the police.”

Police interviewed Angel about the messages but the stress became too much for her and she asked the police to drop the case.

Angel was keen to move on with her life, and went on to have four more children. But then in 2024 while scrolling through Facebook, Angel froze on the spot when she saw her uncle’s face appear in her newsfeed.



The article revealed how he had been jailed for 21 years for 19 offences – including raping a child under 13 years old. The court heard how he would give the victim his phone as a form of distraction whilst he carried out his horrific sex acts over a number of years.

Jailing him at Durham Crown Court, Judge Joanne Kidd said he had carried out the “most heinous, monstrous and violent abuse” during a “campaign of rape”.

Angel says: “I felt physically sick. I also felt guilty, because if I’d come forward this would never have happened.

“I’d only seen my uncle months before at our nan’s funeral. I rang the police, furious. I wanted my own justice.

“The officer told me they were happy to make a new case and took my statement and his confession to the CPS. This time, I was ready.”

With her uncle already starting his prison sentence, he was then charged with five counts of sexual assault against Angel.



While she awaited his trial, Angel went through further hell when her baby daughter died.

She explains: “I was nine months pregnant and was induced, but she had no heartbeat and died from a lack of oxygen.

“As she died, my officer called me to tell me George had pleaded not guilty. It was horrendous.”

In December last year, during George’s trial for the abuse against her, Angel bravely gave a victim statement.

She said: “Throughout the years of abuse as a child I was scared, I was made to believe it was my fault, and that no-one would believe me.

“This affected my daily life from sleeping, socialising, trusting, and engaging in what should have been normal activities. I lived in fear he’d come back for more or find it in other children as I grew up and got older.

“I hope prison brings him time to reflect on the things he has done. He stole my innocence and childhood, the colour from my life, and he made my days a living hell.”

It took just 15 minutes for the jury to give a guilty verdict and his 21-year sentence was increased to 24 years.

With her uncle finally behind bars, Angel is now trying to move on with her life.

She says: “I’ll never mentally or physically recover from this but I won’t be held back by him any longer.



“A lot of family haven’t been a support but I have my beautiful kids and my partner by my side.”

News.title: Mystery as thousands of ‘creepy’ giant spider crabs swarm popular UK tourist hotspot overnight
News.content:
THOUSANDS of “creepy” giant spider crabs mysteriously swarmed a popular UK tourist hotspot overnight.

Commercial fisherman Daniel Gilbert, 37, was heading out on his boat when he was confronted with the astonishing sight.



Daniel was left stunned after discovering hordes of giant spider crabs crawling around Newquay Harbour.

Footage shows the huge crustaceans carpeting the harbour floor and clambering over each other, trying to scale the harbour wall.



The gathering of crabs appeared to have arrived overnight, covering the shallows of the harbour.

In the video, Daniel tells viewers that “these are not stones”, but instead a “vast invasion” of spider crabs.



Pictures show the harbour walls covered in limpets and barnacles, which the grey-blue crabs seemed to be using to climb up.

Daniel was also joined by local seals called Jimmy and Sandra.



They appeared intrigued by the influx of crabs and bobbed next to his boat.

The fisherman said the crabs were in the middle of their annual shedding process, during which they lose their hard outer shells and temporarily become incredibly soft.

He said: “The shedding process takes a month – they go like jelly. You can pick them up; they’re just like jelly.



“They look dead but they are alive. Honestly, it’s quite creepy.”

Daniel said the spectacle is an annual occurrence around July and August, and is something he has witnessed throughout his years as a fisherman.

He said: “I see it every year. I’ve been a fisherman since a young lad.”



However, even though he is accustomed to seeing the crabs arrive, he was taken aback by the sheer scale of this year’s gathering.

Daniel said: “I was very surprised; I’d never seen so many at one time at the harbour.

“Honestly, I can’t get over how many there are. Imagine standing on all that. It would hurt, wouldn’t it?”

The fisherman also urged people visiting Newquay to head down and see the unusual sight for themselves.

He added: “You very rarely get to see this. It’s an amazing sight, to be honest.”

News.title: Man who claimed EV malfunctioned when he struck cops 31 TIMES during 38-mile ‘terror ride’ in elaborate con is jailed
News.content:
A MAN who said his Jaguar EV malfunctioned when he hit cops 31 times in a 38-mile “terror ride” as part of an elaborate con has been banged up.

Nathan Owen, 33, has been jailed for four years and three months after claiming his flash motor wouldn’t brake.



His lies were part of a “frighteningly stupid” attempt to avoid paying his car finance, Liverpool Crown Court heard today, August 3.

He collided with a police car more than 30 times as officers attempted to stop him after he phoned emergency services to tell them his vehicle was accelerating and not in his control.



Owen drove at speeds of up to 86mph on the M58, M57 and M62 in Merseyside for about 35 minutes, over a distance of about 38 miles, during the incident on March 6 2024.

Sentencing him, Judge Ian Unsworth KC said: “You set in train a course of conduct which caused a significant police traffic operation to be deployed, undoubted alarm to the public and very substantial loss and disruption to others.”

The judge said police officers placed themselves in danger because they believed they were dealing with a genuine emergency.

Addressing Owen, he added: “You, meanwhile, sought to profit from a lie.”



Eric Lamb, prosecuting, said Owen, of Prestatyn, North Wales, had entered into a finance agreement in September 2023 for the Jaguar I-Pace.

He ran into “financial difficulties” and was in arrears with CA Auto Finance by March the following year with about £5,000 left to pay, the court heard.

On the day of the incident, he called loan company Plata to ask if he would be able to borrow more on top of the £3,000 he had already loaned from them but was told he could not.

Five minutes later, shortly after 2pm, he called 999 claiming his car would not brake and he had no control over the vehicle, which he said was accelerating.

Mr Lamb said: “In fact, his car was stationary at the time of that call.”



Police attended and the car, which was then travelling at speeds of up to 86mph, had to be boxed off by emergency service vehicles to keep other road users safe before it came to a stop on the M62 near Warrington, Cheshire.

Investigations found there was no fault with the car, the court heard.

Mr Lamb said: “He had fabricated the events in order to enable him to get rid of the vehicle.

“He had full control of the vehicle and with full control of the vehicle he travelled at excessive and extreme speeds.”

Motorways had to be closed because of the incident, the court heard.



Footage of the police pursuit of Owen was played in court, along with the audio from his 999 call, in which he was heard telling an operator he was “shaking” and the car had “gone crazy”.

When the car was eventually brought to a stop the brake lights could be seen turning on.

Owen contacted the finance company 40 minutes after the incident.

In a statement, Murray Paul, from Jaguar Land Rover UK, said the firm had spent an extra £50million in marketing to try and counter the publicity from the false allegations, which they said generated 180 pieces of adverse media coverage.

Daniel Travers, defending, said Owen’s actions were “frighteningly stupid”.



He said Owen, who had no previous convictions and came from a “successful, stable family”, had been described by his father as a Walter Mitty character who “lives in a fantasy world”.

He added: “He had grand ideas and things just went wrong.”

Owen pleaded guilty to dangerous driving and two counts of fraud in June.

He was banned from driving for a period of five years after his release from custody.

Speaking after the sentencing, Detective Constable Michael Doyle said: “It was clear from our investigations that he was in full control of his vehicle throughout the duration of the incident.

“By his own admission there were workers on the hard shoulder of the motorway, and he clearly put them and other road users in danger with his reckless actions.”

A charge of causing a public nuisance was ordered to lie on the file.

News.title: Afghan migrant who ‘killed Brit & hid her body in suitcase’ is pictured after his wife ‘found him at victim’s apartment’
News.content:
THE Afghan man arrested over the murder of a British woman in Athens is a champion boxer who ran a refugee charity in the Greek capital.

Sharif Ahmadzai, 26, is suspected of killing Elisabeth-Jane Ross, 38, before stuffing her body in a suitcase and dumping it in an abandoned building on July 16.



He is also accused of using the Scottish national’s bank cards to withdraw thousands of Euros.

CCTV allegedly showed Ahmadzai leaving the apartment where Elisabeth was staying with a suitcase and dumping it where her remains were found, the Daily Mail reports.



Ahmadzai arrived in Lesvos in 2016, and later married US-born Alaina Hall in 2023.

The couple set up a ministry to help refugees in Athens and are believed to have known Elisabeth through their work.



They also had a key to the flat she was staying in – which was owned by their organisation, Love Every Nation Athens.

Ahmadzai’s wife allegedly reported her husband to cops after she became suspicious he was involved in Elisabeth’s death.



She said she woke up on the evening of July 15 to find him missing, but when she checked his shared location it showed him at Elisabeth’s apartment.

Ahmadzai had also given her 2,550 euros (£2,200) and a new iPhone 17 Pro, which she believed was bought using money stolen from Elisabeth’s bank accounts.

A Greek police source told The Times: “The testimony of the wife has been crucial and it would appear that she did not want to be part of the crime committed by her husband.



“Without her and CCTV evidence, we would not have been able to find this man.”

Ahmadzai has been charged with murder, robbery and illegal possession of a weapon. He is expected to appear at court in Athens this week.

His website states his father, a military commander in Kabul, was shot dead in a Taliban ambush when he was four.



Five years later his older brother was kidnapped by the Taliban and when he was 15 the rest of his family was wiped out in a suicide car bomb, the website says.

After travelling to Greece in a small boat, Ahmadzai went on to win the Greek super lightweight boxing title in March 2023.

Elisabeth arrived in the Greek capital on a flight from Edinburgh on June 26.

Police believe she was killed not far from where her body was found in the abandoned building in Kypseli.

Initial medical reports suggest Elisabeth died from asphyxiation, The Times reports, citing a case file.



Her phone was used to send messages and mislead her loved ones until her identity was made public on July 29.

Her dad, a lawyer from Edinburgh, said he received texts for up to two weeks after her death.

Messages sent to family and friends claimed that she needed to take some time for herself and wanted to be alone for a while.

Her aunt, Anne Bangham, described her as a “beautiful loving and kind young lady”.

Elisabeth regularly travelled to Greece to volunteer with NGOs, working with refugee centres including the One Heart organisation in Athens.



The Foreign and Commonwealth Office said earlier: “Our thoughts are with Elisabeth’s family during this difficult time.

“We are providing consular support and are in contact with the local authorities.”

RECOMMENDED STORIES

A Police Scotland spokesperson said: “We are aware of the death of a Scottish woman in Athens and are liaising with authorities in Greece.

“Officers are providing support to her family in Scotland.”

News.title: Rod Liddle was a caustic but crucial voice on the madness of modern Britain and the explosive issues of gender & race
News.content:
NEWSPAPER pundits are ten a penny. They come and they go, often without trace.

The Sun’s Rod Liddle by contrast is simply irreplaceable.



Rod’s tragic and untimely death at 66 robs us of a controversial, caustic but crucial voice on the madness that is modern Britain.

His weekly columns, much missed in recent times, took a fiercely hilarious poke at the cant and hypocrisy of polarised UK politics.



He loved to flirt with danger, deliberately skating on thin ice over such explosive issues as gender, race and religion.

“His columns make the hair stand up on the back of your neck,” said one veteran editor.



They also made us laugh out loud – a rare and precious talent.

Our star columnist would have been deeply moved by the expressions of public grief as the shock news of his death broke this afternoon.



Tributes more usually associated with the death of a famous pop star flashed non-stop across our screens.

Rod Liddle earned their affection by speaking in their name, pricking the pomposity of po-faced trans-fanatics and puncture the absurdity of Gay Pride pro-Gaza marchers.

His prolific views on race, immigration and multiculturalism constantly landed him in hot water, his favourite spot.

His far-sighted 2005 C4 broadcast, Immigration is a Time Bomb, was denounced by race warriors.

Liddle’s columns on politics, football – he was a Millwall supporter – and rock ‘n’ roll won fierce loyalty from his readers of The Sun, the Spectator, The Sunday Times and Times Radio where he had a regular Saturday slot.



I like to claim a hand in his popular role as a newspaper columnist, suggesting his first column for The Sun in 2012.

But he soon eclipsed me and would have been a star in any publication that chose to use his material.

His first outing was a typically ferocious attack on the BBC over the Jimmy Savile scandal, headlined: “Liar, Liar, Aunt’s on Fire”.



Rod’s criticism was all the more effective because of his experience as a precociously young editor of the BBC Today programme.

Rod parted company with the Beeb when executives tried to ban him from writing newspaper articles clashing with broadcasting policy.

Liddle was proudly working class, working at 16 as a reporter on the South Wales Echo where he wrote his first column – about rock music.



But he was formidably bright and took a degree in social psychology as a mature student at the prestigious London School of Economics.

His politics began on the far left, first with the Socialist Workers Party, then as a mainstream Labour supporter and writing speeches for the party of the Labour Party.

But he joined the breakaway Social Democratic Party and in 2019 suggested the election election be held on a Muslim religious holiday to reduce the Labour vote.

Perhaps surprisingly, given his scepticism, he was a practising Christian and wrote extensively about faith, not least Islam.

He was also a big softie, a lifelong animal rights campaigner who detested the hunting of foxes, fish, hares and badgers for pleasure.



RECOMMENDED STORIES

For Rod Liddle his right to say so and to write about them in a free press was sacred.

We will miss him enormously.

News.title: Donald Trump blasted after he shares AI photo of himself with Abraham Lincoln
News.content:
Donald Trump blasted after he shares AI photo of himself with Abraham Lincoln

Donald Trump is seen sat next to George Washington and Abraham Lincoln in the bizarre image shared by the US president in what appears to be his latest experiment with AI

View 2 Images Donald Trump is shown with Abraham Lincoln and George Washington in the bizarre new image

Donald Trump has been branded "deranged" after he shared a bizarre AI portrait of himself sat next to George Washington and Abraham Lincoln.

‌



The world leader, 80, posted the image of himself with the two US presidents - widely considered the greatest in American history - in his latest spree on his Truth Social platform on Sunday night.

‌



In the mock-up painting, Mr Trump is seen at a wooden table alongside Mr Washington and Mr Lincoln, with what appears to be an upside-down map of the United States placed in front of them.

‌



Mr Trump, who has developed a habit of posting strange, often crude pictures on his social media, did not explain why he had shared it.

Donald Trump faces cheating allegations again after winning another golf tournament READ MORE :

View 2 Images Mr Trump did not explain why he posted the image (Image: AFP via Getty Images)

Another AI-generated image shared a few hours earlier showed a slimmed-down Mr Trump in an Elvis-style low-cut jumpsuit exposing his bare chest, decorated with two sequined bald eagles.

‌



He also likened himself to the American War of Independence hero in another image on Sunday, which showed his face spliced half-and-half with Washington's.

The digital poster, which again appeared likely to have been created with an AI model, read: '250 years - in God We Trust'.

It marks Mr Trump's latest effort to spin the 250th anniversary of the founding of the United States with his own political career, with him frequently attempting to cast his own political movement as a modern continuation of the American Revolution.

‌



This summer, critics accused the president of politicising the anniversary by staging campaign-style rallies and diverting federal funds to his "Freedom 250" task force, undermining a bipartisan commission established by Congress a decade earlier.

MAGA supporters went on to recirculate the image of Mr Trump with Lincoln and Washington on X (formerly Twitter), claiming it showed "three American legends."

But critics were quick to turn the tables on the US president in their own pictures, mischievously swapping out Mr Washington and Mr Lincoln for the late sex offender Jeffrey Epstein to taunt the president over his ongoing second-term scandal.

Article continues below

Another user edited Mr Trump into a clown, while one critic labelled the president's original post as "deranged."

Mr Trump's biggest controversy involving mocked-up images came earlier this year when he shared a since-deleted image of himself as Jesus Christ healing a bedridden man with his bare hands.

He would later claim he thought it showed him as a "doctor" after intense backlash from religious conservatives.

News.title: Met Office names six areas facing power cuts on Tuesday and warns 'get prepared'
News.content:
Met Office names six areas facing power cuts on Tuesday and warns 'get prepared'

The forecaster has warned that major disruption could be coming to six areas covered by its latest yellow weather warning

View 2 Images Six areas of the UK have been warned of possible power cuts

The Met Office has put six areas on alert for power cuts tomorrow (Tuesday) as they brace for thunderstorms and rain.

‌



The forecaster issued a yellow warning for thunderstorms in the whole of Northern Ireland from midday tomorrow until 9pm. It warned that some short term loss of power and other services is "likely" as it urged people to take precautionary measures.

‌



It said: "People cope better with power cuts when they have prepared for them in advance. It’s easy to do; consider gathering torches and batteries, a mobile phone power pack and other essential items."

‌



The national weather agency explained that showers will develop on Tuesday morning and become heavy and "locally thundery" in the afternoon. These will be "slow-moving" and bring significant downpours, the forecaster said, with 20 to 30mm of rain predicted "in an hour or two".

The Met Office warning states: "Strong and gusty winds and hail will also be possible with the heaviest showers. Showers should slowly ease from the west into the evening."

‌



View 2 Images A map of the areas affected by the yellow weather warning (Image: Met Office)

Besides power cuts, people in the six areas targeted by the warning have also been asked to consider whether their homes and businesses are at risk of flash flooding and prepare accordingly. People should also check road conditions before making any journeys, regardless of how they plan to travel.

The Met Office said: "If you find yourself outside and hear thunder, protect yourself by finding a safe enclosed shelter (such as a car). Do not shelter under or near trees, or other structures which may be struck by lightning. If you are on an elevated area move to lower ground."

News.title: Kevin Keegan's 'overwhelmed' family issue heartfelt statement and explain funeral plans
News.content:
Kevin Keegan's 'overwhelmed' family issue heartfelt statement and explain funeral plans

Kevin Keegan died on July 20 following a battle with stomach cancer and his family have now issued a statement to thank those who paid tribute and detail plans for his funeral

View 3 Images Kevin Keegan died aged 75 from cancer (Image: (Liverpool FC via Getty Images))

Kevin Keegan's family say they have been "truly overwhelmed" by the volume of tributes following the death of the football legend. England great Keegan passed away aged 75 last month from cancer.

‌



It was announced on July 20 that the former Liverpool, Hamburg, Southampton and Newcastle striker had died following a battle with stomach cancer. The Newcastle hero left behind wife of 51 years Jean and their children Laura Jane, 47, and Sarah Marie, 43.

‌



Tributes poured in from across the heartbroken football world for the double Ballon d'Or winner, who won 63 caps for England and managed the Three Lions, Newcastle, Fulham and Manchester City.

‌



A private funeral has now been arranged by the Keegan family, who have also set up a fundraiser in King Kev's honour, which will raise money for charities close to his heart.

Gianni Infantino's opponents prepared to launch rival competition to force out FIFA boss READ MORE :

Southampton boss Tonda Eckert says he received death threats after Spygate scandal READ MORE :

A statement from the Keegan family, issued by the League Managers Association, read: “Following the devastating news of Kevin’s passing, we would like to thank the vast number of people who have expressed condolences and shared their memories of Kevin in recent days.

“As a family we have been truly overwhelmed by the volume of tributes and are grateful for them all. We will be holding a small private funeral in the coming weeks and request ongoing privacy and respect whilst we navigate this extremely difficult period as a family.

‌



“Details of a memorial service hosted by Newcastle United that will take place at a later date will be communicated in due course.”

The fundraiser states: "The Keegan family are deeply grateful for all the kind words and support received from far and wide. To honour Kevin’s memory, they feel there would be no more fitting gesture than to give.

View 3 Images Kevin Keegan touched the hearts of many

‌



"We are therefore raising money for two causes that were close to Kevin’s heart: The Christie Charity and Football Families for Justice. The Christie were an immeasurable help to Kevin and his family, as they are to many others. Football Families for Justice is a charity being set-up by John Stiles, son of the great Nobby Stiles, to support former players who are suffering from neuro degenerative diseases caused by heading the ball during their football career.

"A sporting superstar, but also a husband, father, grandfather and friend - Kevin gave so much to us all."

Keegan was most loved at Newcastle, where he enjoyed his most successful spell as a manager. "Kevin was more than a legendary footballer and manager. He was the beating heart of Newcastle United for generations of supporters," the club said in a statement.

‌



View 3 Images Kevin Keegan was a legend at Newcastle United (Image: PA)

"As a player, he brought world-class talent, ambition and belief to St. James’ Park, helping to transform perceptions of what Newcastle United could be. As a manager, he ignited our city. Kevin gave supporters hope and pride, and led a team whose style, spirit and passion captured the imagination of football fans around the world. He was so much more than an Entertainer.

"Kevin forged an extraordinary bond with Newcastle, built on the roots of his father, Joe. He understood our people. He embraced the North East with a passion that was genuine and unwavering, and in return, he earned his rightful place in the hearts of millions."

News.title: UK wildfires live: Flames rage near Shrewsbury as major incident also declared in Wales
News.content:
Firefighters are battling wildfires in Shropshire and South Wales, with crews declaring a major incident as they tackle the blaze in the Rhondda Valley

Firefighters in Shropshire are tackling a large blaze near a historic site, while crews in South Wales have declared a major incident as they battle a wildfire close to homes.

The blaze at Battlefield Heritage Park, a country park north of Shrewsbury, broke out this afternoon. It is understood to be just a few fields away from the site associated with the 1403 Battle of Shrewsbury, fought between King Henry IV and a rebel army led by Henry "Harry Hotspur" Percy.

Meanwhile, crews from South Wales Fire and Rescue Service are battling a wildfire in the Llanwonno area of Rhondda Cynon Taf. The blaze, which began on Saturday afternoon, has already spread across around 150 hectares - roughly the size of 210 football pitches.

No homes have been evacuated, but Rhondda Cynon Taf Council said a rest centre has been set up at a local sports centre for residents affected by smoke and poor air quality from the fire.

News.title: Nigel Farage – recap: Reform UK leader's horrific new 'breaking point' poster is branded 'nonsense'
News.content:
Nigel Farage's Reform UK has proposed using the Royal Navy to transport migrants on the English Channel to France or Belgium under a plan called "operation fortress"

Nigel Farage was today blasted for posting online a new version of his controversial "breaking point" poster.

The Reform UK's latest edit, posted on his X account, depicts migrants at Ceuta rather than Syrian refugees, invoking the 2016 poster denounced by then-Chancellor George Osbourne, who compared it to Nazi propaganda.

Reacting online, other X users voiced their anger today. One said: "Talking nonsense again." Another posted: "Desperate deflection and piffle." A third wrote: "Reform is at a laughing point."

Mr Farage, whose MP seat in Clacton-on-Sea, Essex, is up for contest next week, debuted the "breaking point" poster on the last week of the 2016 Brexit referendum while serving as UKIP leader.

The new version was posted after Mr Farage, 62, broke his cover at a press conference today to unveil visions to use the Royal Navy to transport migrants on the English Channel to France or Belgium under a plan called "operation fortress". This too has been slammed today.

And, while Mr Farage continues to face mounting pressure over his finances, it has now emerged his deputy, Richard Tice, is under investigation by the standards commissioner over an alleged failure to declare an interest.

News.title: Nigel Farage's small boats plan savaged as France hits back over 'violation'
News.content:
Nigel Farage's small boats plan savaged as France hits back over 'violation'

France's interior ministry has blasted Nigel Farage's plan to use the Royal Navy to stop small boats, while the Reform chief was warned his idea will "inevitably" lead to more deaths on the Channel

View 5 Images Nigel Farage is looking to turn around plummeting poll ratings (Image: Getty Images)

Nigel Farage's desperate small boats plan has been dismissed as impractical and illegal as he attempts to divert attention from sleaze allegations.

‌



The Reform UK leader published a thin plan to use the Royal Navy to stop Channel crossings. But France shot back, claiming the move would be a "violation of French sovereignty" and saying it breaks maritime law.

‌



Downing Street also dismissed the 25-page proposal, saying a similar measure under the Tories had not lowered the number of crossings. And charities warned it would inevitably lead to more deaths.

‌



Mr Farage staged a rare Westminster press conference today to launch the plan as he battles to stop plummeting poll ratings. He was accused of trying to create a diversion by saying navy vessels should intercept small boats crossing the Channel and return those on board to France and Belgium.

Reform council leader vows to report café owner who fed kids for free to police READ MORE :

View 5 Images Mr Farage's plan has been dismissed as impractical (Image: Gareth Fuller/PA Wire)

France brands Farage's plans 'a violation'

Reform claimed it anticipated French authorities would support agreed returns. But in a statement the nation's interior ministry said: "This would be a violation of French sovereignty as well as a violation of maritime law and international law."

‌



At the same press conference Mr Farage confirmed reports he had held secret talks about returning as party leader months before the 2024 general election. But he insisted these took place after he accepted a £5million 'gift' from Thailand-based crypto tycoon Christopher Harborne.

This money, which was not declared, was being investigated by Parliament's standards commissioner when Mr Farage stepped down and triggered a by-election in Clacton, Essex. He is battling parody candidate Count Binface after all other major parties refused to engage, branding the contest a circus.

He unveiled Operation Fortress, which Reform says would see 10 navy vessels deployed to stop Channel crossings. But Andy Burnham's official spokesman said getting the Royal Navy involved was tried under the Tories as crossings rose - and made no difference.

‌



The number of people reaching the UK this year is at its lowest since 2021, but the government is under pressure to tackle the number of crossings. The Downing Street spokesman said: "The Royal Navy had primacy for small boat crossings under the previous government in 2022. I'd remind you there was no reduction in small boat crossings in that period.

"The Royal Navy is already tackling many threats, including monitoring any Russian warships operating near our shores, protecting our waters and our critical national infrastructure. Border patrol officers have significant capabilities and skills that make them the best-suited candidate to lead small boats operations in the Channel.

"That's why we're driving down the number of crossings. It's why they're down almost 50% compared to last year and why almost 60% of attempted crossings have been stopped since this Government came to power."

‌



View 5 Images Mr Farage with 'Shadow Home Secretary' Zia Yusuf (Image: Getty Images)

Refugee Council says more lives would be at risk

Under Reform's plan, bay class landing ships, rigid-hulled inflatable boats and Border Force cutters would be used to intercept dangerous boats. People would be removed, treated, and returned to France or Belgium.

A document outlining the policy described it as a humanitarian response, but last night the Refugee Council warned it would inevitably put people in more danger.

‌



Jon Featonby, chief policy analyst at the charity, said: “The deaths of four people trying to cross the channel last week were a tragic reminder of how dangerous this route is. The last thing anyone should be proposing is anything that would risk more loss of life, as this plan inevitably would."

Reform's proposals would create a major flashpoint between Britain, France and Belgium - but it claimed it would not lead to violence in the sea. The Reform document states: "We do not believe for one moment that the French nation or gendarmerie would open fire on Royal Marines conducting a humanitarian mission and transporting civilians."

It went on to say the chances of a tactical confrontation with France is "incredibly low". Mr Farage said:"If the Royal Navy is not there to protect this country from invasion, then, frankly, I can't see what its purpose is."

‌



Following the press conference he unveiled a van with the words 'Europe is at breaking point' on the side. It is a reference to a heavily-criticised poster he posed with during the Brexit campaign.

Reform's home affairs spokesman, Zia Yusuf - who attended the press conference with Mr Farage - said it would be the largest military operation in the English Channel since World War Two.

Farage's popularity plunge

View 5 Images Mr Farage is locked in a by-election showdown with Count Binface (Image: Aaron Chown/PA Wire)

‌



The headline-grabbing policy came after he was dealt a hammer blow last week when two major polls suggested Labour had overtaken Reform after trailing for more than a year. And according to More in Common his personal approval ratings have plummeted, falling by 10 points in just a fortnight to minus 34%.

This makes him the most unpopular leader of any of the five main parties, a long way behind Andy Burnham's +19%. An investigation into the £5million gift is expected to resume if Mr Farage is successfully returned as an MP next week.

If Mr Farage is found to have broken strict rules on declaring gifts in the year before becoming an MP, he could face a suspension and a possible second by-election.

‌



He denies wrongdoing and insisted that when he accepted the money he had no intention of standing for Parliament. But he admitted he had discussed a return as party leader in spring 2024 with Richard Tice.

Mr Farage did not announce his candidacy until June after Rishi Sunak called a snap general election, which Labour won in a landslide. Asked about the discussions, Mr Farage said it "wasn't a deal, it wasn't an agreement, it was subject to if I came back".

View 5 Images Mr Farage poses with a digital poster van claiming Europe is full (Image: TOLGA AKMEN/EPA/Shutterstock)

‌



He said he had been discussing financial liabilities. The Sunday Times reported he negotiated a deal with Mr Tice, who was then party chief.

Under that deal, once Mr Farage became leader Reform would repay or write off more than £1 million in outstanding loans it had received from Mr Tice's company. He said: "Overall questions about money could go on for years.

"I had no intention of returning to politics or as leader of Reform, but in the spring of that year I did talk to Richard Tice about what the liabilities would be if I was to come back to that position. And you'd be a bit of a mug, wouldn't you, to walk into a job and not find our what the potential liabilities were, and they were substantial."

Article continues below

This chat came quite some time after the gift, he said. On top of questions about the donation, it has emerged that the Met Police is investigating donations to Reform by Fiona Cottrell, mum of convicted fraudster George Cottrell, a close ally of Mr Farage.

Officers are working to determine the original source of the funds. Labour Party chairwoman Bridget Phillipson said: “Farage has desperately tried to distract from his catalogue of scandals. But the embattled Reform leader has run out of road and must come clean with the public. If he had done nothing wrong, he surely would have explained himself by now.

“With grubby pacts, police probes, and support from a convicted fraudster – Reform are up to their neck in sleaze and they clearly think the rules don’t apply to them.”

News.title: 'Farage's latest small boats circus is choreographed nonsense designed to divert attention from his crypto scandal'
News.content:
Parliament’s standards watchdog had scarcely opened another investigation into Reform before Nigel Farage began hammering the distraction button.

Within hours of deputy leader Richard Tice becoming the second senior party figure in weeks to face scrutiny over alleged undeclared interests, Farage announced Operation Fortress - a plan to send the Royal Navy into the Channel to forcibly return small boat migrants to France.

The headlines changed. The cameras followed. Reform escaped the questions it did not want to answer.

That is the purpose of this naval pageant. It is an old stunt dressed up as emergency action. Reform proposed the same idea in January 2025, when it collapsed under the weight of its own emptiness. There were no workable details then, and there are none now.

‌



Former Royal Navy commander Tom Sharpe has torn it apart. The Navy lacks the right vessels, while warships costing billions and built to defend Britain from threats such as Putin’s Russia should not be diverted into an expensive Channel pick-up service.

Yet the ugliest deception is Farage pretending to rescue Britain from a disaster bearing his fingerprints.

He was Brexit’s chief salesman. He promised control of the borders. Britain instead lost the Dublin Convention protections, which had offered a route to return asylum seekers to European countries they had already entered.

‌



In 2018, 299 people crossed the Channel in small boats. By 2022, the total had exploded beyond 45,000.

Farage helped tear up the system, then made a career blaming others for the wreckage. Now he expects taxpayers to fund the theatre, concealing his failure.

Reform’s working-class supporters deserve better. Such hard workers are the people this newspaper stands beside, and they should not be patronised or treated as electoral puppets as they are now by Reform in Clacton.

They are being asked to trust a party whose deputy leader is under investigation over an allegedly undeclared financial relationship with a convicted fraudster, whose leader faces an unresolved standards referral and whose response to scrutiny is to wheel out the Navy. There are also serious questions over the millions of pounds accepted from donors living outside Britain.

‌



Voters deserve the unvarnished record. Farage sold them control and delivered chaos. Reform now wants their votes, their trust and their taxes to pay for the damage.

News.title: Seven killed as drone hits packed Russian beach and tourists run for their lives
News.content:
Seven killed as drone hits packed Russian beach and tourists run for their lives

Seven people, including three children and four adults, were killed, while 40 others, including 21 were taken to hospital

Drone dive-bombs beach in southern Russia killing tourists

At least seven people have been killed, including three children, AS a "downed" Ukrainian drone crashed and exploded onto sunbathers on a packed Russian beach.

‌



Forty people were also injured, with 21 of them taken to hospital, as the unmanned device exploded in Arkhipo-Osipovka. The drone was seen dive-bombing onto tourists at the popular beach as temperatures reached 29C.

‌



Beachgoers have claimed no warning sirens were heard before the incident as some sheltered under sun loungers. A video from the beach on the eastern Black Sea coast shows terrified tourists watching as the light aircraft falls on the beach before exploding.

‌



People can then be seen fleeing from the sea in panic. "We were on the beach at the time. I'm in complete shock," said one.

"We were on the beach, didn't have time to leave, hid behind a ledge, covered ourselves with sun loungers, and didn't see where it exploded." Air defence machine gunners were heard seeking to defend the resort from drones as the crippled UAV fell on the tourists.

Moscow explosion: Three dead and 21 injured after bomb detonates at busy restaurant READ MORE :

Its real target was not clear but Vladimir Putin’s high-security £1billion Gelenzhik palace is just 17 miles along the coastline. The building boasts a wooden throne and reportedly used to have a striptease stage and pole dancing boudoir. It includes a 16-storey underground complex and bunker, built inside the cliff to withstand nuclear attack. Another witness said: "While we were parking, we saw crowds of people leaving the beach, cars driving away.

‌



"A friend called me and said we had to turn around and leave because a drone had crashed. We saw a man with a bloody shoulder."

A shocked tourist added: "This all happened in front of the children, and the child is having a nervous breakdown." Another said: "We were already home when we heard a barrage of gunfire, like a machine gun, and an explosion. Everything shook."

"A tragedy has occurred in Gelenzhik," said Krasnodar regional governor, Veniamin Kondratyev, who suggested that it was drone debris that crashed, indicating the kamikaze plane had been downed. He said: "In the village of Arkhipo-Osipovka, three people were killed, according to preliminary information, due to the crash of drone debris.

Article continues below

"I extend my sincere condolences to their families and loved ones." A Ukrainian source suggested the hit may have been on a "private resort" for the Russian engineers from rocket-making Mashinostroenie Research and Production Association. There was no immediate official comment.

Russian tourists have flocked to the Black Sea coastline of Krasnodar, believing it safer than occupied Crimea, which is now a virtual no-go zone due to a Ukrainian blockade of the peninsula. But the area around Gelendzhik has also been reportedly targeted by drones.

Russian tourists have claimed no alarms were sounded before the incident, with one saying: "No sirens. Nothing happened." Mayor Alexey Bogodistov had announced a drone threat at 8.34am but then cancelled it 10 minutes later.

News.title: English FA set to withdraw support for Fifa president Infantino
News.content:
The English Football Association is set to write to Fifa president Gianni Infantino withdrawing its support for him amid the fallout from his scrapped plans to sell off stakes in Fifa competitions to private investors.

It comes as Uefa threatens legal action over the proposals and Wales publicly withdraw backing for Infantino's bid to continue as Fifa president.

Next March, Infantino is set to stand for re-election for a fourth and final term as president and would need 106 votes from Fifa's 211 members to win.

Sources have told BBC Sport the Scottish FA's position on the future of Infantino remains aligned with Uefa's lack of confidence in the 56-year-old.

Infantino's leadership had already been publicly questioned by football's governing bodies in Europe, North and Central America and the Caribbean, with Uefa and Concacaf releasing statements criticising the plans.

Fifa and Infantino wanted to create a commercial subsidiary to run its main events, including its World Cups, and external investors would have been able to buy stakes in it.

World football's governing body said it would "invite third parties to make minority, non-controlling investments" in a new subsidiary called Fifa Forward Enterprise (FFE).

As first reported by The Telegraph, Uefa said in a letter to Infantino "it is actively considering legal action, arbitration, and/or regulatory complaints (together, the 'proceedings') arising out of and in connection with the FFE plan proposed by Fifa".

Uefa added it wants "immediate steps" to "preserve all documents and electronically stored information" in Fifa's possession "independent" of their internal policies that may result in "routine document destruction or deletion".

BBC Sport has approached Fifa for comment.

News.title: France hits out at Reform UK plan to return migrants using Navy
News.content:
France has hit out at a Reform UK plan to return migrant boats using the Navy, saying the proposals would violate its sovereignty and breach international law.

Nigel Farage's party announced that if it was in power it would intercept boats crossing the English Channel and return migrants to French ports, even if France disagreed.

Opposition parties branded the plan unworkable, while a Labour minister said it would lead to "a lot of time arguing with France" instead of "actually getting to grips with the problem".

Responding to the French government, a Reform spokesperson said: "We will always stand up for British interests and protect our people, whether Emmanuel Macron likes it or not."

The spokesperson added: "Humanitarian missions do not violate maritime or international law."

Under the plans, which Reform said it would bring in if it entered government after the next election, military-crewed inflatable boats deployed from 10 Navy patrol vessels would be used to "come alongside" migrant boats crossing the English Channel.

Border Force officers and police stationed onboard would be tasked with arresting people in the boats, and they would then be returned to France or Belgium by Navy personnel or Marines.

The party said returns operations would be conducted by military personnel with Border Force officers on hand in case of "non-compliance", with a Bay Class landing ship providing "detention capacity at sea" for up to 700 people.

Speaking at a news conference on Monday, Reform's home affairs spokesman Zia Yusuf said the party would aim to get agreement to disembark arrested migrants at French ports.

He added: "If the Elysee Palace refuses, make no mistake - His Majesty's Royal Marines will disembark them safely on the very shore they left that morning".

Speaking alongside him, Farage played down the prospect of a diplomatic confrontation with the French, claiming that attitudes in France towards the idea were "softening".

But in a statement issued later on Monday, the French interior ministry said: "This would constitute a violation of French sovereignty, as well as a violation of the law of the sea and international law."

A spokesperson for the department added that measures agreed with the UK, as well as "operations deployed at the local level", had already led to a reduction in crossings so far this year compared to the same period in 2025.

News.title: Inside city gripped by deadly protests in Pakistan-administered Kashmir
News.content:
Dozens of people have been killed in clashes between security officials and protesters across Pakistan-administered Kashmir over the last two months, following a crackdown that left the city of Rawalakot mostly sealed off from the world.

Leading the demonstrations is the Joint Awami Action Committee (JAAC), which says it is protesting for rights including healthcare and electricity.

Authorities say the JAAC is trying to disrupt the current regional elections, that the group is armed, and will not be allowed to leave Rawalakot.

The JAAC was banned in June; they have been labelled foreign-funded terrorists by the government. They reject this characterisation, saying they are peaceful and - though funded from the Pakistan-administered Kashmir community abroad - not sponsored by India.

The BBC is the first media to gain access to the city and speak to people on the ground about what is going on at the heart of the protests. Pakistan correspondent Caroline Davies reports from Islamabad.

News.title: Son who kept mum's body in freezer for years collected £78k of her benefits
News.content:
The court heard Phillips moved downstairs to sleep next to his mother's body. At times he would open the freezer and hold her hand.

Sylvia Phillips had 26 appointments with her local GP practice in 2021, and six in 2022, after which there was no further contact.

The court heard she was last seen in A&E on 24 September 2022 and her local GP made a house call on 26 September but her son continued to pick up her prescriptions.

Sylvia Phillips was invited to a review by the practice, but her son said she would not come to the surgery and she did not need the blood tests.

Christopher Phillips received a total of Â£78,190.92 in state pension, pensions credit, attendance allowance, winter fuel payments, cost-of-living payments and housing benefit payments, which would have ceased had the death been reported.

He had been her primary carer since 2008, and the court heard he had resigned from his job in late 2022 when her health declined further. The pair were described as "somewhat isolated".

Ruth Smith, defending, said Phillips had told police: "I basically didn't want to let her go."

She added: "He described talking to her as if she was still aliveâ¦ Sitting next to her, talking to her about television programmes, Coronation Street, the horse racing, just as they always did," she said, adding that he was a "vulnerable individual".

Phillips sobbed in the dock as Smith said her client was "extremely close to his mother" and was in "extreme grief" following her death.

She said he showed a "lack of acceptance" about her passing and "had almost created a false narrative that she was still alive".

Sentencing Phillips, Judge Lloyd-Clarke said he had "deliberately concealed" his mother's death and "took steps to give the impression that she was still alive".

"You continued to collect her prescription and lied to medical professionals and eventually the police," Lloyd-Clarke added.

"Rather than notify the authorities and make arrangements for her lawful burial, you purchased a chest freezer on March 10th and concealed her body within it," she said.

Lloyd-Clarke added that a timescale for confiscation proceedings would follow.

News.title: Newspaper columnist and broadcaster Rod Liddle dies aged 66
News.content:
Newspaper columnist and broadcaster Rod Liddle has died aged 66 after a short illness.

Liddle's children paid tribute to their father, who they described as their guide "on how to live an extraordinary life", while CEO of News UK, Rebekah Brooks, called him "an inimitable journalistic force."

Brooks added that "he challenged conventional thinking and left an indelible mark on British journalism."

Liddle, a columnist for the Sun and the Sunday Times, died at The James Cook University Hospital in Middlesbrough on Sunday evening.

A former editor of BBC Radio 4's flagship Today programme, he also had a weekly column in the Spectator, as well as a show on Times Radio.

His children, Wilder, Tyler and Emmy, said: "We're all very saddened and shocked at the sudden passing of our wonderful father.

"He raised us much as you might imagine, to be inquisitive, brave and always humorous.

"Even in hospital in the last few weeks, he consistently held the room and never let the awful situation show.

"He has left a legacy that we are all incredibly proud of, he will always be our guide on how to live an extraordinary life."

News.title: X Factor finalist denies murdering influencer by running her over with car
News.content:
A former X Factor finalist has denied murdering a social media influencer by running her over with a car in central London.

Gabrielle Carrington of Manchester, allegedly struck Klaudia Zakrzewska outside Inca nightclub in Argyll Street, Soho, at 04:30 BST on 19 April.

The 29-year-old appeared at the Old Bailey by video link from Bronzefield prison to deny the charge. She had been initially charged with attempted murder but that was changed to murder after Zakrzewska died from her injuries six days later.

Carrington, who was not represented in court by a barrister, also denied a second charge of causing grievous bodily harm with intent to security guard Anoush Chyche.

The defendant was not asked to enter a plea to a third charge of driving with excess alcohol.

Family members of the victims shook their heads as the accused read out her pleas.

Judge Sarah Whitehouse KC confirmed the trial would be held at the same court from 5 January.

Carrington appeared emotional on the video link, wiping tears from her face throughout the hearing and was placed into custody afterwards.

News.title: Farage says he discussed return to politics months before general election
News.content:
Nigel Farage has told the BBC he discussed the "potential liabilities" of returning to politics before the 2024 general election.

It comes after The Sunday Times, external reported Farage had negotiated a deal in March and April 2024 with then-Reform leader Richard Tice to return to lead the party.

Farage confirmed he spoke with Tice in spring 2024 to scope out what would happen to Reform's finances if he returned but said it "wasn't a deal, it wasn't an agreement", adding that talks came "quite some time after" he received a Â£5m gift from a billionaire donor.

Labour said Farage's remarks had "blown a gaping hole" in his argument for not declaring the gift after becoming an MP in July 2024.

Farage has repeatedly argued the Â£5m from British cryptocurrency investor Christopher Harborne was an "unconditional gift", was intended for his personal security, "wasn't political in any sense at all" and he was not an MP when he received it.

Reform's opponents have said he should have declared it in the MPs' register of interests when he was elected to Parliament.

The Parliamentary Standards Commissioner was investigating whether Farage broke the rules, but the process was suspended when he stood down as Clacton MP last month to force a by-election.

Farage said he took this decision as the "people of Clacton should be the judges of my actions". The investigation will be resumed if Farage wins the by-election, which is taking place on 13 August.

Farage left frontline politics in 2021 and embarked on a broadcasting career.

In May 2024, Farage was serving as Reform's honorary president but announced he would not be standing as a candidate in the general election in July of that year.

He reversed this position at the beginning of June and took over the leadership of the party.

Appearing at a press conference on Monday, Farage was asked if he had negotiated a deal on what would happen to Reform's finances if he came back as leader - in light of the report in The Sunday Times.

He replied: "I had no intention of returning to politics or as leader of Reform, but in the spring of that year I did talk to Richard Tice about what the liabilities would be if I was to come back to that position.

"And you'd be a bit of a mug, wouldn't you, to walk into a job and not find out what the potential liabilities were, and they were substantial.

"But without Richard, the party wouldn't have even survived, so that was useful for me to know. But it wasn't a deal, it wasn't an agreement, it was subject to if I came back."

He added: "If you want clarification on this, that came quite some time after the gift, which is perhaps the important point."

Bridget Phillipson, chair of the Labour Party, said: "Nigel Farage has blown a gaping hole in his excuse for why his secret Â£5m 'gift' from a crypto billionaire did not need to be declared."

The Commons code of conduct states that new MPs "must register all their current financial interests, and any registrable benefits (other than earnings) received in the 12 months before their election within one month of their election".

The rules say "purely personal gifts or benefits" from family or commercial loans would not normally have to be registered.

The rules also say "both the possible motive of the giver and the use to which the gift is to be put should be considered", adding "if there is any doubt, the benefit should be registered".
