News.title: Ariana Grande to take a break from public life citing 'endless, ongoing scrutiny'
News.content:
Ariana Grande is to take a "much-deserved break" from public appearances and will no longer star in an upcoming musical production in London when she ends her Eternal Sunshine tour next month.

A representative for the US singer, 33, told People magazine that she "will be taking a step back from visibility" when the tour ends, after her appearances led to "endless, ongoing public scrutiny".

The company behind a revival of Stephen Sondheim's Sunday in the Park with George, due to play at the Barbican in 2027, confirmed that she would no longer be part of the production and had its "complete understanding and support".

Grande's physical appearance and health have been a topic of speculation in recent years.

News.title: Woman has pioneering womb surgery to fix 'miracle' baby with intestines outside its body
News.content:
Doctors have used ground-breaking surgery on an unborn baby to successfully correct a birth defect while he was still inside the womb.

His mother, Maisie Savage, from London, was operated on by doctors in the US while she was 26 weeks pregnant.

Baby Theo, who is now five months old and thriving, had gastroschisis, where the belly button does not develop properly, causing the intestines to grow externally.

Doctors partially exposed his mother's womb and then gently pushed his organs back inside his abdomen using keyhole surgery.

He was the third baby in the world to benefit from the first-of-its-kind clinical trial.

Maisie, 29, and Theo's father, Josh French, 36, both teachers, say they are incredibly relieved by the success of the pioneering surgery.

"He's a little miracle, isn't he?" Maisie told BBC News.

But they both know things could have been very different.

The serious birth defect affects one in 3,000 UK babies each year. In the best-case scenarios, babies can require weeks in intensive care and nutritional feeding through a tube or IV and corrective surgery.

For the most complex cases, like Theo's, outcomes are far more serious with up to six months in neonatal intensive care, multiple surgeries, IV nutritional feeding for up to two years, and a possible intestinal transplant.

Even with the highest level of medical care, one in 10 babies will die.

News.title: Author La Plante banned from driving for six months
News.content:
The court heard she already had nine points on her licence, from three speeding offences in June 2023 and then June and July 2025.

She told the court she believed she would have to have the dog rehomed if she was unable to drive him to his daily walks, saying: "I think the emotional turmoil of that would truly damn my career as a writer.

"It's very, very solitary and I work exceptionally hard and I would just stop."

La Plante, who is best known for creating Prime Suspect's no-nonsense Det Ch Insp Jane Tennison, admitted driving at 24mph twice, 25mph, 26mph and 27mph in the latest offences, which all happened as she was on her way to take her dog for his daily walk.

Giving evidence, La Plante said she got her dog Theo after suffering the devastation of the untimely death of another dog, Hugo.

Fighting back tears, she said she "lost it" when Hugo died and she "didn't know what to do with [her] life".

She added her new dog had helped her through the grieving process.

News.title: Grooming gang found guilty of exploiting teenage girls for sex
News.content:
Four men and a woman have been found guilty of being part of a grooming gang that exploited teenage girls for sex.

Mustafa Iqbal, Mohamed Arshad, Ziaullah Badshah, Jaswinder Singh were convicted of conspiracy to traffic their victims, who were aged 14,15 and 16.

At Caernarfon Crown Court on Monday, Iqbal, Arshad and Badshah were also found guilty of rape while another member of the gang, Sarah Gray, was found guilty of perverting the course of justice and assisting an offender.

The men were remanded in custody ahead of sentencing on 25 September, while Gray was released on bail.

Prosecutor Owen Edwards KC said the men had used the three girls - named only as Child A, B and C - like "sexual commodities".

"They took full sexual advantage of Girl B in particular," he said.

The jury was told Child A had been treated as a "sexual plaything", who finally had gone to the police after having been handcuffed by Iqbal and had been raped.

The court heard the teenagers were given drugs and sexually abused in cars, homes and businesses in Rhyl, Denbighshire and the surrounding area between April 2022 and March 2024.

The first two victims, Child B who was 15 and Child C who was 14, were approached by Iqbal, 43, near a petrol station in the town, and he persuaded them to come back to his home.

They were later joined by local coffee shop owner Arshad, 36, and his friend Badshah, 25.

During the trial the jury had been told how the two girls stated they were 17, had smoked cannabis with the men and had played a game of spin the bottle.

Badshah, who came to Rhyl as a refugee from Pakistan when he was 15, admitted kissing Child B and Child C, and on later occasions having sex with Child B at his home.

Badshah, of Brighton Road, Rhyl, was found guilty of two counts of rape, two counts of conspiracy to traffic, two counts of conspiracy to require a person to perform compulsory labour, supplying cannabis to another.

Arshad, 36, of Clifton Grove, Rhyl, was found guilty of three counts of rape, two counts of conspiracy to traffic, two counts of conspiracy to require a person to perform compulsory labour, and supplying cannabis to another.

The court heard one of the counts of rape happened in an alleyway outside his former business, Zayn's Coffee House.

Iqbal, of Trellewelyn Road, Rhyl, was found guilty of raping Child B and also sexually assaulting Child C. He was also found guilty of raping another teenager, Child A, who was 16 and lived in a care home.

Described as a drug dealer during the trial, he supplied Child A with crack cocaine and cannabis in return for sex.

Iqbal was convicted of 21 offences, including four of rape and three of sexual assault. He was also found guilty of conspiracy to traffic and conspiracy to supply cannabis and cocaine, breaching a trafficking risk order, and he pleaded guilty to possessing a prohibited weapon.

The gang was unmasked after another friend of the men took Child B to London.

Former builder Singh, 61, claimed the girl was looking after his dog and there was no sexual motive in taking her on the trip to see his family in the capital, but a concerned adult was alarmed by Singh's intentions and reported him to the police.

Singh, of River Street, Rhyl, was found guilty of two counts of conspiracy to traffic and one count of supplying cannabis to another.

Gray, 53, of Llanasa Road, Gronant, was also found guilty of conspiracy to supply cocaine to another and conspiracy to supply cannabis to another.

After the guilty verdicts Det Ch Insp Richard Sidney said his thoughts were the three young victims.

"They were children, aged just 14 to 16, when they were subjected to exploitation and abuse by adults who took advantage of their vulnerabilities and sought to manipulate and control them for their own gain," he said.

"No child should have to experience what these young women endured."

He said that the five defendants had denied almost every allegation against them from the outset.

"I hope today's outcome sends a clear message that those who seek to groom and exploit vulnerable children will be relentlessly pursued," he said.

A spokesperson for Denbighshire council said its thoughts were with the young women at the centre of the case, adding that it wanted to "recognise the courage and bravery they have shown".

The spokesperson said the council would work with the North Wales Safeguarding Board on a review, separate to the criminal process, that would "examine agencies' involvement with the young people and to identify what lessons can be learnt for the future".

"We understand that this case has been challenging and has brought up strong feelings. We ask that everyone respects the legal process and each other as we process this outcome," they added.

If you have been affected by any of the issues raised in this story, information and support can be found at the BBC's Action Line

News.title: Driest July on record for England and Wales
News.content:
July 2026 was the driest for England and Wales since records began 190 years ago, according to the Met Office, external.

England recorded just 6.5mm of rainfall and Wales had 9.3mm, both less than half of the previous records for the nations.

The dry conditions have been accompanied by exceptional warmth across much of the UK. It was the second warmest July for the UK as a whole and Wales' warmest ever.

The month was also the UK's sunniest July on record. For England and Wales, it was the sunniest calendar month ever observed.

So far this year, six months of 2026 have seen above average sunshine hours for the UK, with just February seeing below the monthly average.

News.title: Presenter Tony Livesey leaves BBC Radio 5 Live after 16 years
News.content:
Presenter Tony Livesey has left BBC Radio 5 Live after 16 years at the station, the corporation has announced.

Livesey stepped back from his weekday late night talk show in June, following allegations made against his former newspaper boss David Sullivan.

He had previously worked as editor-in-chief of Sullivan's Daily and Sunday Sport publications.

Several women have accused Sullivan, a billionaire businessman and West Ham co-owner, of abusing his power and preying on them for sex, in some cases when they were teenagers. Sullivan has strongly denied the allegations.

The claims against Sullivan were made in a joint investigation by the Times and BBC Panorama.

The BBC previously said Livesey had asked to take a break from presenting his programme while the issues raised by the investigation were being examined.

One alleged victim said that Livesey had arranged a meeting between her and Sullivan in 1999.

Livesey said he had "no recollection" of introducing the young woman to Sullivan and that it was "not part" of his job to do so.

He added that he had "great sympathy for a woman who may have become a victim", but rejected any suggestion that he had played "any role whatsoever in that scenario" and said he found the allegation "abhorrent".

In an email sent to 5 Live staff on Monday morning, the station's controller Heidi Dawson said he had now decided to leave.

"Tony has asked me to pass on his heartfelt thanks to the brilliant colleagues at 5 Live who he has had the pleasure of working with over the years," she wrote.

"I know many of you have also really enjoyed working with Tony, and we wish him well for all his future endeavours."

The award-winning presenter worked for the BBC from 2006 - the same year he left the newspapers - appearing on 5 Live from 2010 onwards, including a successful stint hosting its drivetime show.

He won radio awards - ARIA and APAs - for his reporting on how it feels to lose your mother as a child, and an ARIAS gold award after he was asked by the late Dame Deborah James to conduct her final interview.

His topical three-hour programme was broadcast on 5 Live from Monday to Thursday, featuring interviews and phone calls from listeners.

News.title: Comedian Jimmy Cricket dies aged 80
News.content:
Comedian Jimmy Cricket has died aged 80 after a short illness, his family said.

In a statement posted to social media they said Cricket spent his last few days surrounded by his family, love, laughter and songs.

"Forever our clown, he was cracking jokes to the wonderful NHS staff and to us all, right until the end. His courage, dignity and positivity through all he endured was inspirational," they added.

The comedian, from Northern Ireland, became a household name in the 1970s.

James Joseph Mulgrew was born in Cookstown, County Tyrone in 1945, Cricket left school at 16 and started the summer season of 1966 as a Redcoat for Butlins.

He worked the comedy club scene in the 1970s and 1980s, going on to win LWT's Search for a Star talent contest and eventually getting his own TV show on ITV and a radio series on BBC Radio 2.

Cricket's family said he had been a "force for joy" and the world was a "far less sillier place today".

"We were going to end by using his famous catchphrase and say: 'There's no More'.

"But Jimmy was a man of great faith and a Papal Knight of the Catholic Church.

"He believed that death is not the end and was looking forward to eternity, so reallyâ¦ And there's more."

News.title: I didn't know I'd been hosting a parasite for years - until the most intense pain of my life
News.content:
Jones remembers the May 2016 night when he went into hospital â he was supposed to go out to a dinner with his wife Eileen, but he stayed at home as he felt unwell.

"I hadn't been able to control the pain, and it was more intense than anything I had before.

"Then about midnight, we had to call the ambulance, and they took me to Nevill Hall. Whatever they gave me there cured the pain. I haven't experienced pain like that before."

Jones was in hospital for 10 days, and says the doctors there suspected he had hydatid cysts immediately.

He said: "There was a lot of it around this area at the time, and I remember the Ministry of Agriculture giving worming treatment to the dogs on the local farms.

"Whether they could see that I was an old sheep farmer or not, that might have had a bearing on it. We had plenty of experience in this area â Breconshire as a whole â of hydatid cysts, people that have suffered through it, numerous examples."

Jones was then referred to "the main expert on hydatid cysts" in London where he had two operations in 2018 and 2019 to remove them, one from each lung.

"I swapped two cysts for two scars on the ribs," he said, adding that he still has a cyst on his liver, which surgeons decided not to remove.

News.title: Scottish islanders refused permission to stage annual seabird chicks hunt
News.content:
Agnes Rennie, is chair of Urras Oighreachd Ghabhsainn, the local community land group for the north of Lewis. She said: "The guga hunt is a centuries-old tradition which reinforces our unique communal identity and helps families keep ancient Gaelic customs alive and relevant in the modern world."

Historian Donald S Murray said food security was not guaranteed, and argued that the hunt was not unique.

He said that in New Zealand sooty shearwater, also known as muttonbirds, were traditionally hunted on Rakiura, which is also known as Stewart Island.

Murray described the campaign against the guga hunt as "monstrous".

Anti-guga hunt graffiti was sprayed on walls at NatureScot's headquarters in Inverness in February, and was followed by a rooftop protest in March.

Murdo MacRitchie, of the Save Our Guga Harvest group, said there was "deep disappointment" in Ness following the decision.

He added: "However, that decision has to be respected and we will continue to work with NatureScot to help us fully understand the scientific grounds on which it was based.

"It should be noted that NatureScot addressed the issue of welfare and, having taken advice from Scotland's chief veterinary officer, again confirmed the method of dispatch is humane."

Torcuil Crichton, Labour MP for Na h-Eileanan an Iar, has submitted a Freedom of Information (FOI) request to find out how NatureScot came to its conclusion.

"Last year, when the Men of Ness took 500 guga from Sula Sgeir the science backed them up and the recommendation was for the hunt to go ahead," he said.

"The numbers haven't changed, the situation hasn't changed but the way of measuring the numbers has changed."

He said objectors had won a "hollow victory" stopping this year's hunt.

Michigan health officials just reported the first two deaths from the state’s ongoing outbreak of the explosive diarrhea-causing foodborne illness cyclosporiasis, marking the first fatalities reported in the U.S. since the surge of cases began earlier this year.

The deceased patients had “significant underlying health conditions that may have been impacted by cyclosporiasis and dehydration,” according to the state’s Department of Health and Human Services. Their names or ages were not released.

“No additional information will be provided on these two cases,” it said Monday.

Michigan is the state with the largest number of cases nationwide, and officials reported there were 11,234 sickened and nearly 200 people hospitalized so far. More than 17,000 cases are being investigated in the U.S.

Cases in the Great Lakes state and eight others - including West Virginia, Oklahoma, Pennsylvania, Ohio, Kentucky, Kansas, Indiana and Illinois - have been tied to contaminated lettuce.

open image in gallery The first deaths related to the nation’s ongoing outbreak of cyclosporiasis were just reported in Michigan. The unidentified patients both had underlying health conditions ( AFP/Getty )

That outbreak is the largest in the nation and led to salad-maker Taylor Farms’ recall of iceberg lettuce sourced from Central Mexico. The lettuce had been served at several locations of the fast-food chain Taco Bell and the recall also included lettuce that was sold at retail stores.

There are now several outbreaks reported nationwide, but questions still swirl surrounding sources of exposure. There have also been reports of outbreaks in the U.K.

Some cases in North Carolina have been linked to parsley and cilantro, state health officials said.

In a typical year, the U.S. sees just a few thousand cases, experts told CNN.

While the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention has received 6,707 lab-confirmed cases of cyclosporiasis since May 1 and is aware of more than 11.500 additional cases that are not lab-confirmed, it only shows Michigan with 1,000-4,000 cases on its surveillance webpage.

The agency says there is a six-week lag between illness onset and case reporting, and it anticipates that case counts will continue to rise.

Part of that is because of the nature of cyclosporiasis. Infections are caused when people are exposed to the parasite cyclospora, often through produce.

open image in gallery It’s hard to trace the microscopic parasite cyclospora , which is spread solely through humans ( CDC )

But it can take weeks for symptoms of infection to appear, including vomiting, nausea and dehydration.

By this time, people may have forgotten what they had consumed and tainted products may already be out of grocery stores.

It’s also hard to trace cyclospora. The microscopic parasite - which is only spread by humans - cannot be traced using advanced testing methods that help scientists with bacteria and pathogens.

"FDA relies on whole genome sequencing to effectively fingerprint a pathogen to try to isolate a particular pathogen to ​a particular outbreak to a particular grower. You don't have that in this case,” former FDA Commissioner Scott Gottlieb told Reuters.

Taylor Sheridan’s thriller series Lioness centers on an all-female undercover CIA operation that is loosely based on a real-life U.S. Marine unit.

Lioness, which returned with its third season August 2 on Paramount+, follows Zoe Saldaña’s character Joe McNamara, a CIA operative who leads a top-secret group of female special operatives recruited from various branches of the military and tasked with infiltrating terrorist organizations by befriending their wives and daughters.

In real life, Task Force Lioness operated out of Iraq and Afghanistan to identify women who might have been used to carry out terrorist activities. The concept inspired Lioness executive producer Jill Wagner, who also acts in the show, and her husband David Lemanowicz to approach Sheridan to write a series about it.

“I feared that someone would get a hold of this idea and just create Barbies with guns or try to make the women feel too superhero-like,” Wagner told Decider. “People have to understand that there are many female heroes in the world, and they’re not necessarily in Marvel movies. They’re out there sacrificing for our country, and they have really interesting stories to tell. Because of Taylor’s voice and his mind, I knew he was the one person who could do them justice. So that’s why I went to him.”

Read on for the true story of the all-female Lioness team.

open image in gallery Zoe Saldaña and Nicole Kidman star in ‘Lioness,’ which is loosely based on a real military group used in the Iraq War ( Paramount+ )

open image in gallery ‘Lioness’ is created by Taylor Sheridan, the mastermind behind ‘Yellowstone’ and its many spin-offs ( Paramount+ )

Who were the real-life Lionesses?

During the Iraq War in 2003, the American military ran into a problem as male soldiers stationed in Iraq were not allowed to search female civilians due to strict Muslim beliefs that prohibited any man from touching an unrelated woman.

Rebels quickly caught on to the issue and began to use women to smuggle weapons and explosives for terrorist attacks.

Soon, the Marine Corps and the Army formed the Lionesses to conduct more thorough surveillance on hijabi women. Team Lioness consisted of boots-on-the-ground female soldiers — often mechanics, clerks and engineers — who were deployed to combat units in Iraq and Afghanistan.

The women accompanied male troops on patrols and house-to-house operations, conducted searches on women and children at checkpoints and established rapport with women in the community for the sake of disseminating information and identifying people who might be involved in terrorist activity.

open image in gallery Team Lioness led to the establishment of the Female Engagement Team that was sent to Afghanistan in 2010 ( Getty )

What happened to the Lioness program?

Although Team Lioness was successful, the initiative was eventually phased out because of its short-term tactics. However, the program led to the Marine Corps officially establishing Female Engagement Teams in 2009, which focused more on gaining access to the community rather than being attached to combat units.

In 2013, the Department of Defense also lifted the combat exclusion rule, which allowed female members of the military to join combat units and further eliminated the need for a separate female team.

Although hundreds of women cycled through the all-female unit Team Lioness, the characters in Sheridan’s show — which stars Saldaña, Nicole Kidman and Morgan Freeman — are fictionalized and not based on any specific person.

New episodes of Lioness air Sundays at 3 a.m. ET / 12 a.m. PT on Paramount+.

The English Football Association is set to withdraw its support for Gianni Infantino’s re-election as Fifa president after his scrapped World Cup privatisation bid.

Infantino’s leadership is under intense scrutiny, with a widespread loss of confidence coming after his failed attempt to sell off stakes in the World Cup to private investors.

Wales became the first member association to officially retract its support of the Swiss-Italian in an attempt to force him out, and England is expected to follow suit.

The FA is preparing to send a letter to Fifa to withdraw its backing, piling more pressure on Infantino.

open image in gallery FA chief executive Mark Bullingham next to Infantino in 2023 ( PA )

Infantino, whose decade-long reign is under severe pressure, announced on Friday night that he was shelving the widely-denounced plan, which had been rejected by three confederations after initially being revealed earlier in the week.

Concacaf, the confederation for North America and the Caribbean, along with the Asian Football Confederation, fumed over the lack of consultation while Europe’s governing body Uefa threatened to boycott all Fifa competitions, including next year’s Women’s World Cup and the 2030 World Cup, before Infantino’s eventual climb-down.

Uefa confirmed that it had lost confidence in Infantino’s leadership after he went back on his plans, criticising the “shabby, backroom deal”, and has now written to the Fifa president confirming it is “actively considering” legal action in regard to the sell-off scheme.

The letter orders Infantino and Fifa to “take immediate steps to identify, locate, and preserve all documents and electronically stored information described in this notice that are in your or Fifa’s possession, custody, or control”.

Prime minister Andy Burnham said that Infantino is the “wrong man” to lead Fifa, while the FA called for a “full and robust review” into his leadership as the fallout of his U-turn continues.

Infantino also became the subject of criticism from within his administration, with senior adviser Carlos Cordeiro resigning over the plans, while Fifa chief operating officer Kevin Lamour claimed the president had “deceived” Fifa staff.

The proposal involved establishing Fifa Forward Enterprise and selling a 20 per cent stake to private investors, with Joshua Kushner’s Thrive Eternal reportedly earmarked as the lead investor group. He is the brother of Jared Kushner, who is the son-in-law of US president Donald Trump.

Trump, however, insisted he had not spoken about the sell-off plan with Infantino before it was scrapped.

open image in gallery US president Donald Trump insisted he had not spoken to Infantino about the sell-off plan ( PA )

There are calls for Infantino to resign, but as it stands he will run for re-election in March 2027.

Uefa has indicated that “no option should be off the table” regarding the future of Infantino, hinting at the possibility of a no-confidence vote.

Such a move, if triggered by just 43 national associations, would necessitate an Extraordinary Fifa Congress.

However, this action is considered improbable unless there is a strong conviction, if not certainty, that a majority among Fifa's 211 member nations would vote to remove Infantino at such a gathering.

Several African and Asian football bodies, including those from Morocco, Egypt and Qatar, have publicly voiced their support for Infantino over the weekend.

A weeks-long charade over Todd Blanche’s political future is over, for now. It ended as it began, with President Donald Trump, his family and their businesses receiving sweeping immunity from tax audits.

As a condition for their support for the president’s former criminal defense attorney as U.S. Attorney General, a pair of Republican senators wanted assurance that a nearly $1.8 billion “Anti-Weaponization Fund” to reward the president’s political allies was “permanently” terminated. They also wanted clarification around the IRS deal, which “forever” bars the government from any “examinations or similar or related reviews” into the Trump family’s taxes.

Blanche conceded on Sunday night the so-called slush fund is “rescinded and shall have no force or effect.” But he reiterated the terms of the tax shield, which he says isn’t going anywhere, and he “stands by” testimony in which he said that “nothing has changed” about the plan. That was enough for Senators Thom Tillis and John Cornyn, who say they’re “pleased” with Blanche’s note and will vote to confirm him.

The administration never needed a slush fund to settle claims from January 6 rioters and other Trump allies. They can file, and already have filed, claims against the government that Trump’s Justice Department would be more than happy to settle using a virtually unlimited pot of taxpayer cash.

Instead, the slush fund ran a convenient cover to protect Trump’s immunity deal. He will publicly mourn its end and claim how unfairly rioters who tried to overturn his election loss were treated by federal prosecutors, drumming up support from a base that was promised “retribution” while leaving them behind in his desperate quest for self-preservation.

open image in gallery The Trump administration has agreed to formally drop plans for an ‘Anti-Weaponization Fund’ to save Todd Blanche’s nomination for Attorney General — but a deal granting IRS immunity to Trump and his family remains in place ( AFP/Getty )

Meanwhile, Cornyn and Tillis will pat themselves on the back for what they seem to believe is an important check against the president. Instead, they’ve just enshrined Trump’s corruption.

A slush fund for the president’s allies was dead on arrival and blocked in courts. Nothing is stopping the Trump administration from signing multi-million dollar checks to aggrieved “victims” of government “weaponization” through existing channels, and Blanche and Trump could easily revive plans for the fund at some other point.

For now — at least on paper, under the fraudulent guise of compromise to ensure Blanche’s confirmation — the “slush fund” is dead. Trump’s unprecedented shield from tax investigations, on the other hand, is very much alive.

open image in gallery Tod Blanche faced questions about his refusal to put in writing an agreement to end Trump’s so-called ‘slush fund’ ( Getty )

Remember how we got here: The president sued his own administration for $10 billion in January, pitting his personal lawyers against his own Department of Justice, over allegations that the IRS improperly released his tax documents, leading to revealing reporting in The New York Times that found he paid only $750 in federal income taxes in 2016 and 2017.

The federal judge overseeing the lawsuit appointed a team of outside lawyers to help her untangle the unusual nature of a president suing himself. In their brief to the court on May 14, those outside lawyers stopped short of recommending the lawsuit be dismissed but noted the “significant” and “unprecedented” issues at stake and suggested the court should hear more from the parties involved.

“A sitting president seeks monetary damages for alleged harm to his personal interests from an executive agency that he controls,” they wrote.

Trump and the IRS never filed a response, and on May 18, the Justice Department published a press release announcing the “Anti-Weaponization Fund,” which promised massive taxpayer-funded payouts to alleged “victims” of government “weaponization,” including January 6 rioters and close allies of the president.

One day later, in a memo that Blanche later called an “attorney general order,” the Justice Department granted the president immunity from tax investigations.

That immunity, which applies only to existing audits and not future investigations, shields the president from potentially damaging rulings that could have cost him more than $100 million.

A different judge ultimately blocked the slush fund after Blanche testified to members of Congress that the administration was “not moving forward” with the plans, and the judge overseeing the IRS lawsuit sanctioned the president’s legal team for laundering the “settlement” scheme through her courtroom.

open image in gallery Sens. John Cornyn, pictured, and Thom Tillis wanted DOJ’s written assurance that the ‘slush fund’ was dead, but their terms effectively enshrined Trump’s sweeping IRS immunity deal under the guise of compromise ( Reuters )

To be clear, Blanche’s appointment to attorney general was never in doubt. Trump threatened to pull his name from consideration after Republican senators drew their weak line in the sand, but Trump could keep him in his “acting” role indefinitely.

Cornyn and Tillis didn’t ask for the Justice Department to rip up the IRS deal. They wanted firm language that would let Trump keep it, or risk a drawn-out confirmation process through a politically volatile period for congressional Republicans despite a result for Blanche that was always inevitable.

Enter the president’s corrupt bargain: The administration will permanently abandon plans for a slush fund the government never needed to settle claims brought by his allies, and the IRS deal will remain in place.

In a letter dated August 2 on the Office of the Attorney General letterhead, Blanche said the "Anti-Weaponization Fund” is “rescinded and shall have no force or effect.”

A second undated and unsigned notice notes that Blanche’s IRS immunity deal applies “only retroactively” and affects only the “named parties in the lawsuit” referenced in the order.

“From the outset, we were clear that we needed a written document addressing our concerns on the IRS audit agreement and the anti-weaponization fund that included constraining the scope of audit protection by limiting it to the parties of the Settlement Agreement and legally ending the anti- weaponization fund,” Cornyn and Tillis said in a joint statement Monday.

The senators were “pleased” by Blanche’s statements and expressed “gratitude” for putting them forward.

January 6 rioters looking for payouts from the government, despite mass pardons getting them off the hook for assaulting law enforcement and storming the halls of Congress, won’t get a dime from the nonexistent $1.8 billion fund.

Lawyers representing them are already lining up other lawsuits against the government, but they’ll have to wait. Trump’s protections, after all, come first.

The teenage girl made it through the waves to Spanish territory. Her little brother did not, drowning in the Mediterranean, while their mother disappeared in the chaos when tens of thousands of people surged through the breakwater, trying to leave Morocco behind.

The tragic story of a 17-year-old from Tangier is representative of the plight of many of the more than 800 minors who four days after the collective push by migrants into Ceuta face a scary present and an uncertain future.

She told an Associated Press photojournalist how she and her family joined the massive crowd that tried to swim around a border fence to reach the Spanish territory on Thursday. Like many, she said they did so seeking better opportunities. The AP is withholding her identity because she is a minor in a vulnerable situation.

She described how she saw Spanish police pull the body of her 8-year-old brother from the water.

She made it to the shore but became separated from her mother, and has spent the last four days on her own. She said some locals gave her food and some clothing, with one woman taking her into her home so she could bathe. She then went to a center for youths run by the government for some help, but found it was full.

“I saw people stepping on the dead,” she said through a translator since she doesn't speak Spanish. “Now we are children begging on the street.”

She is one of some 860 minors who remained in Ceuta on Monday after crossing over, according to local officials. AP journalists saw other minors asking for food.

Those minors now make up a large part of the 3,000-5,000 migrants who have avoided expulsion from Ceuta of the original 60,000 who came across. Spanish authorities confirmed 72 people died, mostly in the water, during the crossing. Morocco reported 11 deaths which are not included in the Spanish total, the Spanish interior ministry said.

Minors must be cared for under Spanish law

Spanish law says that adult migrants can apply for asylum. If rejected, they will face expulsion procedures. The bar is normally very high for Moroccans to be granted humanitarian protection.

Migrant minors who are unaccompanied by adults, however, are supposed to be granted protection and taken care of by Spanish authorities.

An AP journalist witnessed Spanish soldiers escorting an unaccompanied Moroccan boy who was crying and begging not to be sent back to Morocco. A few meters before reaching the border, and due to pressure from local residents who insisted he was a minor, as well as the presence of the media, a lieutenant colonel in the Spanish Army stopped the repatriation and transferred the boy to the Spanish Civil Guard.

Most of the Moroccan adults have either voluntarily gone home or were pushed back by Spanish police. Among those who remain in Ceuta are significant numbers of people from other countries, including Sudanese fleeing their war-torn country, Palestinians from Gaza and Afghans, as well as people from several African nations.

The city’s migrant center with a capacity for 600 people is completely full. Food is scarce among the migrants, according to reporting by AP journalists.

“The strategy is that hunger, thirst and exhaustion forces these people to finally decide to voluntarily return to Morocco,” said local migration activist Ramsés Mohamed Azumik of Asociación Elín.

Many migrants sleep or rest on the beach or hills surrounding the spec of Spain. In the hazy distance, mainland Europe, their ultimate goal, lies across the sea.

___

Associated Press writer Joseph Wilson reported from Barcelona, Spain.

News.title: Nigel Farage leaves door open for pact with Rupert Lowe’s Restore Britain
News.content:

Whether it's investigating the financials of Elon Musk's pro-Trump PAC or producing our latest documentary, 'The A Word', which shines a light on the American women fighting for reproductive rights, we know how important it is to parse out the facts from the messaging. At such a critical moment in US history, we need reporters on the ground. Your donation allows us to keep sending journalists to speak to both sides of the story. The Independent is trusted by Americans across the entire political spectrum. And unlike many other quality news outlets, we choose not to lock Americans out of our reporting and analysis with paywalls. We believe quality journalism should be available to everyone, paid for by those who can afford it. Your support makes all the difference. Read more

Nigel Farage has opened the door to talks with his ally-turned-rival Rupert Lowe over a pact between Reform UK and Restore Britain as he tries to reverse his party’s fortunes after a series of major setbacks.

Mr Lowe, a former Reform MP, extended an unlikely olive branch to Mr Farage, despite several public rows between the pair in recent months.

The Reform UK leader offered a lukewarm response at first, before revealing on Monday he had “reached out” to Mr Lowe to discuss working with Restore Britain.

Reform is facing crises on multiple fronts, with continued scrutiny over its financial dealings, the resurgence of Labour in the polls, and the growing threat of Restore Britain as it continues to eat into the party’s vote share, among some of the key issues it is yet to resolve.

Meanwhile, Mr Farage, who last week saw his approval rating hit its lowest level since the 2024 general election, faces a by-election next week that he is widely expected to win but which could still prove humiliating, given his main opponent is comedian candidate Count Binface.

Discussions about Restore and Reform working together come after Mr Lowe acrimoniously left Mr Farage’s party in March 2025 amid claims of bullying and threatening behaviour, before going on to found his own party, Restore Britain. The Crown Prosecution Service (CPS) said Mr Lowe would face no criminal charges.

open image in gallery Nigel Farage and Rupert Lowe arrive at the House of Commons together in July 2024 after both being elected as Reform UK MPs ( PA )

The party – which until now has largely been based in Mr Lowe’s constituency, Great Yarmouth – is further to the right than Reform on issues such as immigration and has enjoyed support from tech billionaire Elon Musk, who has publicly backed Restore Britain a number of times on his X platform.

But despite Mr Farage saying he was “open-minded” about talks, relations quickly soured again when Mr Lowe accused the Reform UK leader of lying about having “reached out”.

In a press conference on Monday, Mr Farage said: “If you want to do a political deal with somebody, you know, you would contact them privately and not do a 12-minute video.

“That said, I did actually reach out back yesterday to him. I did say, ‘look, should we have a call?’ I haven’t heard back yet, so I don’t know what the sincerity of this is.”

open image in gallery Rupert Lowe has urged Nigel Farage to put their past disagreements aside ( PA )

However, in a post on X after the press conference, Mr Lowe shared a screenshot of a message he said was from Mr Farage, which read, “Will call later”.

The MP for Great Yarmouth added: “I do not want to make private conversations public, but Farage has just done so at a national press conference.

“He just stated he said to me yesterday ‘Shall we have a call?’ Sadly, that is just a lie.

“Yesterday, at 10.30, Nigel messaged me, saying the following three words: ‘Will call later’, the evidence is below. I have received no call.”

Mr Lowe said his offer to the party “remains open” but added: “Outright lying about our private conversations does not help that.”

Outlining his conditions of a pact with Reform, Mr Lowe on Sunday said that Mr Farage would have to commit to not having any former Conservative ministers, such as Tory defectors Robert Jenrick and Suella Braverman, in any future cabinet.

“I truly believe there could be sufficient common ground for our two movements to cooperate collectively (to) destroy the looming left-wing alliance that will finish off what hope remains for this country,” Mr Lowe said in his video.

open image in gallery Nigel Farage during a press conference on Monday ( PA )

“We have recently shown how effectively cooperation can work locally on the Norfolk County Council, so why not at national level?”

Responding to that, Mr Farage in the press conference said: “I don’t ditch my friends. I don’t ditch my allies, whether that’s Suella Braverman or Posh George (Cottrell), you know I do not ditch people because somebody else wants me to.”

The Reform leader added: “In broader terms, look, you could see a situation where Restore, without the hope of winning anything outside Great Yarmouth, I mean literally without hope of winning a single seat in the country, could do us great harm.

“I think online you will see a lot of Restore potential voters now beginning to worry about the impact that might have.

“I finalise that by saying if it was the offer of a deal, it came in a very unusual way. I have responded to it potentially, you know, with an open mind, as I would, but I’m certainly not going to be ditching people who I view to be allies and a great asset.”

open image in gallery The Reform UK leader rejected conditions that Rupert Lowe had attached to a possible pact ( PA )

Mr Lowe’s party claimed fourth place in the Greater Manchester mayoral by-election, gaining 8.7 per cent of the vote while Reform came second with 21 per cent.

In the Makerfield by-election, which was won by Andy Burnham, the two parties also outpolled the Conservatives and Liberal Democrats.

But Mr Farage continues to face questions after he and his party became embroiled in a series of financial scandals.

Deputy leader Richard Tice has become the latest figure to be facing an investigation by the parliamentary standards watchdog for allegedly failing to declare ‌an interest.

The standards commissioner, Daniel Greenberg, confirmed on its website that an investigation had been opened into allegations against the Reform UK deputy leader on Tuesday last week.

Mr Tice has claimed the investigation relates to a complaint over “whether I should have referenced my register of interests at the start of a debate on UK democracy and Israeli influence”.

The probe comes just days after the standards watchdog declined to investigate a complaint relating to an undeclared loan of almost £80,000 to Mr Tice from convicted fraudster and Farage ally Mr Cottrell.

Meanwhile, Reform UK has come under fire for its “ridiculous” plan to use Royal Navy ships to stop small-boat crossings from France.

Dubbed Operation Fortress, Farage’s party announced plans on Monday to intercept migrant boats and return them to France or Belgium should they win the next election.

But the plan – unveiled amid heightened unrest at the Spain-Morocco border – has sparked criticism from political opposition, former navy officers, as well as legal and migration experts, who claim the plan is dangerous, “lacks substance” and would be unworkable under maritime law.

News.content:

Emma Raducanu will miss the US Open due to a stress fracture in her right leg, the latest blow in a career and season hampered by injury woes.

The 23-year-old sustained the fracture during the grass-court season and pulled out of Wimbledon on the eve of the tournament after being pictured in an orthopaedic boot.

She also wore a protective boot in videos she posted on social media recently as she continues her recovery in St Moritz, prompting further concerns over her fitness and ability to take part in the final grand slam of the year.

PA has reported that Raducanu has decided on advice from her medical team that she will withdraw from the US Open, which begins on 30 August.

Having made positive progress last summer, including winning her first matches at Flushing Meadows since lifting the trophy five years ago, it has been a frustrating 12 months for Raducanu with more persistent physical issues.

After a foot injury severely hampered her pre-season training Raducanu then spent two-and-a-half months off court with a lingering post-viral illness after initially falling unwell in early February.

She finally returned for the end of the clay-court season having rehired Andrew Richardson, the coach who guided her to the US Open title, but the pair’s time on court together has been limited.

Raducanu enjoyed one of the best weeks of her career by reaching her biggest final since the 2021 US Open at Queen’s in June, where she lost to Croatia’s Donna Vekic.

That week produced some of her best and most consistent performances in some time but also triggered her latest injury setback, which then forced her to withdraw from Wimbledon the evening before her first-round match.

She was not among the players named in Great Britain’s team for the Billie Jean King Cup Finals in late September and there must be question marks over whether Raducanu, who will slide from her current ranking of 49, will compete again in 2026.

Additional reporting by PA

News.title: The 13 best castle hotels in England
News.content:
Few places capture the imagination quite like a castle, and England is home to some of the most remarkable places to spend the night. If it’s not the romance of waking up in a canopied four-poster bed, or losing ourselves in centuries-old tapestries and visceral oil paintings, we are lured by tales of brave knights and plotting dignitaries, duplicitous royals and ghosts parleying secrets in the hallways.

Part of the magic is spending an afternoon wandering grounds and gardens followed by evenings in front of a roaring fire, or dining in a banquet hall that may have hosted medieval kings and queens. While not every castle has crenellated battlements, glistening moats or royal connections, each stony stronghold on our list has something special that makes it worth travelling for. In this modern age that might include a spa, fine-dining restaurant or extra touches like free admission to exhibitions and museum tours. Here’s our pick of the best castle hotels in England.

News.title: Careless Liverpool concede same goal twice in second-half capitulation against Leeds
News.content:
Soldier Field in Chicago hosts an all-Premier League tie encounter as Liverpool take on Leeds as both sides bring their US tours to a close. Both Premier League encounters between these sides last season ended in draws; a 3-3 draw at Elland Road was followed up by a 0-0 stalemate at Anfield. The draw at Elland Road was immediately followed by Mohamed Salah speaking to the media, claiming he had been thrown under the bus.

It is a new era at Liverpool as former Bournemouth boss Andoni Iraola has replaced Arne Slot at Anfield. They kicked off the Iraola era in Nashville, Tennessee, with a 4-2 win over Sunderland, following that up with another victory in New York on Wednesday night, beating Wrexham 1-0, and will be aiming to make it three wins from three on their US tour.

“I think it [the US tour] has been really, really useful,” Iraola said in an interview on the official Liverpool website. Obviously, you spend a lot of time with the players, with the staff, you get all the information you can. And I think there is also an evolution, it has to be. We start to understand each other better, what we need to do. Every game, I hope we can get closer and closer and put ourselves in a position where the few players that still are not here start to train also, they are helped by the others.”

Virgil van Dijk and Cody Gakpo resumed training back on Merseyside whilst Alexis Mac Allister, Alisson and Victor Munoz are yet to return to training following their World Cup exploits. The trio of Florian Wirtz, Alexander Isak and Ryan Gravenberch are all set to feature for the first time this pre-season.

Leeds’ pre-season campaign began with a 3-2 loss to Championship Wrexham in Tampa, Florida before beating Sunderland 1-0 in New Jersey courtesy of a long-range strike from Lukas Nmecha. Former Liverpool man Harry Wilson joined Leeds on a free from Fulham this summer.

“Really tough but that is expected,” Wilson said. That is what pre-season is for, building up a base for when the season starts, making sure you are in the best physical position you can be to attack the season. It has been good. I played against them [Leeds] twice last year when I was at Fulham. Both games were really, really tough games.

“I think when the fans have got a good team to support, I think that [the atmosphere at Elland Road] goes up a notch. I think the size of the club was a massive part of me coming. Then speaking to the guys, the chairman, the sporting director, and seeing kind of the plans and the aims for the club, it is something I wanted to be a part of.”

Team news to follow shortly.

News.title: Oil plummets as Trump calls off Iran strikes
News.content:
Oil prices have plunged after Donald Trump called off strikes and said the US and Iran would hold further peace talks.

Brent crude, the international benchmark, sank as much as 9.5pc early on Monday to less than $82 a barrel after the US president said he had halted plans for “disastrous” strikes.

Mr Trump said: “Obviously, they don’t want to be attacked. They knew the extent of the attack because they saw it forming.

“Now what we’re doing is we’re talking to them in the form of a negotiation. It begins tomorrow afternoon.”

Mr ‌Trump also ordered oil companies to lower petrol prices for American ‌consumers ‌and criticised ⁠Chevron’s chief executive for not crediting his administration for supporting the fossil fuel industry.

The president said that he had been asked by Iran as well as US partners Saudi Arabia, the United Arab Emirates and Qatar to hold off on strikes. He halted plans for a major attack against Iran on Saturday, which he said would have been the biggest since the Second World War.

Mr Trump claimed the sides were on the “perimeter” of a peace deal.

Oil’s sharp fall also sent the cost of government borrowing lower on Monday over hopes that it would ease inflation.

The yield on 10-year UK gilts, a benchmark for what the Treasury pays to borrow money, dropped from 5.05pc to 4.98pc, while the equivalent US bonds dropped from 4.74pc to 4.69pc.

Stock markets in Europe also rose, with the FTSE 100 up 0.2pc, the Cac 40 in Paris up 0.3pc and the Dax in Frankfurt climbing 0.1pc.

News.title: Inside the trial for a vaccine to end malaria
News.content:
A small group of brave volunteers were given an experimental vaccine in Oxford this week in a bid to bring to an end the centuries-old scourge of malaria.

“I’m on my second vaccine now. Then I’m due to have my third vaccine soon, and then in November, I’ll be given malaria,” said an upbeat Mike Luciw, a 32-year-old local who works in recruitment.

“The hope is to help find something that could save millions of people.”

There are already two licenced vaccines for malaria but the new Oxford “RH5” shot is not like anything that has come before.

The existing jabs only act against malaria as it moves towards the liver in the early stage of infection, and provide only partial protection.

The new combination vaccine, in contrast, is designed to fight it off both at the liver stage and in the wider bloodstream, effectively knocking it out altogether.

The project is being run by the husband and wife team of Simon Draper, Professor of Vaccinology and Translational Medicine at the University of Oxford, and Professor Angela Minassian, an infectious disease specialist and clinical lead for their malaria programme in Oxford’s Department of Paediatrics.

“The dream for malaria … has been to have these two lines of defence, liver and blood, so if the first line fails, you’ve got a second,” says Prof Draper, who leads on the science.

“Our dream is to have a vaccine that gives over 90 per cent efficacy in African children,” adds Prof Minassian, who heads the clinical trials for the new jab.

News.title: Dowman weaves his magic and new signing shines as Arsenal hit ground running
News.content:
Hello and welcome to our live coverage for this pre-season friendly between Girona and Arsenal at Estadi Montilivi in Catalonia.

With the transfer speculation surrounding Vinícius Júnior’s and Bruno Guimaraes’ potential moves to Arsenal ramping up, the reigning Premier League champions are in action against Girona as they step up their preparations ahead of the upcoming campaign.

Unlike other Premier League heavyweights, Arsenal have kept their pre-season tour relatively local with a selection of games in Spain, Ireland and England, before they face Manchester City in the FA Community Shield on August 16 at the Millennium Stadium in Cardiff.

Arsenal beat League One side MK Dons 3-0 in a behind-closed-doors friendly on July 25 at the Sobha Realty Training Centre, thanks to goals from Reiss Nelson, Ethan Nwaneri and Ceadach O’Neill.

After featuring in this victory and setting up Nelson for the opener, Christos Tzolis will be looking to continue his positive momentum with his new club, after joining Arsenal for £34m earlier this summer. Many fans will be keeping a close eye on the recently-signed winger given that various core members of last season’s Premier League-winning squad are yet to return from their post-World Cup breaks, having progressed deep in the competition.

Tournament winners David Raya, Martin Zubimendi and Mikel Merino, Norway captain Martin Odegaard, as well as England internationals Bukayo Saka, Declan Rice, Eberechi Eze and Noni Madueke are all missing for this game, while France’s William Saliba is out injured and set for an extended period on the sidelines.

Those who exited the World Cup earlier than the aforementioned players, including Gabriel Magalhaes, Gabriel Martinelli, Piero Hincapie, Kai Havertz, and Viktor Gyokeres, have all joined up with the squad in northern Spain.

Mikel Arteta’s men will play a wounded Girona, who suffered relegation from the top flight of Spanish football last season due to a 19th-place finish.

Kick-off is at 19:00, with team news arriving shortly.

News.title: Josh Kerr turns ‘race of the century’ into one-sided show of power
News.content:
For many the 100m is the Blue Riband event the one everyone wants to watch and the race that steals all the headlines. For these Commonwealth Games, however, tonight’s mile race is the one that has grabbed all the attention – and it is not hard to see why.

Josh Kerr, fresh from his new world record of 3:42.66 (a time that beat a mark that had stood since 1999) takes on fellow Scot Jake Wightman and Australia’s new superstar Cameron Myers. Three great runners over a distance that evokes sepia-tinted memories of Roger Bannister and the seminal four-minute mark.

Some of you may be wondering why the mile is back at an international event. Well, Seb Coe, the president of World Athletics and someone who broke the mile record three times, says the race distance is easy to understand and resonates with fans. And, coming on the back of Kerr’s world record, who can argue with him?

This is the first time the mile has been run at the games since 1966 and the hope is that tonight’s final matches the Miracle Mile run in 1954. Earlier that year Bannister broke the four-minute barrier, only for Australia’s John Landy to go lower with a time of 3:58.0 soon after. The Games in Vancouver were the first time two sub-four minuters had gone head-to-head. And the race didn’t disappoint – Bannister beating Landy with a time of 3:58.8 minutes. The Australian also ran under four minutes, making it the first time two men had done so in the same race.

Obviously all three of the expected main protagonists will go well under four minutes, but if they can recreate the drama of the 1954 final then we’ll have a race to savour.

Stay here for all the action with the gun set to go off at 8.55.

News.title: Exciting young talent JJ Gabriel makes debut as Man Utd beat Atletico Madrid
News.content:
Manchester United 2 Atletico Madrid 1

JJ Gabriel showed glimpses of his potential as he made his Manchester United debut in their 2-1 win over Atletico Madrid in Stockholm.

The 15-year-old may have been introduced with only eight minutes remaining, but, given how highly rated he is, it was a significant move by Michael Carrick to give him game time in the senior team.

There were hints of why Gabriel is so well regarded during those eight minutes, as he found space in the centre of the pitch and linked well with Leny Yoro. But he was also on the receiving end of some physical challenges – something he will have to grow accustomed to the more he plays at senior level.

Yoro, who himself made his senior debut as a 16-year-old for Lille, was impressed by Gabriel and said: “He’s a really good player. He is still really young and still has a lot to learn and a lot to improve on but he’s really humble and still working, so I’m happy for him to get his first minutes. I hope, for him, it’s going to continue like that.”

News.title: City fire blanks in shoot-out as Maresca’s opening game ends in defeat by Inter
News.content:
Manchester City 1 Inter Milan 1; Inter win 3-1 on pens

Manchester City lost the Asahi Super Dry Trophy 3-1 on a penalty shoot-out against Inter Milan.

Enzo Maresca took charge of the Premier League runners-up for the first time since his arrival as Pep Guardiola’s replacement, though he was without many of his stars who had yet to return from World Cup duty.

One of the players missing was Elliot Anderson, the £116m signing from Nottingham Forest, though Jeremy Monga, 16, was an unused substitute after being brought in from Leicester City in the summer transfer window.

City took the lead on 14 minutes through Divin Mubamba as he tapped in an Antoine Semenyo cross, but Inter’s experienced defender Benjamin Pavard levelled just six minutes later when City failed to clear a corner.

The Premier League side dominated possession in the second half after an even first 45 minutes but could not find a way through. Phil Foden, the captain, was again underwhelming after a difficult year last season, but with the season still to come he had plenty of time to show his best form once more after signing a new contract at the Etihad.

The game went to penalties after full-time with no extra time played, and only Claudio Echeverri held his nerve for City as Inter Milan scored three of theirs, Matteo Lavelli netting the winning spot-kick.

Both teams learnt little from the match as Inter made 11 changes and City eight, though Maresca will have been impressed by Ryan McAidoo’s performance as a second-half substitute, as he regularly threatened from the right wing. The 18-year-old forward will surely be in demand from other clubs looking to loan him, and City may yet be tempted to keep him around for the coming season.

Sports.title: Tonda Eckert reveals he was sent DEATH THREATS after Spygate and police warned Southampton boss not to drive his car
Sports.content:
TONDA ECKERT has revealed that he was sent DEATH THREATS following Southampton’s Spygate controversy.

The Saints were booted out of the Championship Play-Off final after being found guilty of spying on rivals Middlesbrough.



Boro were handed Southampton’s spot in the final which they ultimately lost to Hull City.

The south coast side were also handed a four-point penalty, which comes into action at the start of the 2026/27 season.



Eckert, 33, could be further punished as he is currently the subject of a charge from the FA.

The German manager is awaiting the punishment after the FA found that the spying on Oxford United, Ipswich Town and Boro was a “contrived and determined plan from the top down”.



Southampton have stood by the coach and refused to sack him and instead want him to continue in post.

However, he could be handed a substantial touchline ban by the FA.

Eckert has been sent supportive messages from “well-known colleagues” from both Germany and in England.

The public view has been less kind as he revealed that some have even sent him death threats.



SUN VEGAS WELCOME OFFER: GET UP TO £100 BONUS

Due to the intensity of the threats, Eckert was advised not to drive himself and even to sit in the back of his car.

He told Kicker: “Yes, it could no longer be handled without the police.

“I do not want to go into details, only this much: I was advised not to drive myself any more, but to sit in the back of the car instead.

“That was very difficult.



“It was a situation no coaching course prepares you for.

“No training explains how to react when, for security reasons, you are suddenly supposed to sit in the back seat.

“As I said, it was very difficult.”

Eckert has been charged by the FA with acting in an improper manner and bringing football into disrepute.



He has still been taking training and preparing Southampton for the new season with the aim of promotion to the Premier League.

However, he has admitted that the charge is complicating things and hanging over him.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

He told BBC Radio Solent: “I would be lying if I said that it is not in the back of my mind.

“I think that’s true for everyone involved, but the positive thing is I just love the game. I love football – there’s so much to prepare for.”

Sports.title: Newcastle ‘make contact with Victor Froholdt’s agent but face two issues over landing £73m Bruno Guimaraes replacement’
Sports.content:
NEWCASTLE have reached out to the best player in Portugal as they search for Bruno Guimaraes’ successor, according to reports.

With the Magpies’ Brazilian superstar seeking a multi-million pound move to Arsenal, Newcastle have been exploring a potential bid for Porto‘s Victor Froholdt.



The Tyneside outfit are understood to have moved beyond merely scouting the midfielder, and have approached Froholdt’s agents to gauge interest in a move to the Premier League.

However, any attempt to entice Porto’s leading light to St James’ Park will have to overcome significant personal and financial barriers.



If Newcastle were to formally approach the Portuguese giants about their 20-year-old starlet, they would have to be prepared to meet a hefty €85million release clause (roughly £73 million).

Porto’s No8 recently underlined a dream debut season by scooping up the league’s two biggest individual accolades, winning Player of the Year and Young Player of the Year alongside the Primeira Liga title.



Although Newcastle’s plush Saudi owners may not be deterred by the Dane’s sky-high valuation, they could struggle to move past Froholdt’s personal attachment to Porto.

Two days ago, the box-to-box midfielder secured yet more silverware in Portugal‘s second city by heading home the winning goal in the Portuguese Super Cup.

Speaking shortly after claiming the trophy, Froholdt was quick to spurn any speculation over his future at the Estadio Do Dragao.

In the Dane’s own dismissive words: “People talk about taking the next step, but for me, FC Porto is a huge club.



CASINO SPECIAL – BEST CASINO BONUSES FROM £10 DEPOSITS

“I’m already focused on the next game, for the championship.

“I like being here. Now, let’s go all out for the championship.”

Newcastle had been scouting the midfield maestro prior to his £18m move to Porto last summer, but have ramped up their interest amid Arsenal‘s attempts to poach Bruno Guimaraes.

The Magpies rejected a bid for their captain earlier today, but are battling against the allure of the Premier League champions, alongside the Brazilian’s personal wish to leave.



Tyneside has already been rocked by a whirlwind summer window.

League Cup winning manager Eddie Howe confirmed his shock resignation last week, while superstars Sandro Tonali and Anthony Gordon have jetted off for a combined £169m.

Five fresh faces have touched down at St James’ Park in the meantime, alongside a new manager in Matthias Jaissle.

Sports.title: Gianni Infantino opponents ‘plotting rival World Cup competition’ to ‘paralyse’ Fifa until he quits
Sports.content:
UEFA has joined forces with other confederations and threatened to set up their own version of the World Cup if disgraced Fifa supremo Gianni Infantino refuses to quit.

The Swiss millionaire, 56, sensationally vowed to desperately cling onto his job after sending shockwaves through football.

Infantino made shock plans to flog shares in the World Cup to private investors before being forced into a humiliating U-turn.



And Uefa president Aleksander Ceferin, along with Concacaf and the Asian Football Confederation chiefs, is pushing for him to resign.



The Times report an alliance has been formed in a bid to topple Infantino and “paralyse Fifa”.

They are considering staging their own international competitions if he insists on remaining in power and seeks re-election in March.

Uefa already has a blueprint for a global Nations League, which would rival the World Cup, after it was initially commissioned in 2017.



Infantino’s furious opponents have also made plans to boycott Fifa council and committee meetings, as well as refusing to ratify decisions.

The lawyer has only notched 15 declarations of support from the 211 member nations since his botched project was revealed.

And The FA joined their Welsh counterparts in withdrawing their backing ahead of next year’s presidential election.

A scathing statement from the FAW read: “The recent failures in good governance, processes, leadership, values, stakeholder management, communications and sound judgement have led us to a position where Mr Infantino has lost the confidence of the FAW to remain at the helm of world football.



“Failing to put the best interests of football first is a failure we cannot accept.”

Uefa announced England and all other member nations would sensationally BOYCOTT the World Cup if Infantino’s proposal got the green light.

European football’s governing body is also considering legal action in the fallout.

Infantino, Joshua Kushner, Greg Maffei, JP Morgan and OpenEconomic received letters from Uefa last Friday.

They were warned not to ditch any material relating to the World Cup sell-off.

Sports.title: Alexander Isak had his ego bruised by Liverpool team-mate during ‘disaster’ season, says club icon
Sports.content:
LIVERPOOL star Alexander Isak had his ego bruised by Hugo Ekitike becoming a fan favourite last season.

That is according to Reds legend Jason McAteer, who labelled the Swede’s first year on Merseyside a “disaster”.



The striker’s debut campaign, following his £130million British record move from Newcastle, was derailed by a broken leg in December.

But McAteer also believes fellow forward Ekitike becoming a hit with the fans while Isak was out injured added to his woes.



The former Reds winger said: “He (Isak) thrives on confidence.

“His career at Liverpool has been very much stop and start. He had a terrible beginning with the whole Newcastle saga, which weighed heavy on him.

“It was handled terribly by everybody and in this situation it came out the worst for the player.

“Obviously, later on he broke his leg which is never great and Ekitike quickly became a fan favourite, which affected his ego.

“How the new manager is going to handle the Isak and Ekitike debate is going to be interesting. We will have to see how that pans out.

“He has two good players he will have to choose from which is a nice problem, but Isak needs a good pre-season.

“New manager, new playing style now and it will help him, because last season was a disaster for Isak.

“Now, he gets to press the reset button and can start fresh.”

Ekitike is set to be out at least until the turn of the year after rupturing his Achilles in April.

Isak was in action on Sunday night and played the first half as Liverpool lost 4-2 to Leeds in a friendly.



The Reds were two goals to the good at the break thanks to Luke Chambers and Florian Wirtz.

But they crumbled in the second half and Dominic Calvert-Lewin found the net twice, with Brenden Aaronson and Sean Longstaff getting in on the act.

Liverpool boss Andoni Iraola said: “We learn a lot of things.

“Obviously it’s not the result you want but [it was] probably the most useful friendly we played – in a positive way in the first half and in a negative way in the second half. We’ve learned a lot from today.”



Liverpool’s loss to Leeds concludes their pre-season tour of the US and midfielder Dominik Szoboszlai echoed Iraola on the need to learn from Sunday night’s defeat in Chicago.

Sports.title: Inside Xabi Alonso’s Chelsea start, from shining in staff match against youngsters to golf bonding sessions
Sports.content:
AUSTRALIA was probably not top of the list for Xabi Alonso to start his Chelsea revolution.

You could forgive the new Blues boss for not jumping for joy when, having agreed to take over, he was told the other side of the world would be his first port of call after Cobham.



However, where previous Chelsea tours have largely brought scandal and disgruntled coaches – Alonso has looked a picture of calm contentment, away from the dugout at least.

If anything, a trip to Sydney gives a new manager the chance to get under the skin of his players and new colleagues.



That process began even before they took off. The week before the Chelsea circus took off for Australia and Asia, Alonso decided some early bonding was in order.

A staff match was arranged on the pristine pitches of Cobham. Alonso, the staff he had brought with him and a number of others from the first team building at the training ground took some whipper-snappers from the club and, frankly, stuffed them.

To the surprise of no one, the new manager was prolific when it came to teeing up the goals.

There was serious work to do before departure, too. The club sports scientists devised a plan for players, coaches and all levels of club staff to beat jet lag on their flight from Gatwick, via Sri Lanka, down to Sydney.

It involved switching to Australian time as soon as they boarded the flight in Sussex, sleeping as quickly as possible once airborne and disembarking for a stretch at the stopover.

Some were more successful than others, with some of the squad reporting sleeping 10 hours on their first night, though Alonso had not quite shaken the sleepiness a few days in.



SUN VEGAS WELCOME OFFER: GET UP TO £100 BONUS

Similar plans would have been in place ahead of boarding their chartered Airbus A340 for a near ten hour flight from Sydney to Hong Kong.

Despite any lingering jet lag, the Spaniard managed a swift couple of scenic 10 kilometre runs from their base, the W Hotel in Darling Harbour. The World Cup winner remains in remarkable shape and manages to tick along at a commendable four minutes, 30 seconds a kilometre at 44-years-old.

There was more bonding, for both players and staff, too. Alonso, a keen golfer, managed to fit in a round with club staff in order to get some precious one-on-one time with figures he is still new to working with.

Players visited a yet-to-open swimming pool in the shadow of the Sydney Harbour Bridge, while a few headed to the scenic Ice Bergs club overlooking Bondi Beach.



Younger players, with some as young as 16 on the trip, were encouraged to get out and see the sights, keeping busy to avoid staying shut away in rooms for as long as possible.

Some were joined by family. Mahdi Nicoll-Jazuli, the England youth midfielder born in Sydney and a favourite topic of the local press, was joined by his mother and younger brother, who was allowed to take in training at the Allianz Stadium.

It was not all nicey-nice getting to know you jaunts Down Under, however. Alonso worked them hard and, despite many being impressed with his ice-cool demeanor, his deep frustration following a 2-1 defeat to Tottenham did not go unnoticed.

Alonso had been upset that a number of ideas worked on ahead of the game had not been replicated against their London rivals, while few were happy that they ended up facing ten men after Kevin Danso’s red card.

Players responded well to training. Balls were involved in warm-ups at the start of sessions while many noted that there was less focus on rigid patterns of play, a welcome change from previous managers.



Chelsea used Sydney FC’s Sky Park as their base for the week in Australia, where cockatoos and kookaburras made a racket as they observed from eucalyptus trees dotted around the site in northern Sydney.

Senior staff from both clubs met over coffee to exchange ideas while Alonso also got the chance to pick the brains of Wallabbies head coach Les Kis ahead of their first training session in the city.

Rugby Australia’s offices are based next to the Allianz Stadium, where Chelsea trained in front of more than 5,000 local supporters, and the Blues boss did not need telling who Kis was – already an admirer of his work.

As always with Chelsea, there was news no one was expecting – with a £10million FA fine for dodgy dealings under the previous ownership finally confirmed and the surprise return of Mykhailo Mudryk from his doping ban.

Sports.title: Dad of huge British pop star launches Fulham’s new away kit as fans say ‘that is absolutely beautiful’
Sports.content:
LILY ALLEN’S dad has pulled off a kit launch for the ages after producing, starring and narrating Fulham’s spine-tingling new campaign film.

Actor Keith Allen took centre stage as the Cottagers unveiled their new away strip for the 2026-27 season.



The new shirt reimagined one of the club’s most popular designs, bringing back the iconic black-and-red chequerboard pattern first worn in the mid-1990s.

Allen – who is also the dad of Game of Thrones star Alfie – was the creative force behind the campaign.



The whole thing paid tribute to Fulham’s rich history as they blended the 70s love with 90s soul in a love letter to the club’s travelling supporters.

Set in a dramatic red-and-black world, the film celebrated the fans who follow Fulham home and away.

Allen’s narration pays tribute to “the early starts, the long miles and the commitment to follow Fulham”.

The retro feel continued with the return of the classic ‘FFC’ crest – first seen on four Fulham kits during the 1970s.



For long-time supporters, it is a nod to the side that reached the 1975 FA Cup final, one of the club’s most memorable campaigns.

As eager fans rushed online to comment on their side’s new kit, one X user wrote: “A genuine ten out of ten.”

Someone else said: “Red and black checkered kit goes hard ngl.”

The film also features first-team stars Tom Cairney, Calvin Bassey, Ryan Sessegnon and Rodrigo Muniz, alongside Fulham Women’s players Stella Gandee Morgan, Olivia Dale and Anna Grey.

Liverpool are said to be in advanced talks to open permanent retail stores in the United States. No Premier League club has yet to launch any physical shops Stateside, with Manchester City coming closest, but only previously running pop-ups.

‌



Paris Saint-Germain are the pioneers in this regard across European football, opening their first store in Los Angeles five years ago and have since opened two more in Miami and New York City. The latter is their largest outside of France.

Liverpool have launched stores in Bali and London in recent months, with existing outlets already operating in Denmark, Hong Kong, Indonesia, Ireland, Singapore, South Africa and the United Kingdom.
