In the 2018-19 season, Como were in Serie D, the fourth tier of Italian football, after going bankrupt twice in the previous 15 years. Last season, the small northern Italian club finished fourth after an extraordinary campaign, producing a series of outstanding performances that surprised the football world.

Sports.title: Football Daily | Scrapped proposals, statement wars and the ongoing Infantino furore
Sports.content:
ANOTHER LONG WEEKEND

Here we go again. And, no, we are not talking about the start of the new Scottish Premiership season or the preliminary round of the Carabao Cup – although that Tranmere v Rochdale shootout was a cracker. Yes, after a week of talk about money, greed and Donald Trump’s son-in-law’s brother, the hot topic around the water cooler on Monday was again Gianni Infantino and, more specifically, the English and Welsh FAs’ decisions to row back on their support of a stalling ship. Along with Finland, they’re the first of Uefa’s 55 members to withdraw their letters of support for next year’s Fifa overlord elections.

By the time Football Daily hits your inboxes, there could be a flurry of other nations frantically clicking unsend on those endorsement emails – more than 200 had their flags planted on Terra Gianni just a matter of weeks ago. This U-turn has us harking back to the hazy days of the €uropean $uper £eague, when the Premier League’s super-elite turned their backs on the super-project one by one. Instead of a handful of club statements and Petr Cech trying to calm protestors on Kings Road, now we could be looking at hundreds of withdrawals from federations across the world. Who will go next? Norway? Japan? Would Gianni pick up the phone to the Oval Office if US Soccer decides enough is enough, maybe to try and get it to reverse the decision? Or at least suspend it until next year.

Either way, the threat of a World Cup boycott is over – for now – after Fifa scrapped its proposal to sell stakes in its tournaments to private investors in the early hours of Saturday morning. It was half past midnight in the UK when a statement “attributable to the Fifa president” appeared on its website. That followed a statement called “Clarifications on Fifa Forward Enterprise (FFE)” at 4am the night before that doubled down on the plans. It’s not exactly reassuring that such major dealings and decisions are being pondered, seemingly by one man, in the dead of night – but then again, these could be learned behaviours after all.

Statement wars continued with Uefa’s response on Saturday morning, which read: “We cannot keep going on like this with secret schemes on fast track timescales, cooked up by faceless individuals and of dubious benefit to the game.” That dubious is doing a lot of work there. Uefa added: “The current Fifa leadership has not only lost Uefa’s confidence, but also that of many other members of the football family.” The first member of the football family out of the traps on Monday morning – once it had given the Cymru Premier’s opening weekend time in the spotlight – was the Welsh FA. It withdrew that precious letter of support for Gianni and proclaimed: “Failing to put the best interests of football first is a failure we cannot accept.” Football Daily waits with bated breath to find out what the next statement will say. The Premier League, after all, is still three weeks away.

RECOMMENDED LOOKING

It’s the 50th anniversary of the first ever Panenka penalty so here is a labour of love/splendid piece of work remembering 50 of the most famous – and infamous – attempts at the Czech’s chip since 1976.

View image in fullscreen The classic. Photograph: Colorsport/Shutterstock

QUOTE OF THE DAY

“Some worried about health problems or being unable to attend because of bad weather, as well as people who frequently travel for work. They are terrified and all asking the same question: will our season tickets be taken away?” – La Provincia, Como’s local paper, says it has received dozens of calls and emails from concerned supporters after the club said it will revoke season tickets from fans who fail to attend four home matches, under a series of new rules.

double quotation mark I write to you with my deep regret on hearing about the death of the heroic and granite-made Franco Baresi. Two moments stand out to me, both off the pitch, and show what a great man he was. The first was when Arrigo Sacchi, the Milan manager, dropped his intensity in training, fearing he was overworking the players; Baresi convinced Sacchi to up it instead for the sake of the team, with spectacular results. The second was an older Baresi reflecting on his 1994 World Cup final loss to Brazil, which he appeared in 25 days after knee surgery. Rather than lamenting his lot, having missed a penalty and lost the final, Baresi instead recalled watching the 1970 final between Italy and Brazil, only the second game he had seen on TV. The first game was the West Germany v Italy semi-final, where he recalled watching the players who ‘to me, they were Martians’. He said: ‘I would never have thought 24 years later, at 34 years old, I would have the possibility to play in that same game, the final, against Brazil, the same team. It was a dream that came true.’ Rest in peace” – Nick Kinsella.

double quotation mark I was wondering if Gianni Infantino might revist his Big Sale Opportunity by allowing smaller, club-level contestants from less lucrative leagues to participate in a seriously revamped World Cup, replacing their boycotting national sides. For instance, from the lower leagues of Scottish competitions. Mainly to render possible the wonderful hypothetical headline result of the last match of the (?) 2038 edition: Fifa Forward Final fiasco … East Fife 4, Forfar 5” – Russell Richardson.

double quotation mark Steve Bennett’s comment on Newcastle United’s new kit (Friday’s Football Daily letters) made me think of West Bromwich Albion’s similarly ‘bar-coded’ Premier League strip from the 2020-21 season, at the end of which they were relegated. Newcastle may have to hope that isn’t an omen” – Derrick Cameron.

If you have any, please send letters to the.boss@theguardian.com. Today’s prizeless letter o’ the day goes to … Russell Richardson. Terms and conditions for our competitions, when we run them, are here.

Sports.title: Mauricio Pochettino agrees deal to stay as US coach through World Cup 2030
Sports.content:
US men’s national team head coach Mauricio Pochettino and the US Soccer Federation have agreed to a contract extension that will keep Pochettino attached to the program through 2030, US Soccer announced on Monday.

The two sides had been actively engaged in discussions on a contract extension for several months, long before the USMNT’s disappointing, last-16 exit in this summer’s World Cup, with the federation making it clear it desired Pochettino to stay. Conversations picked up in the weeks following the World Cup, with the Guardian reporting last week that the sides had been in the “final stages” of agreeing to a deal. Financial details of the contract extension were not released, but Pochettino is expected to get a raise on top of the $6m per year he earned under his previous deal with the federation – already the largest outlay for a US head coach.

The Guardian understands that billionaire hedge fund manager Ken Griffin, who bankrolled US Soccer’s initial contract with Pochettino, will once again be the primary funder for the new deal. A source familiar with the agreement characterized Pochettino’s return as being in an “expanded role.” Another source said the primary focus of Pochettino and his staff will be on the senior US team, while the federation’s announcement said that the coaching staff will “advise and support” the federation on “the broader development of the full national team pathway, youth soccer, coaching education, professional league collaboration and other technical facets across the soccer community.”

“It has become clear to us that there is tremendous potential to make the men’s national team program even stronger,” Pochettino said in US Soccer’s announcement. “The passion we experienced from the fans throughout the World Cup only strengthened our belief in what is possible here. We are excited by the opportunity to bring all our experience and knowledge to even more areas of U.S. Soccer while helping strengthen the pathways for players, coaches and teams across the Federation.”

Under Pochettino, the US’s World Cup got off to a bright start and featured arguably the program’s best-ever performance at the tournament, a comprehensive, 4-1 dismantling of Paraguay in their group-stage opener. Strong efforts against Australia and Bosnia and Herzegovina followed, setting the stage for the last-16 encounter with Belgium. The US were outclassed in every way in that match, with Pochettino – along with many players – taking the brunt of the blame for the loss.

View image in fullscreen Mauricio Pochettino’s US team put forth strong performances before crashing out of the World Cup against Belgium. Photograph: Julio Cortez/AP

Pochettino is widely liked by players and staff, with some crediting the coach for overhauling the group’s mentality. He clashed with some players who he felt weren’t fully committed, most notably Milan midfielder Christian Pulisic, going as far as to air his grievances publicly. His relationship with the media also came under scrutiny in his tenure, the result of a handful of dust-ups with reporters and journalists who cover the team regularly.

After the USMNT’s crashout against Belgium, Pochettino expressed pride in the work his staff had done with players. He had been at the helm for about 20 months at that point, and Pochettino suggested that the truncated tenure had only been enough to evaluate the group properly and put standards and practices in place.

“With good things and not so good things,” Pochettino told the Guardian after the Belgium loss, “it was amazing, this journey. It still hasn’t been two years working here. And we all know that a process is about a four-year cycle. Today I think we closed the chapter about assessing players, playing in that competition that is so difficult. I think now we have a complete assessment from a lot of players, and if we commit to be here in the future, we have a clear idea of our decisions for the future – before, it was very difficult.”

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Twice weekly Sign up to Soccer Desk Jonathan Wilson and Guardian journalists bring expert analysis and reporting on the biggest stories in soccer. Preview latest Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

During his time with the US, Pochettino has put together a respectable record of 18 wins, 12 losses and one draw. His early struggles included a fourth-place finish in the 2025 Nations League and a loss to Mexico in the final of the Gold Cup, a tournament he navigated with a heavily rotated squad. He did have his highlights – the electrifying start to this summer’s World Cup, and a 5-1 thrashing of Uruguay in a friendly that ranks as one of the program’s most surprising results.

Still, Pochettino was largely hired to do one job: advance the US past the last 16 and into the quarter-finals at a home World Cup. He did not manage to do so, but the federation has now offered him another chance to hit that goal in 2030.

Sports.title: Emma Raducanu is OUT of the US Open: British tennis star's horror run of injuries continues as doctors advise former champion to skip New York - hours after releasing video training in protective boot
Sports.content:
Emma Raducanu is OUT of the US Open: British tennis star's horror run of injuries continues as doctors advise former champion to skip New York - hours after releasing video training in protective boot

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

Emma Raducanu will miss the US Open as she continues to recover from the stress fracture which forced her to pull out of Wimbledon on the eve of the Championships.

It is a continuation of the British No1's dreadful run of injury and illness and - given the Open is the final Grand Slam of the year - her season is in danger of petering out.

The 23-year-old has been in St Moritz, Switzerland, from where she posted a video of herself practicing serves - with the significant caveat that she was still wearing a protective boot on her right leg.

And Daily Mail Sport understands that after her latest medical checks, the British No1 has been advised that the injury needs more time to heal and so she will be unable to contest the final Grand Slam of the season.

This latest issue is a continuation of a theme - since she won the US Open Raducanu has rarely been able to stay fit for a sustained period.

The lower-leg stress fracture - which first came to light when she was spotted leaving the All England Club in a protective boot in the week before Wimbledon - came on the back of a viral illness which laid her low for much of February through until May.

Emma Raducanu is set to miss the US Open later this month as her injury woes continue

The British No 1 had earlier shared a photo of her practicing in an orthopedic boot on Monday

Raducanu has been spending some of her rehab time in the high luxury of the Suvretta House hotel.

Opened in 1912 in the mountains of St Moritz, rooms can cost up to £2,500 a night.

The five-star hotel has a picturesque clay tennis court - upon which, it appears, Raducanu was unable to do much more than serving off one leg.

British tennis fans who follow and support Raducanu are used to disappointment but this recent run of illness and injury is particularly maddening given how well she has played during her brief periods of health.

In Cluj, Romania, and at the Queen's Club this year she made her first finals since the US Open title in 2021.

And her promising reunion with Andrew Richardson, the man who coached her to that miraculous Grand Slam title, is stuck in the starting blocks.

As ever, Raducanu's talent and athletic ability mean she is still capable of great things if she can stay fit. The problem is, with each passing year that 'if' becomes ever bigger.

Sports.title: Why Vinicius Junior IS worth the risk and the money for Arsenal: Better defensive numbers than you would think, how he would fit into Mikel Arteta's system and the link to Bruno Guimaraes signing
Sports.content:
It seems a bit silly, on the face of it, to even question why Mikel Arteta might want to sign one of the best players in the world.

Why wouldn’t he be keen to bring Real Madrid superstar Vinicius Jr to the Emirates Stadium in one of the biggest blockbuster moves in Premier League history – and especially when the Brazilian would fix the biggest flaw in Arsenal’s lop-sided attack?

It’s no secret that Arsenal relied far too much on its right flank last season, depended far too much on Bukayo Saka to conjure up some magic and, if that didn’t work, fell back on set-pieces to make up for it, while on the other wing Leandro Trossard and Gabriel Martinelli never lacked in endeavour and industry but fell woefully short in output.

Arsenal ended the season as champions so perhaps we cannot complain too much but if Arteta wants to keep the Gunners on top of the mountain, and scale the one that has a Champions League trophy at its summit, he knows he needs to find a way to tip the scales back the other way.

Mikel Arteta is said to be highly enamoured with Vinicius Jr, but it will take a mammoth financial package to sign the Real Madrid man

Arteta knows Arsenal need an elite forward to go one step further and finally lift the European Cup for the first time in the club's 140-year history

Vinicius Jr would do that, and then some. The winger is one of the most dangerous ball carriers in world football. Even among the most elite dribblers across Europe’s Big Five Leagues, he stands alongside Barcelona sensation and World Cup winner Lamine Yamal as the very best.

Whenever he gets the ball at his feet, Vinicius Jr drives towards the box and either gets a shot away or, if you think you’ve closed the angle off, slips in his team-mate to get off one of their own.

No player created more chances after carrying the ball five metres or more across the Big Five Leagues last season than Vinicius Jr. The 49 shots he took himself after such carries was just one behind leader Yamal.

ALL COMPETITIONS, 2025-26 Player Games Goals Assists Total Vinicius Jr 53 22 14 36 Bukayo Saka 49 11 9 20 Leandro Trossard 50 8 11 19 Gabriel Martinelli 53 11 7 18 Noni Madueke 43 8 4 12

Saka is, by some distance, Arsenal’s best with the ball at his feet, but even his numbers are dwarfed by the staggering figures for Vinicius.

Trossard and Martinelli mustered just 19 shot-ending carries and 18 chance-ending ones between them.

Just a quick look at Vinicius Jr’s decisive carries shows how relentless and devastating he was at getting the ball, driving into the box and making things happen. Arsenal need more of those if they are to break down deep defences that often caused them problems last term.

No player created more chances after carrying the ball five metres or more across the Big Five Leagues last season than Vinicius Jr

He has scored in, and won, two Champions League finals in the last five seasons for Real Madrid

And yet, for all that brilliance, it’s impossible not to ignore that lingering doubt about whether he really is the right fit for Arsenal. Or, more specifically, for Arteta.

Spanish media outlet AS claimed that Arteta, in his bid to coax Vinicius Jr to north London, has promised to build his team around the Brazilian. Only, that goes against everything that has brought Arsenal glory under him.

So much of Arsenal’s success comes from their press and their teamwork in applying it together. They defend as a unit with everyone playing their part. If one part of the press doesn’t do its job, they are easy to play through.

As part of Daily Mail Sport’s analysis of why Arteta was so keen to sign Morgan Rogers, before they were gazumped by their rivals in blue down the road to the tune of £117million, we showed how a huge part of the allure in signing him was the defensive work Rogers did alongside his ability with the ball at his feet.

Not only did Rogers rank alongside Saka for joint-third most shot-ending carries in league last season but he also sat behind only the Arsenal winger for the most times any player won possession in the final third.

Even though his goals and assists were poor, no player with more than 500 minutes of league action averaged more ball recoveries in the final third than Martinelli.

Arteta wants his front line to be as busy without the ball as with it. You don’t get that with Vinicius Jr. Such demands have rarely been placed on him at Real Madrid either. Quite the opposite, in fact, where he has often been allowed to shirk those duties and focus on getting the most out of his devastating attacking qualities.

He wanders about the pitch, waiting for his colleagues to win the ball, then springs into action on the counter-attack. His perceived lack of effort saw Real fans turn on him frequently last season. ‘Work rate zero, tantrums 100’, was one cutting verdict after a shock home defeat to Getafe in which he preferred to gesture to the Bernabeu crowd instead of tracking back.

Vinicius showed his X factor at the World Cup, scoring four times in five matches

But for all his attacking prowess, Vinicius will be expected to do more defensively if he joins Arsenal

He won’t get such a free rein from Arteta, or the fans. If he does join – he returned to Real Madrid for pre-season training today – he will be expected to do his bit.

He’ll certainly have to do more than what he does already. Vinicius Jr won possession during matches far less than Saka, Martinelli or Trossard last term and nearly half as much in the final third as compatriot Martinelli.

DEFENSIVE DUTIES League games, 2025-26 Possession won Won in final third Duels won Bukayo Saka 4.7 1.1 6.8 Gabriel Martinelli 4.4 1.3 4.6 Vinicius Jr 2.8 0.7 6.3 Noni Madueke 2.6 0.7 5.6 Viktor Gyokeres 2.2 0.8 3.0 Kai Havertz 2.2 0.5 5.6

For all the grumbles, though, his numbers suggest there is room for improvement. He won possession high up the pitch about as often as Madueke. He won more duels – something Arteta values very highly – than all Arsenal forwards bar Saka.

His ball-winning figures from last term bettered those of Arsenal striker Viktor Gyokeres so, if Arteta is to build his team around him, then perhaps that opens up the possibility of Vinicius Jr playing up front, as he did frequently for Real and Brazil, especially in matches where Arteta wants to exploit space in behind.

Vinicius Jr did so in the Champions League last 16 second leg against Manchester City. Pep Guardiola’s side were 4-0 down on aggregate and chasing the game, leaving Vinicius Jr – playing as the central striker – the chance to break away as he did below. Despite scoring twice in the game, he raced through only to blaze his chance over the bar.

Vinicius bursts clear of the Manchester City defence, demonstrating how he could play as a central striker for Arteta

If Arteta is to make an exception on the pitch, he’ll have to make one off it too. It’s just that maybe, at the end of it all, he just thinks Vinicius is worth it

Arteta wants his team to play more of those passes to find more of those runs, and the potential arrival of Bruno Guimaraes from Newcastle would help unlock that.

That’s a definite option but that would still not fix the left-sided problem. Perhaps Arteta is willing to make a compromise: Know that Vinicius Jr won’t work as hard as Trossard or Martinelli but will more than make up for it with the weight of goals, assists and star power. If Arteta allows him to stay high up the pitch, it not only gives Arsenal the ideal out ball for a quick counter but will likely petrify opponents into leaving a player back to stop it.

Arteta maybe feels as though he has the players around Vinicius Jr to pick up the dirty work if left to do his thing. Again, if they land Guimaraes, his all-round, all-action ability would allow Arsenal's left-sided central midfielder, usually Declan Rice, to take on more of a clean-up role once Arsenal lose the ball.

Myles Lewis-Skelly would have the legs to cover the extra ground and the defensive nous that came from his time as a left-back. It might just mean Arsenal’s actual left-back, whether that be Riccardo Calafiori or Piero Hincapie, might have to resist any urges to bomb forward on the overlap.

Vinicius Jr’s arrival would also shatter Arsenal’s balanced wage structure. He’s a superstar that would come with a superstar salary. If Arteta is to make an exception on the pitch, he’ll have to make one off it too. It’s just that maybe, at the end of it all, he just thinks he’s worth it.

Sports.title: Newcastle REJECT Arsenal bid for Bruno Guimaraes as he joins team-mates in La Manga, Chelsea agree £26m deal to sell Trevoh Chalobah to Como... and Preston skipper is set for controversial £3m exit to Wrexham: WINDOW WATCH
Sports.content:
Newcastle REJECT Arsenal bid for Bruno Guimaraes as he joins team-mates in La Manga, Chelsea agree £26m deal to sell Trevoh Chalobah to Como... and Preston skipper is set for controversial £3m exit to Wrexham: WINDOW WATCH

It's that time of the year again – the transfer window is now open until September 1 and it's sure to be a busy period with clubs looking to make big signings ahead of next season.

Here are today's latest developments from Simon Jones and the Daily Mail Sport team...

Preston boss hits out with Whiteman set for exit to Wrexham

Preston North End have accepted a £3million bid from Wrexham for their wantaway captain Ben Whiteman.

Manager Paul Heckingbottom voiced his displeasure at the weekend, saying Whiteman had crossed a line after telling them he had played his last game for the club in an effort to force through the move.

'Ben knew there was a line I didn't want him to cross and unfortunately he has,' Heckingbottom told BBC Radio Lancashire. 'There's a valuation on him, I just hope for Ben's sake that Wrexham are willing to pay it otherwise he's put himself in a sticky situation. He's made his bed. I'm not bothered as long as I get another player.'

The 30-year-old midfielder is now free to have a medical and complete the transfer, with personal terms not expected to be a problem.

The deal is expected to go through in the next 48 hours and Preston are looking to reinvest the money in another three or four new signings this summer.

Paul Heckingbottom says Ben Whiteman has 'crossed a line' in making his move

Hammers plot £18m bid to land Parrott

West Ham are preparing to outbid European rivals to sign former Tottenham striker Troy Parrott.

The Hammers want to bolster their attack quickly with the new Championship season looming and after being rebuffed for Sunderland's Wilson Isidor, are targeting AZ Alkmaar forward Parrott.

The Republic of Ireland international has interest from Ajax, Como, PSV Eindhoven and Real Betis but Alkmaar are reluctant to sell to a Dutch rival.

The Hammers hope an offer of around £18million will be enough to fend off the competition.

Parrott struggled while at Spurs but after an initial loan to Excelsior Rotterdam he began to find his feet and has been prolific with Alkmaar since.

Read more on this story HERE

Troy Parrott celebrates winning the Johan Cruyff Shield with Alkmaar on Sunday

Henderson's relish as he joins Chelsea

Chelsea have announced the signing of 36-year-old Jordan Henderson, after he was allowed to leave Brentford with a year left on his deal.

‘Given the size of the club, the manager, who I have great admiration for, and the quality of the players, this was a huge opportunity I couldn’t turn down,’ Henderson said.

‘I was also so impressed with how much the ownership want Chelsea to be successful and move in the right direction.

For more on this story click HERE

Jordan Henderson signs on the dotted line as he joins Xabi Alonso's Chelsea revolution

Sunderland block the door to Isidor

West Ham have asked to take Sunderland winger Simon Adingra on loan, but the Wearsiders have no plans to sell forward Wilson Isidor.

West Ham have asked about both players but after initial conversations Sunderland have made it clear that they want to keep Haiti international Isidor.

Discussions are ongoing between the clubs over a straight loan for 24-year-old Ivory Coast international Adingra.

Despite interest from a host of clubs, however, Sunderland will not entertain offers for Isidor. The 25-year-old remains an integral part of their squad ahead of their season in European competition and the club believe he can build on an excellent World Cup with Haiti.

West Ham are continuing to discuss AZ Alkmaar striker Troy Parrott while Lazio are interested in the Hammers' German international forward Niclas Fullkrug.

Wilson Isidor is back after the World Cup and Sunderland say he is not for sale despite interest

Como agree £26m Chalobah deal... as Napoli eye Badiashile

Chelsea and Como have agreed a £26million fee for defender Trevoh Chalobah.

The deal will include a further £5.2m in add-ons for the 27-year-old England centre-back who is expected to travel to Italy on Wednesday evening.

Chelsea defender Benoit Badiashile continues to attract interest from Napoli. The Blues are looking to recoup funds for the French centre-back as well as for Axel Disasi who has been the subject of talks with Crystal Palace and West Ham - both are discussing offers.

Disasi had a spell on loan at West Ham last season but ideally wants a top flight offer.

Chelsea hope to make progress with Rayo Vallecano over the purchase of left wing-back Pep Chavarria.

Trevoh Chalobah is on his way to Como, managed by former Blues star Cesc Fabregas

Newcastle reject Arsenal bid for Bruno as he joins Magpies in La Manga

Arsenal's opening bid for Bruno Guimaraes has been rejected by Newcastle. As reported earlier, the clubs are now in direct talks over a deal for Brazilian.

Guimaraes has landed in Spain and is travelling to report back for Newcastle’s pre-season camp in La Manga today.

Newcastle's new manager Matthias Jaissle is at La Manga with the squad and wants to meet the captain.

Bruno Guimaraes is subject of interest from Arsenal but they have not yet made a formal offer

Bernardo gets shirty at Real

Bernardo Silva has arrived at Real Madrid as he joins up with Jose Mourinho's side. The 31-year-old left Manchester City at the end of last season.

The Portugal star, who has returned from the World Cup, was seen signing shirts for fans after medical tests.

🚨 Bernardo Silva continue de signer quelques maillots avant de quitter Sanitas.



🎥 @ainoafrndz pic.twitter.com/7wFAeRQm2F — Le Journal du Real (@lejournaldureal) August 3, 2026

Man United would loan out Chido Obi for game time

Manchester United are willing to send striker Chido Obi Martin out on loan this summer.

The 18-year-old Denmark U21 international had interest from Cologne earlier in the window, but they have moved to sign Jaiden Heskey from Manchester City and are lining up Tottenham winger Mikey Moore.

Chido Obi joined United from Arsenal's academy in 2024 and has made seven first-team appearances though failed to score.

United want to ensure his next club is one where he can develop properly with competitive game time.

Join the queue for Everton's Tim

Everton midfielder Tim Iroegbunam is attracting increasing interest from rival Premier League clubs and from abroad.

Coventry City, Hull City and Ipswich Town have all made enquiries while two Italian clubs have also asked about the 23-year-old.

Lazio tried to sign the former England U20 international in January.

Everton are continuing to discuss a deal for Arsenal's Christian Norgaard which, if completed, could pave the way for Iroegbunam to depart once a suitable offer comes in.

Everton paid around £9million to Aston Villa for Iroegbunam in 2024.

Tim Iroegbunam joined from Aston Villa two years ago

Coventry keen on Mudryk

Chelsea have received multiple approaches about Mykhailo Mudryk from clubs following the news of his return to football – including three from the Premier League.

Coventry City, managed by Frank Lampard, who worked with Mudryk at Stamford Bridge in 2023, are believed to be among those to have enquired, sources have told Daily Mail Sport.

All options are open between Mudryk and Chelsea this summer, including whether to send him out on loan after his sudden comeback from a doping suspension.
