Sports.title: West Ham set to battle clubs across Europe for former Tottenham wonderkid Troy Parrott - as Hammers chase FOUR other signings ahead of Championship promotion push
Sports.content:
West Ham are preparing to outbid European rivals to sign former Tottenham striker Troy Parrott.

The Hammers want to bolster their attack quickly with the new Championship season looming and after being rebuffed for Sunderland's Wilson Isidor, are targeting AZ Alkmaar forward Parrott.

The Republic of Ireland international has interest from Ajax, Como, PSV Eindhoven and Real Betis but Alkmaar are reluctant to sell to a Dutch rival.

The Hammers hope an offer of around £18million will be enough to fend off the competition.

Parrott struggled while at Spurs but after an initial loan to Excelsior Rotterdam he began to find his feet and has been prolific with Alkmaar since.

He has scored 68 goals in 127 games across all competitions during his three seasons in the Netherlands – averaging a goal every 137 minutes. That includes 51 goals in 96 games for AZ in all competitions.

West Ham are preparing to outbid European rivals to sign former Tottenham striker Troy Parrott

Parrott has shone in the Netherlands since leaving Spurs (pictured in 2019) back in 2024

In the league alone he has netted 40 Eredivisie goals in 81 appearances over the past three seasons, placing him among the Dutch top flight's leading scorers during that period.

Last season was his most prolific campaign with 31 goals and 12 assists in 48 appearances – a goal involvement every 86 minutes – including a career-best 16 Eredivisie goals.

He backed that up with five goals in five KNVB Cup matches last season, including in the final, helping AZ lift their first major trophy in 13 years.

Indeed, his 30th goal of the season came in that 5–1 final win over NEC Nijmegen.

AZ have already started the season with intent, winning the Johan Cruyff Shield with a 4-0 victory over reigning champions PSV Eindhoven on Sunday. It was only the second Shield Alkmaar had won in their history.

The 24-year-old Parrott has 37 caps for the Republic of Ireland and has scored six goals across his last three competitive internationals, including both goals in the World Cup qualifying win over Portugal, a hat-trick against Hungary to secure a play-off place, and the opening goal against Czechia.

He would be open to a return to London with West Ham despite them being in the Championship.

The Hammers want another finisher to play alongside Jarrod Bowen.

They expect Niclas Fullkrug to depart with Lazio interested and are working on a loan for winger Simon Adingra from Sunderland.

They will also make an improved bid for midfielder Arne Engels at Celtic.

They would like defender Axel Disasi from Chelsea but he has top flight interest with Crystal Palace ready to bid.

Cardiff defender Dylan Lawlor is also a target.

Sports.title: Inside the Chelsea tour where Xabi Alonso wowed his new players: The new methods stars raved about, an emergency alarm, how squad reacted to Mykhailo Mudryk news, a run club and Australian hosts' cheeky dig at Cole Palmer
Sports.content:
Inside the Chelsea tour where Xabi Alonso wowed his new players: The new methods stars raved about, an emergency alarm, how squad reacted to Mykhailo Mudryk news, a run club and Australian hosts' cheeky dig at Cole Palmer

Unlock more from Kieran Gill inside the Chelsea camp with a DailyMail+ subscription - brilliant exclusives, in-depth insight, analysis and more

Before Chelsea travelled to Sydney, Australia, Xabi Alonso arranged a staff-only game at their Cobham training ground, mixing his new guys who had arrived with him alongside those who already worked within the first-team building.

To save you reading a match report of a seven-a-side kickabout, let’s just say the team featuring Alonso won, because one source says he was providing the assists for their goals, one after another.

Nothing gets a good working culture going like a game of football, and Alonso has clearly still got it, the talent which made him a fine midfielder for Liverpool, Real Madrid, Bayern Munich, Spain and more. By all accounts, the players have loved watching him in training, too.

Levi Colwill told us during one conversation in Sydney how Alonso has been ‘spraying balls around for no reason’ and playing ‘a perfect pass every time’. A few within the Chelsea squad said similar, while adding they have liked how Alonso is not as rigid as other coaches who like to stop the session if they spy a player out of position by a few yards. You can’t pause live matches, after all.

At the beginning of this visit, Colwill and everyone else was advised by Chelsea’s sports science department to essentially act as if they were on Australian time from the moment they left the tarmac in London. Dinner was served shortly after departing, despite their flight leaving in the morning, and then they were told to sleep. The squad stopped at the Bandaranaike International Airport in Katunayake, Sri Lanka for a stretching session halfway through.

Daily Mail Sport stopped off in Singapore, where our connection was cancelled, giving us a spare day to walk the Marina Bay Street Circuit Formula One track. That was tricky, mind. We had packed for an Australian winter; not the humidity of Singapore.

Xabi Alonso's training sessions have gone down well with his new Chelsea charges

And the Spaniard, donning a pair of adidas Predators, has not been afraid to join in training

The squad at Sydney Harbour Bridge, close to their five-star hotel

It was indeed chilly in Sydney, where Chelsea stayed in the W, a luxurious five-star hotel complete with an infinity pool overlooking the Darling Harbour. Before training at the Allianz Stadium, Les Kiss, the new head coach of the Australia rugby union team, walked by. Alonso knew who he was, too. Chelsea's manager bumped into him and had a good chat before training began.

He might have been getting some good jogging tips from Kiss. There has been a Chelsea running club of sorts between the backroom staff, all meeting in the lobby of their swish hotel before pounding the pavements. Alonso likes to try to do 10 kilometres three times a week, aiming for four minutes and 30 seconds per kilometre. He kept this up – and managed to get in the odd round of golf in Sydney – despite struggling with jet-lag throughout the trip.

Chelsea's open training session at the Allianz Stadium was watched by 5,289 fans, several of whom were wearing Kairat FC shirts and holding Kazakhstan flags for Chelsea’s 17-year-old newbie Dastan Satpayev. The teenager was technically an ‘international trialist’ on this tour, as his transfer from the Kazakh champions will not go through until he turns 18 on August 12. That required Chelsea receiving permission from Kairat and his parents.

There were fans for every player over here. We even saw one lad with a cardboard cutout of Liam Delap’s face. Another had a sign which read: ‘Robert Sanchez could have saved the Titanic.’

Fitness coach Ismael Camenforte Lopez led the drills, shouting instructions at the squad. Alonso occasionally chipped in, like when he told Romeo Lavia to check his surroundings when the Belgian midfielder met one cross which he should have left for a team-mate behind him. There were a few wayward balls during a crossing drill.

Then Alonso won one almighty cheer from the crowd. As Camenforte Lopez blew his whistle to signal the session’s end, Alonso smashed a ball bouncing towards him on the half-volley and into the goal from 25 yards, much to the delight of the supporters. Like we said: he's still got it.

Willie Isa, Chelsea’s hire from rugby league who tries to improve the squad mentality, was a fan favourite, too. He was signing autographs and taking selfies with our rugby-mad Aussie crowd, and was heard telling the supporters that they can expect a better season while doing so.

In other sessions, Chelsea’s squad was split into two for a big passing exercise. Sanchez and Filip Jorgensen were involved in those – Alonso wants his team playing from the back – while the younger goalkeepers Ted Curd and Teddy Sharman-Lowe practised catching crosses with coach Ben Roberts. Jorgensen was only here in Sydney for a few days before being sent home because he was closing in on leaving the club. Long old way to travel for a couple of sessions.

Dastan Satpayev impressed on tour, though he was officially down as 'international triallist' as his transfer from Kairat does not go through until he turns 18 on August 12

Alonso guides Moises Caicedo through a training session at Sky Park in Sydney

Youngsters Aaron Anselmino, Estevao Willian and Mahdi Nicoll-Jazuli battle it out

On their first Monday in Sydney, Chelsea's players and staff were at Sky Park, the training ground for Sydney FC on a university campus. The local club were a little cheeky. Their WiFi password was ‘Football Is Coming Home’ with some numbers replacing letters. It was written on a big whiteboard, right next to where we spoke with Colwill and Cole Palmer, neither of whom made it into England's World Cup squad.

At 2pm that day, everybody’s mobile phones started going haywire, simultaneously letting off deafening sirens. The Australian Government had sent us all a test message of their new emergency warning system.

One of Chelsea’s staff members was on a pre-season tour for the first time with the club, and so tradition called for an initiation song. Mercifully it was not for performing in front of the players – just some of the internal staff. I Want It That Way by Backstreet Boys was the choice.

When we spoke with Palmer he was on fine form, joking that he was going to get the bailiffs to Morgan Rogers’ door if his new team-mate and close friend dared use his ‘cold’ celebration next season.

Apparently Palmer actually asked Chelsea to choose him for that presser. Maybe he had seen others getting picked before him and fancied chatting about his best pal, Rogers. It did make a difference as he was indeed in a good mood, and hopefully he has a more enjoyable season in 2026-27.

The vibes inside the Chelsea camp were positive. Mind you, I did wince when I saw Estevao Willian hop on for a piggyback from Wesley Fofana, fearing a pre-season injury to Chelsea’s defender.

Chelsea had a fair few academy youngsters with them on this trip. Among them, 16-year-olds Reggie Watson and Mahdi Nicoll-Jazuli. You do not want those kids simply sitting in their rooms, glued to their devices, bored to tears.

So Chelsea helped entertain them, such as by arranging boat trips and the like. The club appreciate that these boys’ parents essentially put their trust in them, and so they wanted to repay that faith.

Cole Palmer was in a distinctly better mood as he tries to put last season - and missing out on England's World Cup squad - behind him

Reggie Watson ran the show against Western Sydney Wanderers despite being just 16 years old

Alonso's Premier League reign is getting ever closer

Meanwhile, the seniors had sponsorship duties to perform. Colwill, Aaron Anselmino and Tosin Adarabioyo headed to Bondi Beach. Palmer, Joao Pedro, Dario Essugo and Delap attended a Q&A at the headquarters of the club’s pre-season tour partner TMGM. They had a games room at the W, where they could compete at table tennis and darts, the usual.

Chelsea owner Behdad Eghbali came to join the tour before the Tottenham match. His team lost that 2-1, but there’s no need to panic. It’s only pre-season and it can happen.

Along with their sporting directorship team, players were asking questions as news broke of Mykhailo Mudryk’s suspension being lifted – what happened, what it means, what happens next. There are many within the club who are delighted for the Ukrainian after nearly two years of not playing any professional football.

Chelsea’s players departed from Sydney International Airport at lunchtime on Sunday, August 2, bound for Hong Kong on a private plane. At the same time, Mudryk and new signing Danny Welbeck were flying from London to link up with the squad. It's now just three weeks until the season opener at Fulham. Alonso's Premier League reign is getting ever closer.

Sports.title: Why Liverpool tour leaves Andoni Iraola with a host of questions: How his No2 stepped in to fix injury crisis, the left-sided problem, two youngsters pushing to start Premier League opener and what's already changed from Arne Slot reign
Sports.content:
Why Liverpool tour leaves Andoni Iraola with a host of questions: How his No2 stepped in to fix injury crisis, the left-sided problem, two youngsters pushing to start Premier League opener and what's already changed from Arne Slot reign

Unlock more from Lewis Steele inside the Liverpool camp with a DailyMail+ subscription - brilliant exclusives, in-depth insight, analysis and more

‘Quicker, quicker, come on,’ bellows Andoni Iraola, wearing a club tracksuit and blowing on a whistle on a lanyard.

The setting is the Endeavor Health Performance Center several miles outside of downtown Chicago, with stunning views of the Windy City. But there is no time to stop and admire the skyline, which boasts the third-tallest building in the country, or the multitude of helicopters buzzing overhead.

For Liverpool and their new head coach, this pre-season tour has been all about hard work, intensity and consequences. Those are the buzzwords of the fortnight and, had we a pound for every time a player talked about ‘intensity’, we would be able to afford to buy the new players that Liverpool desperately still need to give Iraola a platform for success.

The 19-year-old winger Kieran Morrison, a breakout star of the tour and contender for first-team minutes, told us that his ‘legs are finished by 9pm most nights’ after double sessions that include tough gym workouts and heart rate-raising pressing drills.

Last season’s best player Dominik Szoboszlai, whether intentional or not, had an indirect dig at the former regime led by Arne Slot, saying: ‘The intensity we need, it’s here now. What we have been missing, it’s back from the coach's side, from the players’ side as well.’

Fellow Hungarian, left back Milos Kerkez, who has made huge strides tactically and stepped up as a mentor to youngsters this pre-season, told reporters: ‘It's the intensity, he (Iraola) is not scared to play one-on-one all over the pitch, to press high and to be on the front foot always.’

‘Quicker, quicker, come on,’ bellows Andoni Iraola, wearing a club tracksuit and blowing on a whistle on a lanyard

The setting is the Endeavor Health Performance Center several miles outside of downtown Chicago, with stunning views of the Windy City

After training, players have been known to be lying flat on the pitch – think of a tennis player after a five-set thriller at Wimbledon. On afternoons off, they have enjoyed shopping trips around Chicago but also have just put their feet up in the hotel rooftop bar. No Aperol Spritz or fancy cocktails like the fellow patrons of the Park Hyatt Hotel – hot chocolate has been a favourite.

There has been time for games of Uno and cup stacking competitions and, in these regards at least, Mohamed Salah is not missed. He used to be the king of everything, not excluding pre-season pastimes such as ping pong. Szoboszlai has stepped up in that regard.

But Salah’s exit after nine years, 257 goals and seven major trophies has left a gaping hole in the squad, with a leadership vacuum also felt on this trip given the post-World Cup absences of Virgil van Dijk and Alisson. Given that captain Van Dijk played more minutes than anyone last year, the 35-year-old was offered an extended summer break and began his pre-season work back at base in Liverpool instead of living out of a suitcase for two weeks here.

Iraola has still left a lasting impression in training, with relentless pressing drills. There have been modern touches but also old-school punishments. If players are on the losing team in training, they face consequences. Found slacking in one of the exercises? That’ll be a sprint to the other end of the pitch and back, sunshine. Lose out in the small-sided games? Off you go, get running.

There have been some celebrity sightings. Jon Bon Jovi was in the same hotel Liverpool spent an afternoon in New York City, while music artists such as Olivia Dean and Charli XCX were also in town for the Lollapalooza music festival.

Fashion designer Tommy Hilfiger has also taken pictures with staff and some players took a trip to learn about the legendary 1990s Chicago Bulls basketball team and posed for selfies with a Michael Jordan statue. While other team-mates shot hoops, back-up goalkeeper Harvey Davies showed his reaction skills by diving to save a basketball that was careering towards a photographer’s camera at full pelt.

Others visited a sandwich joint where hit show The Bear is set and were saved by a member of the media team pulling some strings after they nearly missed the opening hours. The owner had no idea what ‘soccer’ was, or who these people were outside of his store.

Legendary former Bayern Munich and Barcelona striker Robert Lewandowski was rubbing shoulders with the team at the base of Chicago Fire, which Liverpool trained at for the fortnight at a camp not too dissimilar to what nations did at the World Cup – instead of moving from state to state, they used Chicago as a base and flew in and out of Nashville and New York only for matches – though one flight was cancelled due to a storm.

Liverpool's players took in the training base of the legendary Chicago Bulls team that dominated the 1990s in the NBA

Virgil van Dijk has been beginning his recovery back at Liverpool's home base after his World Cup exploits

Chicago Fire also rented their base to Germany last month and want to showcase why America can be a go-to destination. Club staffers at the Major League Soccer side were gutted to learn Van Dijk was not on tour as they thought they could make an unofficial pitch to sign him in the future by showing him around their state-of-the-art facilities. Van Dijk’s £350,000-a-week contract expires next summer.

Given the absence of some high-profile stars, some teenagers have stepped up. None have impressed more so than young midfielder Trey Nyoni, 19.

Even before the three friendlies, sources spoke about how he was stepping up in training sessions and now there is momentum behind him to start the opening Premier League fixture away at Newcastle on August 23.

Nyoni, who joined from Leicester’s academy as part of Liverpool’s aggressive approach to sign the best young talents in the country, is a deep-lying midfielder who can also play in multiple other positions.

‘Even when he has one opponent quite close, he asks for that ball and he’s confident, he doesn’t rush,’ said Iraola in New York. ‘For me, that is very valuable.’

The breakout star of the last 12 months, Rio Ngumoha, now looks nailed on to start at St James’ Park, where he scored his first senior goal last season to snatch a 3-2 victory at the death. Iraola has tried to convert all his wingers to be able to play on both sides, given they are lopsided with the current crop all preferring to play from the left-hand side – a problem that will increase if they sign top target Bradley Barcola.

New £34.5million signing Victor Munoz, another left-sided winger, will begin pre-season work this week after winning the World Cup with Spain, while Cody Gakpo has been given time off after his partner lost a child during pregnancy in June. Tottenham want to sign Gakpo but the Reds have no desire to sell. But the balance of the wingers is not Iraola’s biggest problem.

That would lie in defence, where the tour started with Joe Gomez limping off injured after eight minutes of the first friendly, a win over Sunderland in Nashville. Liverpool hoped January signing Jeremy Jacquet would be fit by now but they have instead gone careful on the young French defender, who they agreed a deal to sign for £55million in January just before he suffered a shoulder problem with Rennes. He has not played since.

Trey Nyoni has shone on tour and there is now momentum behind him to start the opening Premier League fixture away at Newcastle on August 23

The breakout star of the last 12 months, Rio Ngumoha, now looks nailed on to start at St James’ Park, where he scored his first senior goal last season to snatch a 3-2 victory at the death

Joe Gomez's injury eight minutes into the first tour match has plunged Iraola further into a centre-back crisis

It means Gomez’s eight minutes are the only action of any senior centre-back this tour, with right back also a problem given the long-term injury to Conor Bradley. Jeremie Frimpong had to be substituted in that last friendly but it is not understood to be a serious issue.

Austrian 18-year-old Ifeanyi Ndukwe, 18, has been a class act but does not have a work permit after a move from Austria Vienna and so cannot yet play competitive matches, while versatile defender Luke Chambers has also shown significant promise after spending last season on loan at Charlton.

Chambers, 22, has always impressed staff and appears to be over several lengthy injury setbacks, scoring the opening goal in the final tour match, a 4-2 defeat by Leeds. ‘What a diamond of a boy he is, Liverpool are lucky to have him,’ his former Kilmarnock boss Derek McInnes, now at Rangers, told Daily Mail Sport.

On the youngsters, one source said how the rookies have been taken aback by Iraola’s approach. No player is bigger than another, Iraola will devote as much time to a youngster with zero first-team minutes as star attraction Szoboszlai.

His coaching staff have helped him settle in, with English duo Tommy Elphick and Shaun Cooper well-liked by the group. When trying to eavesdrop on Iraola's on-pitch instructions at training, it was amusing to instead hear Elphick’s south coast accent.

The former Brighton, Aston Villa and Bournemouth defender has even put on a bib and joined in training sessions to make up the numbers amid a crisis at centre-half. Elphick had offers to be a first-team manager in the Championship this season but opted to stick by Iraola as his No2.

Iraola’s predecessor Slot was criticised for giving the squad too many days off last season. Although that theory was categorically not true – they had the same amount of downtime in the season that they won the Premier League – fans will be pleased to learn Iraola is relentless.

Slot’s sacking came as a surprise to many, especially after the club backed him all season, though it was the right decision after a torrid campaign. Van Dijk was not consulted and found out only when landing in Amsterdam for pre-World Cup duty, while Kerkez was woken up from a holiday nap by his shocked brother.

Austrian 18-year-old Ifeanyi Ndukwe, 18, has been a class act but does not have a work permit after a move from Austria Vienna and so cannot yet play competitive matches

Iraola brought assistants Tommy Elphick (left) and Shaun Cooper (right) with him from Bournemouth and they have done a lot of the hands-on coaching so far

Although Iraola laughed off suggestions from his former Bournemouth pupil Antoine Semenyo that he never gives time off, the Basque believes that hard work now will lead to success in the long run.

Some players have worn Whoop armbands that track physical data and new fitness coach Pablo de la Torre – described as much more than just a physical guru – has a big job alongside medical staff to avoid the injury crisis that plagued last year.

Iraola differs from Slot in terms of the amount of video meetings and his teachings are more physical than in a classroom. The new boss does not conduct post-match briefings on matchday and instead talks to the team the following morning.

He would have much to ponder as the squad jetted back across the Atlantic. The tour was broadly positive but had negative notes, not least an on-pitch spat between Szoboszlai and Curtis Jones, who is subject to interest from Italian champions Inter Milan and will be allowed to leave if they pay £35million.

Jones and Szoboszlai were rowing about how the latter gave the captain’s armband to Kostas Tsimikas, after a 1-0 win over Wrexham at Yankee Stadium. The trio were all smiles the next time the cameras were on, with Jones glancing over at photographers in a move that hinted at it being a calculated act, though every suggestion is that the issue has been brushed away.

There is a desperate need for signings. Without a top-class winger to replace Salah and at least one defensive reinforcement, Iraola’s platform for success will be lowered. Further movement with the Barcola deal is expected in the next week.

Opponents bypassed Liverpool’s midfield far too easily last year and a true No6 would stiffen their weak underbelly. Iraola also believes Florian Wirtz and Alexander Isak will be ‘massive’ and last summer’s £241million duo are expected to be better for their struggles in their debut campaigns.

There is also a cloud of uncertainty off the pitch, with Fenway Sports Group chief Michael Edwards quitting his role and sporting director Richard Hughes all but certain to join Al Hilal in Saudi Arabia. Hughes recruited Iraola at both Bournemouth and Liverpool but changes upstairs look likely now.

Curtis Jones (centre) and Dominik Szoboszlai (right) rowed about how the latter gave the captain’s armband to Kostas Tsimikas (left), after a 1-0 win over Wrexham at Yankee Stadium

But Szoboszlai and Jones were all smiles by the next time the cameras were on them

This Stateside trip has seen more positives than negatives and Iraola has been immensely impressive. But there are plenty of questions left to solve

Former Jurgen Klopp ally Mike Gordon was in Chicago and he is back running the show as president of FSG, who are exploring selling a 30 per cent stake for £1.35billion to a consortium led by Amit Bhatia.

The former QPR supremo is trying to get Amazon billionaire Jeff Bezos, the fourth-richest man in the world, on board with the bid, while reports suggest Facebook co-founder Eduardo Saverin is also keen. FSG are open to selling the minority stake which would see money go to the Boston-based owners rather than the club but would have a positive knock-on effect for Liverpool.

It has, though, raised suspicions with fans that the long-term custodians of the club, led by 76-year-old John W Henry, are heading closer to the end of their tenure.

This Stateside trip has seen more positives than negatives and Iraola has been immensely impressive. But there are plenty of questions left to solve before the trip to Tyneside in just three weeks.

Sports.title: Furious UEFA warned Gianni Infantino NOT to destroy botched World Cup plan documents with lawsuit threatened before FIFA president abandoned his plot
Sports.content:
Furious UEFA warned Gianni Infantino NOT to destroy botched World Cup plan documents with lawsuit threatened before FIFA president abandoned his plot

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

UEFA threatened Gianni Infantino with legal action on Friday over his botched plan to sell off the World Cup to private investors.

The FIFA president was forced to abandon a hugely controversial proposal to sell stakes in the tournament to a group led by Josh Kushner, the brother of Donald Trump’s son-in-law Jared, on Saturday, following a major revolt from the footballing world.

That heaped the pressure on Infantino, with UEFA subsequently declaring a loss of confidence in the Italian-Swiss administrator.

European football's governing body had previously led the rebellion, announcing on Thursday that their 55 member nations would boycott the World Cup if the plans weren't scrapped.

And now, UEFA threatened to go to court over the scheme, which was known as FIFA Forward Enterprise (FFE), in a letter they sent to Infantino on Friday.

The report adds that UEFA also wrote to Kushner, Greg Maffei, J.P. Morgan and OpenEconomics, and said they were 'actively considering legal action, arbitration, and/or regulatory complaints' as a result of the collapsed proposal.

UEFA reportedly threatened Gianni Infantino with legal action over his botched World Cup plan

FIFA president Infantino pictured with his UEFA counterpart Aleksander Ceferin in 2024

The letter to Infantino read: 'Uefa hereby gives formal notice that it is actively considering legal action, arbitration, and/or regulatory complaints (together, the “proceedings”) arising out of and in connection with the FFE plan proposed by Fifa and all related matters as further described below.

'You and Fifa are required to take immediate steps to identify, locate, and preserve all documents and electronically stored information described in this notice that are in your or Fifa’s possession, custody, or control.'

UEFA went on to warn FIFA that 'any destruction, deletion, alteration, concealment or loss of relevant materials' after their letter 'may constitute spoliation of evidence'.

They then refused to rule out further action if any of the aforementioned actions took place, but the letter itself is not legal action.

The letter also insisted that FIFA must ensure that certain individuals, including Infantino, Arsene Wenger, FIFA's chief of global football development, secretary general Mattias Grafstrom and Kevin Lamour, FIFA's chief operating officer, 'specifically preserve all such materials in their possession'.

UEFA confirmed to Daily Mail Sport that a document preservation letter was sent.

Kushner was expected to lead the proposed investor group through his Thrive Eternal fund, while Maffei, who is a Trump donor, was also set to be involved.

J.P. Morgan and OpenEconomics were involved in the search for investors.

UEFA also wrote to Joshua Kushner, who was expected to lead the group of private investors

Speaking on Saturday as he announced the abandonment of his plans, Infantino said: 'The FIFA Forward Enterprise project was intended to provide a basis for further strengthening our FIFA Member Associations and our sport worldwide, especially in those countries where support is most needed.

'And more so, as we said from the outset, to do this only if a majority of the FIFA Member Associations were in support and always subject to a consultation process with them, the FIFA Council, the Confederations and wider stakeholders.

'Having listened carefully to all the views, it has become clear that the project has created divisions of a nature that, regardless of the level of support, are no longer in the interest of the objective set out in the first place.'

He continued: 'Our purpose has always been - and will always be - to unite and improve. As a result, this proposal will not proceed.

'Moving forward, my intent is to bring all interested parties back together in the coming days and weeks in the spirit of shared interest in our game, and with the objective to continue growing football everywhere, and particularly in those countries that mostly need our support.'

The statement marked an embarrassing u-turn for Infantino, given it came less than 24 hours after he attempted to clarify his plans and blamed the media for misconstruing them.

It remains to be seen what happens to the FIFA president, with Infantino having previously been expected to run unopposed in the governing body's elections next March.

That may change now, while FIFA member nations could trigger a vote of no confidence to oust Infantino. The threshold to initiate the process is 46 FIFA member associations. For context, UEFA have 55 members.

Sports.title: Jordan Henderson's move to Chelsea confirmed: England midfielder, 36, joins Blues after ripping up Brentford contract
Sports.content:
Jordan Henderson's move to Chelsea confirmed: England midfielder, 36, joins Blues after ripping up Brentford contract

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

Chelsea have confirmed their signing of Jordan Henderson on a free transfer, after Brentford allowed the 36-year-old to terminate his contract a year earlier than expected.

It comes two days after they secured the signature of Danny Welbeck, 35, from Brighton.

Between them, Henderson and Welbeck will add 863 Premier League games’ worth of experience to a changing room now overseen by new manager Xabi Alonso, 44.

Henderson said: 'Given the size of the club, the manager, who I have great admiration for, and the quality of the players, this was a huge opportunity I couldn’t turn down.

‘I was also so impressed with how much the ownership want Chelsea to be successful and move in the right direction.

‘For me, it's about giving everything every single day, both on and off the field, to help the players around me and the team as much as possible. I'm very excited to get going.’

Jordan Henderson's move to Chelsea has been confirmed after he ripped up his Brentford deal

The midfielder was all smiles as he spent the day at Chelsea's Cobham training ground

Henderson, 36, said he was ready to 'give everything every single day, on and off the field'

Alonso identified during his talks to take over Chelsea that their squad was in need of greater balance among the players. The Blues had broken Premier League records for fielding the youngest sides over the previous two seasons, but they had been criticised by fans on occasion for appearing to lack maturity on and off the pitch.

Chelsea previously targeted Granit Xhaka, the 33-year-old Sunderland captain who had worked with Alonso at Bayer Leverkusen, but were unable to get him out of the Stadium of Light. They likewise showed interest in John Stones, who has now joined Inter Milan at 32.

Yet they have now secured Henderson for free, while the fee for Welbeck is being described as ‘undisclosed’, though his cost is by no means substantial, if indeed there even is one.

Welbeck has already travelled to Hong Kong to join his new team-mates. Daily Mail Sport reported last week how Brentford were ready to sanction Henderson’s exit rather than seek a fee from Chelsea. He is still recovering from the broken arm he suffered with England at the World Cup.

These signings are concrete confirmation that Chelsea have adjusted their transfer strategy by now aiming to add experienced leaders to their squad. Previously, there had been a focus on finding younger players of potential.

Maxence Lacroix, 26 and from Crystal Palace, has already been confirmed by Chelsea for £52million. Morgan Rogers has also arrived for £117m from Aston Villa.

Sports.title: Eddie Hearn makes seven-figure demand for latest star but admits he 'might not be the best'
Sports.content:
Eddie Hearn makes seven-figure demand for latest star but admits he 'might not be the best'

England and Northampton star Henry Pollock is now managed by Matchroom and Eddie Hearn - who is seeking a record pay day for the player's next contract

View 2 Images Eddie Hearn is handling Henry Pollock's contract talks

Eddie Hearn has claimed that Northampton star Henry Pollock is "a seven-figure player" as he goes into contract talks with Northampton - even if the promoter admits "there might be players who are better".

‌



Pollock opted to join up with the Matchroom supremo several months ago and now has Hearn leading his contract negotiations with the Prem champions. The 21-year-old’s contract is thought to be around £150,000 per year, but it expires at the end of next season.

‌



Hearn is looking to land the England back rower a bumper pay day and has told Northampton to "recognise what they have got" whilst he stated that Pollock was "making an unquestionable difference to the bottom line of the club."

‌



The Matchroom chief is a hugely influential figure and has talked up the money Pollock could get if he chose to move elsewhere - and his financial demands would make Pollock comfortably the highest paid player at Franklin's Gardens.

Lewis Moody health latest as star arrives at Wimbledon after MND diagnosis READ MORE :

England strategy in the spotlight as Prem's best leaves and Exeter boss spells out reality READ MORE :

Hearn told the Telegraph: “It is all very well saying that there might be players who are a bit more consistent or might be better or whatever, but there aren’t players that are making an unquestionable and undeniable difference to the bottom line of the club.

‌



“Henry Pollock drives season ticket sales. Henry Pollock puts bums on the seats. Henry Pollock drives viewership on TNT or wherever it’s going to be. Henry Pollock sells shirts, right? That’s the difference. So you can actually put an economic value over having Henry Pollock on the team, and that has to be recognised, regardless of the want from Henry. He cannot stay at this club on the money that he’s on.”

Alongside his Northampton contract Pollock also receives around £150,000 per year from the Rugby Football Union as an enhanced elite player squad member with England. Northampton though have spent under the £6.4m cap with their marquee player thought to be fly-half Fin Smith.

View 2 Images Henry Pollock was recently with Eddie Hearn on his yacht (Image: @henryjpollock)

Article continues below

Reports claim Tommy Freeman will soon pen a deal that makes him the Prem's best paid winger but Hearn has talked up Pollock's financial pull off the pitch, even if the player would like to remain at Northampton. He also claimed the club's opening offer was not a “fair representation of his commercial value”.

“The first thing I said to Henry was: ‘Do you want to stay at Northampton?’” Hearn said. “And he said, ‘Yes.’ He said, ‘I love the club, I love the team, I love that I live 10 minutes away, and I think we’re going to win the championship again next year and I want to win championships'."

If Pollock wants to remain playing for England, which is the case, then he will have to sign with a club in the Prem. Many of those are already spending close to the cap and few would have the scope to pay a player £1m as things stand.

Sports.title: Emma Raducanu OUT of US Open as injury nightmare continues for British No.1
Sports.content:
Emma Raducanu OUT of US Open as injury nightmare continues for British No.1

Emma Raducanu has been forced to skip the US Open due to a stress fracture in her lower right leg, having missed Wimbledon earlier in the summer

View 2 Images Emma Raducanu has been hampered by injuries recently (Image: Getty)

Emma Raducanu will miss a second consecutive Grand Slam tournament as she continues to recover from a stress fracture in her lower right leg.

‌



The world No. 49 is set to skip the US Open after pulling out of Wimbledon on the eve of the tournament earlier this summer.

‌



Raducanu, 23, has not played a match since finishing runner-up at the Queen’s Club almost two months ago. It’s now been five years since the Brit made history at the US Open, becoming the first and only qualifier to win a Major title.

‌



But on the half-decade anniversary of her heroic run, she will not compete in Flushing Meadows.

The US Open gets underway in less than four weeks, but Raducanu has already decided to skip the event on medical advice and is said to be sad to miss such a special tournament.

Since pulling out of Wimbledon, the British No. 1 has been spotted wearing a protective boot on her right leg. She has also shared footage from some early practice sessions. One video showed Raducanu sitting on a bin and hitting balls. In a second clip, filmed during a trip to Switzerland, she stood on a clay court and hit some serves.

‌



The US Open concludes on September 13, by which time Raducanu won’t have played a match for three months. She was also not named in Britain’s squad for the Billie Jean King Finals, which takes place in Shenzhen from September 22 to 27.

View 2 Images Emma Raducanu withdrew from Wimbledon less than 24 hours before her first round match (Image: Getty)

The world No. 49 also missed more than two months of competition from March to May due to post-viral illness, while a bone bruising injury in her foot wrecked her pre-season preparations. And the stress fracture is the latest issue to derail Raducanu’s 2026 season.

Article continues below

Announcing her withdrawal from Wimbledon on the night before her first-round match this summer, she said: “I can’t believe I’m saying this, but sadly I’ve had to withdraw from this year’s Wimbledon.

“I’ve done everything possible to try to get to the start line tomorrow but after a final scan tonight, the niggle I’ve been managing has developed into a stress fracture and I’ve been medically advised to stop pushing through.

“Playing at Wimbledon, in front of a home crowd, means everything to me, so this is really difficult to process. I want to thank you all for your support and encouragement. Especially at a time like this, it is invaluable. I look forward to seeing you when I’m back.”

Sports.title: Saffie Osborne to captain Ryan Moore and Dylan Browne McMonagle in Shergar Cup at Ascot
Sports.content:
Saffie Osborne to captain Ryan Moore and Dylan Browne McMonagle in Shergar Cup at Ascot

The Dubai Duty Free Shergar Cup at Ascot on Saturday has been boosted by the news that Ryan Moore and Dylan Browne McMonagle will be in action

View 2 Images Saffie Osborne (centre) will lead a team featuring Dylan Browne McMonagle (left) and Ryan Moore (Image: PA)

Ryan Moore will make only his second appearance in the Dubai Duty Free Shergar Cup at Ascot on Saturday, with the event further strengthened by confirmation that rising star Dylan Browne McMonagle will compete.

‌



Moore, who secured the Silver Saddle award for leading rider in the team competition during his only previous participation in 2006, has been freed up with no Flat racing scheduled in Ireland that afternoon.

‌



Moore and McMonagel will represent the Great Britain and Ireland team which will be captained by Saffie Osborne at the event which will also feature teams from Hong Kong, Europe and the Rest Of The World.

‌



The Hong Kong Jockey Club will field a team, led by Vincent Ho, who claimed Shergar Cup glory in 2019 as part of the victorious Rest of the World squad. He will be accompanied by Jerry Chau and Luke Ferraris.

Christophe Lemaire will skipper Europe, alongside Marie Velon and Frida Valle Skar, while Jamie Melham (nee Kah) will return to spearhead the Rest of the World. She will be partnered by Japan's Yutake Take and Suraj Narredu, who steered team Asia to victory last year.

‌



Ascot's head of corporate and industry affairs Will Aitkenhead said: "It's absolutely fantastic to have Ryan and Dylan on board. Both had very strong Royal Ascots, with Ryan the leading jockey, and both had very good weeks at Goodwood.

View 2 Images Jamie Kah: Melbourne Cup winner will ride at Shergar Cup (Image: Getty Images)

"It's really helpful the Phoenix Stakes has moved from the Saturday to the Sunday at the Curragh this year which frees them up and it's great to have them board.

Article continues below

"We'd been in discussions with Oisin (Murphy) and Billy (Loughnane) earlier in the year and they were keen, but they just don't know where they'll be. Obviously Hollie Doyle would have been here, but she's sadly injured.

"In previous years we've lined them up early which helps with the marketing and everything, but this year we were keen to get the strongest teams that we could so waiting until this week made sense."

On the subject of overseas riders, Aitkenhead commented: "Jamie Melham returns as a Melbourne Cup winner, she's huge in Australia and Yutake Take is the biggest name in Japan. We've got Christophe Lemaire and the Hong Kong team led by Vincent Ho as well so we've got some really strong teams."

Sports.title: Jockey allegedly headbutted official and told another ‘if you keep filming, I am going to slap you’
Sports.content:
Jockey allegedly headbutted official and told another ‘if you keep filming, I am going to slap you’

Jerome Claudic became aggressive and insulting after staff tried to stop him entering an area reserved for corporate guests at ParisLongchamp

View 3 Images Jerome Claudic (second right) was banned for one month (Image: Icon Sport via Getty Images)

A jockey allegedly headbutted an official and told another ‘if you keep filming, I am going to slap you’, according to a disciplinary inquiry.

‌



Jerome Claudic, a jockey with nearly 20 years experience, has ridden 27 winners in France this year and over 500 during the course of his career.

‌



He was reported to the France Galop stewards following an incident after racing at Paris Longchamp in July in a corporate hospitality where a garden furniture design business was entertaining guests. The disciplinary panel was told that Claudic, who appeared "heavily intoxicated", had attempted to enter the area with two female friends insisting he was entitled to be there.

‌



When challenged he unleashed “a torrent of insults” at France Galop and described the guests and partners as “buffoons”.

During a six minute outburst, which included racist comments, he was filmed by the company's head of digital who he ordered to put away her phone, telling her, "If you keep filming, I’m going to slap you". He then delivered a “completely unprovoked headbutt” to a member of France Galop staff, the hearing was told.

Claudic was escorted to the exit by a France Galop staff member but as he left uttered “death threats, threats of physical violence, and racist remarks—shouting, in particular, 'You two are dead men walking'.

‌



View 3 Images The incident occurred after racing at Longchamp (Image: Getty)

Claudic explained when interviewed that he had been looking for somewhere to watch the football. He admitted losing his temper when he saw someone filming him but denied headbutting anyone. He said he had been under the influence of alcohol after drinking a "small glass," but that he was mainly tired and annoyed by the video taken without his knowledge.

He explained that jockeys undergo gruelling work schedules, including in intense heat on that day, and he felt worn out.

‌



The panel was told: “He intends to go straight home after races from now on; he and his colleagues feel unwelcome at this racecourse—which provides no designated space for professionals—and since this has caused problems before, he will never set foot there again.”

He apologised and said he had never behaved in that way before and on that evening it was simply a case of having "had enough".

View 3 Images Claudic said jockeys don't feel welcome at Longchamp (Image: Getty Images)

‌



The France Galop stewards said Claudic had “displayed behavior that was absolutely intolerable and unacceptable. This conduct cannot be justified by the explanations he provided; while the apologies he offered must be taken into account, they do not absolve him of responsibility.”

The panel added his behaviour damaged “the image and reputation of the racing institution and the sport itself”.

It said it was also clear Claudic had not learned the lessons of previous disciplinary actions having previously been suspended for six months in 2021, following a test that revealed the presence of a narcotic substance.

Article continues below

Claudic was referred to the France Galop Medical Department for potential psychological, medical, and addiction-related follow-up. He was suspended from riding for one month with another three months suspended for five years.

Sports.title: Frank Lampard green lights £89m Chelsea transfer reunion after signing son of ex-teammate
Sports.content:
Frank Lampard green lights £89m Chelsea transfer reunion after signing son of ex-teammate

Frank Lampard's Coventry City have enquired about facilitating a reunion for the Chelsea icon by making contact over a current Blues star

View 2 Images Frank Lampard is looking to equip his team for the Premier League (Image: Pete Norton/Getty Images)

Frank Lampard could be set for a reunion with Mykhailo Mudryk after Coventry City made contact with Chelsea about his availibility. The newly-promoted side are one of three Premier League sides to have reached out.

‌



Lampard coached the Ukrainian winger during his spell in charge of the Blues in 2023 and now has the possibility of utilising his services once again but in more positive circumstances. The Chelsea icon led Coventry to the Championship title last season in his first role since a difficult second stint in the Stamford Bridge dugout when he replaced Graham Potter on an interim basis.

‌



Mudryk, meanwhile, has made his return to football, having not played since November 2024 against Heidenheim. The 25-year-old tested positive for meldonium but the FA has now ended its anti-doping proceedings after Mudryk accepted breaching anti-doping rules.

‌



The parties agreed to a suspension equal to the one year and eight months already served by the ex-Shahktar Donetsk player. His return has led to no shortage of interest, with three Premier League teams and three more from Europe making contact about Mudryk's future.

The Chelsea speedster, who signed for the Blues in a deal worth up to £88.5m, is in Hong Kong with the west London side as Chelsea's pre-season tour continues. Xabi Alonso gave little away about Murdyk's future.

Alejandro Garnacho takes brutal swipe at Chelsea immediately after Aston Villa debut READ MORE :

Chelsea squad's immediate reaction to Mykhailo Mudryk bombshell and imminent return READ MORE :

"We need to see," he said. "It's too early to tell, to see how he is in terms of fitness, in terms of this game time that you need to be involved again, so it's still early to tell."

‌



"We can expect that [it will take longer to get back to full fitness and sharpness]," Alonso added. "We have the Mudryk that [we had], it will take time, but once there is a change, things start moving, and for him it's a massive change.

"So he trained on his own every day, and I think it had to be really, really hard, because he wanted to play football, he wanted to be part of a team, and he was not allowed to do that for such a long time.

FOLLOW OUR CHELSEA FB PAGE! Latest Blues news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

‌



View 2 Images Mykhaylo Mudryk has not played for Chelsea since November 2024. (Image: Sebastian Widmann - UEFA, UEFA via Getty Images)

"So once this big change has happened, now things will move on, and afterwards we will see if it's quicker, if it's slower, but we need to be aware of that."

It comes after Coventry added to Lampard's squad over the weekend. Teenage goalkeeper Jack Ruddy joined Coventry from Norwich.

Article continues below

Ruddy is the son of former Norwich and Newcastle United shotstopper John Ruddy, who left the Magpies at the end of last season. Lampard was team-mates with Ruddy senior on the international stage with both selected for England in 2021 for a win over Italy.

Sports.title: Gianni Infantino and Donald Trump meeting not happening as third nation calls out FIFA boss
Sports.content:
Gianni Infantino and Donald Trump meeting not happening as third nation calls out FIFA boss

Gianni Infantino's future as FIFA President has been the subject of speculation following the failed FIFA Forward Enterprise (FFE) proposals

View 2 Images FIFA President Gianni Infantino is under immense pressure (Image: Alex Pantling/FIFA via Getty Images)

Gianni Infantino has not scheduled a call with members of Donald Trump's Cabinet in a bid to save his FIFA job, the Mirror has been told. Claims that the under-fire FIFA president requested a call where he was reportedly set to appeal for support have also been denied by the US government.

‌



Infantino’s future as FIFA President has been a topic of speculation ever since controversial proposals emerged, which would have seen the federation sell shares in its major tournaments, including the men’s and women’s World Cups, as well as the Club World Cup.

‌



FIFA have since confirmed that the plans, which were named the FIFA Forward Enterprise (FFE), have been dropped after the widespread criticism which has followed.

‌



As a result, speculation has been swirling about Infantino’s future as FIFA President, with the New York Post now reporting that a meeting has been arranged with US Secretary of State Marco Rubio.

Leandro Paredes sparks uproar for unsportsmanlike act weeks after World Cup final ‘punch’ READ MORE :

Gianni Infantino was set to earn huge salary from World Cup plan as staggering figure revealed READ MORE :

Mirror Football understands that, despite the recent reports, no meeting is scheduled to take place between Infantino and members of the Trump administration, including the US Secretary of State.

Assistant Secretary of State for Global Public Affairs Dylan Johnson has written in a post on X, formerly known as Twitter, to deny that such a meeting is taking place between Rubio and Infantino.

‌



England and Wales have already called for a leadership change at FIFA, with both nations withdrawing their support for Infantino’s re-election bid as President.

Serbia recently became the latest country to withdraw their support for Infantino to be re-elected as FIFA President.

In a statement released on Monday, they said: "We recall that FA of Serbia formally expressed its support for Mr Infantino in writing on 25 May this year, but after a thorough consideration of the developments that have seriously undermined the reputation and credibility of both FIFA and its President in the past period, this is the only logical and rational move.

‌



View 2 Images FIFA President Gianni Infantino said the controversial FFE proposal will not proceed (Image: VCG via Getty Images)

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

"Football Association of Serbia is of the opinion that the future of world football must be founded on transparency, dialogue, mutual respect, and partner relations among all confederations and national associations.

‌



"We believe that no decision of strategic importance for the future of football should be made without broad consensus and open consultation with all relevant stakeholders.

"Football Association of Serbia remains committed to cooperation with FIFA, UEFA, and all national associations for the purpose of development and improvement of football, but is also of the opinion that at this moment a new trust is needed, as well as a new approach, and management that will contribute to restoring dialogue, unity, and the credibility of international football institutions."

Sports.title: Glasgow hailed as 'blueprint for future of Commonwealth Games' after major success
Sports.content:
Glasgow hailed as 'blueprint for future of Commonwealth Games' after major success

A new format using exisiting facilities proved to be a "Games changer". The event sold more than 430,000 tickets to show that it was a real Box Office success.

The King and The Queen's entrance to the Opening Ceremony of Glasgow 2026 Commonwealth Games

Glasgow 2026 was today hailed as a 'blueprint' for future Commonwealth Games.

‌



The event ended with a message to the rest of the world - the new format using exisiting facilities is a "Games changer". It sold more than 430,000 tickets to show that it was a real Box Office success.

‌



And Phil Batty, chief executive of Glasgow 2026, said: "We have created a Games that will inspire more nations to host. Probably more importantly, it is one that every nation feels it could host at some point in the next 100 years.

‌



"The future of the Commonwealth Games was in jeopardy. Glasgow saved the Commonwealth Games but it also reinvented the Commonwealth Games."

Jim Kerr and Simple Minds brought down the curtain on the event at the closing ceremony. The Games' projected cost was £162.6m compared with £543m for Glasgow 2014 and £680m for Birmingham 2022.

View 3 Images Jim Kerr of Simple Minds at the closing ceremony of Glasgow 2026 (Image: Getty Images)

‌



Prince Edward shares sweet moment with Prince Louis at Commonwealth Games READ MORE :

The public backed the Games as netball proved to be the most popular sport selling more than 100,000 tickets. English powerlifter Mark Swan won the first gold medal of the 215 that were on offer.

The rising star from Seaham, Co Durham, said it had provided an 'unforgettable experience'. The more compact 23rd edition featured 215 medal events compared to 261 when the city last staged the Games in 2014. It also saw a record 47 para-sports events, which included the symbolic first gold medal.

View 3 Images Jim Kerr of Simple Minds on stage at the closing ceremony of Glasgow 2026 (Image: Getty Images)

‌



Australia dominated the medal table by amassing 171 followed by England with 110. The host nation finished fifth, with 39 medals, behind Canada and India.

It was a performance described by First Minister John Swinney as "truly historic". Welsh star Emma Finucane created history by becoming the first sprint cyclist to win four track gold medals at the same Games.

Louise Hoskins became the oldest Commonwealth Games gold medallist, winning the para-bowls women's pairs title for Australia at the age of 76 years and 173 days. And legendary South African swimmer Chad le Clos became the most decorated athlete in the 96-year history of the event with 21 medals.

Article continues below

View 3 Images Fireworks closed Glasgow 2026 (Image: Jane Barlow/PA Wire)

Prince William and Princess Kate were among those who took in the action with their children. Mile world record holder Josh Kerr produced another thrilling triumph in the mile, which last featured at the Games in 1966.

The star repaid fans by taking 45 minutes to pose for selfies and autographs after his emotional medal ceremony.

Sports.title: Vinicius Jr to Arsenal transfer hint as key figure flies into London
Sports.content:
Vinicius Jr to Arsenal transfer hint as key figure flies into London

Vinicius Junior might have reported back to Real Madrid for pre-season training, but he is still the subject of growing speculation over a transfer to Arsenal

View 3 Images Vinicius Junior is being eyed for a blockbuster move to Arsenal (Image: (Antonio Villalba/Real Madrid via Getty Images))

Vinicius Jr continues to be linked with a move to Arsenal - and now the president of the agency that represents him has confirmed he is going to be in London. The Gunners have launched a stunning move to sign the Real Madrid star, as Mikel Arteta looks to add some quality to his title-winning squad.

‌



Vinicius, who reported back to Real on Monday for pre-season training, has scored 128 goals in 375 appearances for the La Liga giants, who are keen to keep hold of him this summer. So much so that they have been trying to renew his deal for a number of months now.

‌



The Brazilian's deal expires next summer, and Real opened further talks with him last week in a bid to reach an agreement. But with nothing forthcoming, the La Liga giants have informed the 26-year-old’s camp that the latest contract offer they submitted is final and there will be no further increase or another round of negotiations.

‌



If Vinicius accepts, his deal will be renewed; however, if he rejects the offer, Madrid will open the door to a sale this summer to prevent the Brazilian from entering his final year of contract and leaving for free later, according to Spanish publication Marca.

But now, in an interesting development, the president of Roc Nation Sports confirmed on Monday morning that he is travelling to London. Michael R. Yormark took to Instagram to post an update saying: “London, here I come. Let’s go!”

Arsenal receive immediate response after finally submitting first Bruno Guimaraes offer READ MORE :

Mikel Arteta sends Vinicius Jr transfer message ahead of Real Madrid meeting READ MORE :

FOLLOW OUR ARSENAL FB PAGE! Latest Gunners news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

‌



View 3 Images Michael R. Yormark's post on Instagram

Amid the speculation around the attacker’s Real future, Roc Nation took the unusual step on Sunday by hitting out at 'fake and damaging' reports in a statement shared by Yormark on Instagram. It's not clear whether Roc Nation were speaking about Vinicius and the ongoing rumours surrounding a Real Madrid exit and a move to Arsenal or something else.

But the statement said: "Roc Nation Sports International and our entire team cannot stand idle when unprofessional and uninformed media publish fake and damaging information for attention-seeking purposes.

‌



"This is especially unacceptable when it personally targets our clients without any foundation. It is disruptive, harmful and libellous. Media outlets and journalists need to hold themselves more accountable."

The Gunners have already bolstered their attacking options this summer with the £34million signing of Christos Tzolis from Club Brugge earlier this month. And as well as Vinicius, they're also working on a deal to sign Bruno Guimaraes from Newcastle United, but have seen their opening offer rejected.

View 3 Images Christos Tzolis in action for Arsenal (Image: Getty Images)

‌



And speaking over the weekend, Gunners boss Arteta admitted: "A lot is happening. We all know about the context of this transfer window.

"From ownership to the board, the sporting director and myself, we know that we want to take this club to a different level. That is going to require a better squad, better individuals.

"We have identified where we have opportunities to grow and to improve and to evolve our game and what is going to be needed to achieve that. Hopefully, very soon we can start to put things in a very concrete way."

Sports.title: 'Brutal, searing and punishing heat' - Babb on playing for Ireland at USA '94
Sports.content:
While none of the home nations qualified for the 1994 World Cup, the Republic of Ireland did.

It was a second successive appearance at the tournament for the Boys in Green, who were again led by 1966 World Cup winner Jack Charlton.

At Italia '90, the weather had been hot - but at USA '94, it was a different kettle of fish altogether.

The iconic image of Charlton launching an open bottle of water in the direction of Andy Townsend and Tommy Coyne always provides a reminder of that.

Image: Jack Charlton led the Republic of Ireland at Italia '90 and USA '94

He clashed with FIFA over their policy that bottles could not be thrown to the players on the pitch, so took to throwing the contents instead before FIFA later relented and allowed water bags to be thrown.

"They trust me to do what is right for them and I will continue to do it," Charlton said. "We have been right in pursuing this matter and FIFA's change of heart proves that."

Charlton was rarely seen without his white baseball cap that summer. Steve Staunton famously even wore one during the national anthem before the second group game against Mexico.

One of the players in the Ireland squad that summer was Phil Babb. The defender, then 23, had just completed his second full Premier League season at Coventry.

He made his international debut in a 0-0 friendly draw with Russia in March 1994, then played in the next four friendlies leading up to the tournament.

Image: Phil Babb played in all four of the Republic of Ireland's games at the 1994 World Cup

Nothing was set in stone, but he knew he would at least have a decent chance of being included in Charlton's 22-man squad, so started to physically prepare himself.

"A coach at Coventry asked me if I wanted to do anything specific - we ended up doing 12-minute sessions in a sauna!" Babb recalls, with a smile.

"We were doing burpees, press-ups, just trying to acclimatise to that intense heat. We did about six sessions - but I wouldn't recommend it for anyone now!

"I was a fit lad and had played pretty much all the Premier League games Coventry had played that season. I adapted to the heat pretty well, but I know some of the older lads really struggled."

Babb started alongside Paul McGrath in the heart of defence for Ireland's tournament opener at Giants Stadium in New Jersey.

Image: Ray Houghton's stunning strike earned a shock 1-0 win over Italy

That Saturday, they shocked an Italy side that featured Paolo Maldini, Franco Baresi and Roberto Baggio. John Aldridge's stunner sealed a memorable 1-0 win.

It was an achievement made all the more impressive by the fact the Azzurri went on to finish as runners-up - but also given the fact it was played in temperatures exceeding 30C.

"When we walked out onto the field, about two hours before kick-off, you could tell it was going to be absolutely roasting," he recalls.

"You could tell that straight away and we didn't stay out long. I just checked the grass to see which studs I wanted, then I went straight back in. I know some of the lads were walking around and taking the atmosphere in, but I thought: 'This is too hot'.

"I didn't go out for a warm-up with the rest of the lads, either. I stayed in the changing room. It was built for NFL, so they had a 40m sprint track. I warmed up in there and waited until we went out. It was brutal, it was searing, it was punishing.

"It affected everyone's game. You were saturated after just 10 minutes walking onto a pitch, so you had to conserve energy at the right times.

"Recovery was very basic and there was very little ball work because of the demands of the actual games and the fluids you lose. When you're that dehydrated, it's quite difficult. You want a drink, but you don't feel hungry and that is a key part of the recuperation."

Image: Babb, whose Ireland were knocked out by Dennis Bergkamp's Netherlands, joined Liverpool later that summer

Thirty-two years on from that tournament, football has evolved exponentially.

Sports science has taken on a key role in the game and, this summer, is likely to play into the way teams approach games tactically due to the heat. A slower tempo is expected in many.

Charlton was not prepared to facilitate the same in 1994, though.

"We only played one way, so if you tried to go off-piste, Jack would certainly let you know!" adds Babb.

"We had one style of play, with a lone striker. If it wasn't Tommy Coyne, it might have been Niall Quinn up there and we'd be putting long balls up to him, with either willing runners out wide or the midfield bombing on.

"That was the Irish way back then. Tommy ran tirelessly, to the point where he actually collapsed with heat exhaustion on the plane home.

"I think Jack's sports science was a barrel of Guinness in his room and he'd call the lads in and have a pint! I'm sure there's a high calorific content in that, so maybe he was ahead of his time!"

In spite of that, Babb's memories of the tournament are largely positive.

"I enjoyed it, I have to admit! I'd rather play in the searing heat than a wet Tuesday night in Hull," he says.

"I was a fit lad and it was quite easy for me playing alongside Paul McGrath, who was imperious in that tournament. I learned a lot from him and how he conserved his energy.

"I felt I got stronger because I got used to it. I guess our 0-0 draw against Norway would probably attest to the heat and the style of play.

"It all comes down to the individual. Footballers are supreme athletes now and they leave nothing to chance, so I think they'll cope a lot better than we did in the mid-90s."

The methods may have moved on since Charlton was throwing water onto the pitch, but Babb's memories from USA '94 provide a reminder this World Cup will be a battle against more than just the opposition.

Sports.title: Ogbene earns Republic of Ireland draw with Canada
Sports.content:
Chiedozie Ogbene's equaliser ensured the Republic of Ireland continued their good run of results as they drew 1-1 with World Cup co-hosts Canada in Montreal.

Canada went ahead in the 24th minute from an own goal by defender Jake O'Brien, heading a failed clearance into his own net from Stephen Eustaquio's corner.

Ireland were then awarded a penalty in the second half after Cyle Larin - who signed a two-year deal with Southampton earlier in the day - took out Jamie McGrath.

Canada goalkeeper Maxime Crepeau saved Troy Parrott's initial attempt, but Ogbene was on hand to slam home the rebound and tie the game in the 60th minute.

Image: Ireland's Jake O'Brien heads the ball into his own net

Ireland, who failed to qualify for this summer's World Cup, went close to a winner but Crepeau denied a charging run from Mason Melia late on.

The Orlando City goalkeeper missed out on the 2022 World Cup in Qatar after breaking his leg while playing in the MLS Cup final.

Canada, managed by former Leeds boss Jesse Marsch, officially open the World Cup on June 12 in Toronto against Bosnia and Herzegovina, before facing Qatar on June 18 and Switzerland on June 24.

They remain without captain Alphonso Davies, who is still nursing a hamstring injury he sustained while playing for Bayern Munich.

Sports.title: Republic of Ireland edge past Qatar in friendly as both sides end with 10
Sports.content:
Captain Nathan Collins headed the Republic of Ireland to a 1-0 friendly victory over World Cup-bound Qatar as both sides were reduced to 10 men.

Collins ensured Ireland got the better of a side managed by his former Wolves boss Julen Lopetegui with an early header.

However, just how the evening might have panned out had Jack Moylan not been dismissed as half-time approached, a sparse crowd inside the Aviva Stadium will never know.

Heimir Hallgrimsson's side, whose hopes of making it to the World Cup finals were dashed in heartbreaking fashion in March when they lost their play-off semi-final to the Czech Republic on penalties, were in complete control until Moylan's premature exit.

Qatar substitute Almoez Ali suffered the same fate 12 minutes from time.

Image: Jack Moylan was sent off before half-time at the Aviva Stadium

The game was played out against the backdrop of ongoing unease at the forthcoming Nations League clashes with Israel, and play was interrupted on several occasions during the first half as 'Stop the Game' protesters among a crowd of 28,981 repeatedly hurled tennis balls on to the pitch.

Ireland will now head for Montreal and their friendly against World Cup co-hosts Canada on June 6, while Qatar continue their preparations for the finals - they launch their Group B campaign against Switzerland in San Francisco on June 13 - against El Salvador in Los Angeles on the same day.

The Republic took the lead with just five minutes gone when, having been fouled by Ayoub Al-Oui wide on the left, Moylan curled the resulting free-kick on to the head of Collins, who glanced the ball effortlessly past 'keeper Mahmoud Abunada.

Image: Qatar's Almoez Ali was also sent off

There was a brief interruption after the protesters made their presence felt for the first time as Qatar's Pedro Miguel underwent treatment for injury, but once order had been restored, Troy Parrott whipped a first-time shot wide after being picked out by Seamus Coleman.

The Qataris simply could not get anywhere near Hallgrimsson's men and a mid-half drinks break did little to improve matters for the visitors with Abunada having to field Jayson Molumby's deflected 24th-minute shot from distance.

Lopetegui could not hide his frustration on the sideline and only the bravery of defender Ahmed Fathi denied Chiedozie Ogbene a second goal as he attempted to latch on to Liam Scales' header back across goal.

But the home side's night took a turn for the worse on the stroke of half-time when Northern Irish referee Jamie Robinson deemed Moylan's challenge on Jassem Gaber worthy of a red card, much to the Lincoln frontman's clear astonishment.

Image: Former Wolves and West Ham boss Julen Lopetegui is now in charge of Qatar

With defender James Abankwah having replaced Dara O'Shea at half-time, the 10 men found themselves under pressure for the first time on their return, although Coleman very nearly caught Abunada off his line with an audacious 52nd-minute attempt from the right wing.

Edmilson Junior dragged a long-range effort wide two minutes later after Molumby went down in midfield under Fathi's challenge and it took a fine 71st-minute reaction save by Caoimhin Kelleher - his first of the night - to keep out Yusuf Abdurisag's deflected shot.

However, Qatari hopes of salvation were dashed with 12 minutes remaining when Ali struck out at Molumby off the ball on several occasions and was also sent off.

Sports.title: Parrott out of luck as Republic of Ireland draw with North Macedonia
Sports.content:
Troy Parrott had two goals disallowed as the Republic of Ireland played out a stalemate against North Macedonia on the night on which they had hoped to book a trip to the World Cup finals.

Five days after their dreams came to an end for another four years in Prague, Ireland drew 0-0 with the Macedonians in a friendly encounter neither side wanted as the Czech Republic and Denmark fought for the big prize.

Even a third successive home victory for the first time since the 2015-16 campaign would have provided scant consolation for Thursday night's disappointment but Heimir Hallgrimsson's men had to make do with a disappointing draw.

AZ Alkmaar striker Parrott came closest to breaking the deadlock as 37-year-old defender Seamus Coleman received a standing ovation from a crowd of 39,560 at the Aviva Stadium when he was replaced during the second half of what could yet prove to be his final appearance for his country.

Nevertheless, the squad will reconvene for a series of friendlies at the end of the season ahead of next season's Nations League campaign and later Euro 2028 qualification having restored a measure of pride and established a momentum they hope will serve them well when they return to competitive action.

The hosts went on to the offensive from the off, although they were unable to find the final ball to allow either Parrott or Chiedozie Ogbene to threaten.

John Egan could not direct an 11th-minute corner at goal and Ogbene saw his snapshot deflected over three minutes later, but goalkeeper Caoimhin Kelleher had to parry Enis Bardhi's 21st-minute free-kick after it flicked off the defensive wall, with Bardhi volleying high over after the resulting corner had been only half-cleared.

Macedonia keeper Stole Dimitrievski saved Parrott's 23rd-minute header comfortably after Dara O'Shea and Finn Azaz had sparked a concerted attack, and Azaz failed to make the most of a free-kick two minutes later after he had been tripped just outside the penalty area.

Parrott was played into a promising position by Knight nine minutes before the break, only to miss the target by some distance.

The in-form striker - he scored his sixth goal in three games in Prague - might have done better again two minutes later after Azaz's clipped pass had caused problems for the Macedonian defence but he snatched at his attempt and fired high and wide.

Parrott twice had the ball in the net as time ran down but an offside flag stalled his celebrations on each occasion.

Ireland were unfortunate not to take the lead with 52 minutes gone when Azaz accepted Seamus Coleman's pass and found Parrott, who turned smartly before shooting against the upright.

Azaz curled an effort just wide and Tihomir Kostadinov denied Parrott a clear run on goal as the hosts began to turn the screw but it was veteran Coleman's 61st-minute departure as

Hallgrimsson made changes which attracted the biggest cheer of the night to that point.

Wholesale changes did not help the flow of the game, which rather petered out as the whistle approached, although Ireland substitute Johnny Kenny passed up a glorious opportunity to win it at the end with a weak shot at the keeper.

Sports.title: Szmodics out of hospital and 'on the mend' after collision
Sports.content:
Republic of Ireland forward Sammie Szmodics has been released from hospital in Prague after being knocked unconscious during Thursday's World Cup play-off defeat by the Czech Republic.

The 24-year-old, who is currently on loan at Derby from Ipswich, was hurt in a collision with defender Stepan Chaloupek just two minutes after his introduction as an extra-time substitute at the Fortuna Arena, sparking concerned medics to rush to his aid.

Szmodics was carried from the field on a stretcher and taken straight to hospital, where Ireland head coach Heimir Hallgrimsson later revealed he would spend the night under observation.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Danyal Khan looks back on the heartbreaking result for the Republic of Ireland who lost their World Cup qualifying play-off against Czech Republic on penalties

A Football Association of Ireland spokesperson said on Friday morning: "Sammie Szmodics was transferred to hospital yesterday having sustained a head injury during extra time of the play-off against Czechia.

"Following further tests and a period of observation, he has been safely discharged from hospital and will continue his recovery under the care of the Republic of Ireland and Derby County medical teams."

Szmodics, who Hallgrimsson confirmed would have taken a penalty in the shoot-out which Ireland ultimately lost 4-3, took to social media to express his thanks to those who had helped him.

He posted on X: "Gutted the way it ended. Fans and boys immense all evening!! Appreciate everyone's messages. And thank you to the medical staff who acted so quickly to help me. On the mend."
