World.title: Costa Rica’s Romería Closes With Zero Deaths and 1,772 Medical Cases
World.content:
Costa Rica’s Romería closed without a single reported death, ending a nine-day emergency operation in which the Costa Rican Red Cross treated 1,772 people along the roads into Cartago and moved 34 of them to hospitals. The count covers July 25 through August 2, the feast day of the Virgen de los Ángeles, and it climbed steadily through the final Sunday.

At midday the Red Cross reported 1,681 people treated — 1,477 medical cases, 164 trauma injuries and three burns — with 31 transfers to medical centers, of which 20 were classified urgent, six critical and five stable. The 1,772 figure released Sunday evening is the most recent tally and remains provisional until the institution issues its close-out report.

Milena Bogantes, regional operational sub-coordinator for the Red Cross, reviewed the pattern of cases as the operation wound down. Before the walking began, the organization had said the emergencies it sees most often on this route are heat-related illness and blood pressure episodes, and it had asked pilgrims to hydrate, wear broken-in shoes and reflective clothing, and carry any prescription medication with them. In the earliest cuts of the operation, most patients were over 40, with the single largest group aged 61 and up.

The scale of the response is hard to overstate. The Red Cross fielded more than 850 responders and over 145 emergency vehicles across eight aid stations strung between San Pedro, on the eastern edge of San José, and the Basílica de Nuestra Señora de los Ángeles. The busiest posts were at the basilica itself, at Ochomogo and at La Galera, with smaller volumes recorded at El Cristo, Conventillos and San Pedro.

Raúl Rivera Bonilla, director general of the Fuerza Pública, said officers seized small quantities of drugs and weapons over the course of the operation. Around 500 officers were assigned to the corridor from La Sabana to Cartago during the heaviest days, working alongside roughly 150 Traffic Police officers, municipal police units and a network of surveillance cameras along the route. Authorities have not announced charges arising from the seizures, and the Fuerza Pública said it would keep its deployment in place through Monday.

Mario Redondo, the mayor of Cartago, said municipal crews recovered 13 dogs found abandoned along the pilgrimage route and took them to the city’s animal care center, where they will receive veterinary attention and, where appropriate, be neutered. Redondo put the total municipal and interinstitutional deployment at roughly 3,000 people across police forces, the Red Cross and sanitation crews, and said they collected more than 34 metric tons (37 short tons) of solid waste.

The pilgrimage itself is a walk of about 22 kilometers (14 miles) from central San José to Cartago, though many people set out from far greater distances and walk for days. Church estimates put participation across the period at close to two million, and this year’s program carried additional weight as the centenary of the Virgin’s pontifical coronation, granted by Pope Pius XI in April 1926. The 2025 operation, by comparison, ended with 2,196 people treated, 47 transferred to medical centers and no deaths.

The observance is not quite finished. The traditional Pasada takes place Monday at 9 a.m., when the image of the Virgin is carried from the basilica to the Catedral Nuestra Señora del Carmen through streets covered in flower and sawdust carpets, accompanied by bands, mascaradas, oxcarts and boyeros. Roads through central Cartago close for the procession, and nine schools along the route switched to at-home learning for the day, returning to classrooms Tuesday. Anyone driving through the Cartago canton center Monday morning should expect closures and delays until the procession finishes and traffic is restored.

Since Costa Rica has just over five million people, moving a crowd on that scale along public highways for nine days and finishing with no fatalities is the number the institutions involved will point to. The operation has been refined over decades of repetition, and the outcome reflects that: the traffic plan staged months in advance, aid posts placed where the walking gets hardest, and thousands of volunteers standing on the shoulder of a highway at three in the morning handing out water.

World.title: CONCACAF Calls for Reckoning With Infantino’s FIFA Leadership
World.content:
North and Central American football’s governing body CONCACAF yesterday called for a “comprehensive reckoning with” Gianni Infantino’s leadership of FIFA after his aborted plan to allow private investment in the World Cup. “This recent unilateral and egregious act of poor governance and leadership follows a pattern of missteps and similar behavior,” CONCACAF said in a statement.

“A comprehensive reckoning with this presidency is imperative.” Last week, world governing body FIFA had announced plans to create a commercial subsidiary which would run its biggest events, including the World Cup and Club World Cup. This body would be open to minority private investment, under a plan which Infantino said would “turbocharge the development of the game globally” by raising up to $4.2 billion.

On Friday, facing a fierce global backlash, Infantino pulled the plug on the plan. CONCACAF, which includes all three co-hosts of the recently concluded 2026 World Cup — the United States, Canada and Mexico — as well as Caribbean associations, yesterday welcomed the decision to scrap the divisive proposal.

It joined European organization UEFA in criticizing Infantino’s actions and expressing doubt over his suitability to continue in the role. “This concern is not CONCACAF’s alone. It is shared across many confederations, Member Associations and those who serve and love the game,” said the statement.

In defending his initial proposal, Infantino had said that it could provide each of FIFA’s 211 member associations with a one-off payment of $20 million in early 2027 and increase their funding allocation for the 2027-2030 cycle from $8 million to $20 million. But the CONCACAF statement noted that FIFA already has “vast reserves,” and said that its members would push for those finances to be disbursed “for football development across our region, without compromising our shared future.”

Infantino’s plan had “advanced outside every established governance framework, without transparency, consultation or due process,” it said. “A proposal of this magnitude does not reach that stage by accident. It is a symptom of leadership that has stopped putting football first.”

World.title: Belize Police Department concludes 27th annual Police youth cadet corp summer camp
World.content:
Belize Police Department concludes 27th annual Police youth cadet corp summer camp

By Zoila Palma: The Belize Police Department concluded the 27th Annual National Police Youth Cadet Corps Summer Camp 2026 in Dangriga.

The youth cadet corps summer camp was a transformative week-long program that brought together 279 cadet members and 80 police and civilian instructors from across the country, including the Cayes.

The camp was held at Ecumenical High School Campus in Dangriga Town, from Saturday, July 25, to Saturday, August 1.

The camp embodied this year’s theme, “Command with Honor, Inspire Action, Teaching Young Minds for a Successful Tomorrow.”

The official featured addresses by Commissioner of Police Dr. Richard Rosado; Sr. Supt. Gerald Jones; Supt. Elroy Carcamo (Campground Commander); and other distinguished officials.

Sponsors and cadets received certificates of participation and appreciation, followed by a ceremonial march through the principal streets of Dangriga Town accompanied by the Belize Police Department Marching Band.

The Belize Police Department reaffirmed its unwavering commitment to strengthening the National Police Youth Cadet Corps and investing in the nation’s greatest resource—its youth.

World.title: UDP hosts party convention in Twin Towns, selects 5 councillor candidates for municipal elections
World.content:
UDP hosts party convention in Twin Towns, selects 5 councillor candidates for municipal elections

By Breaking Belize News Staff: On August 2, 2026, the United Democratic Party (UDP) selected its five councillor candidates as it gears up for municipal elections in San Ignacio and Santa Elena Town.

The party convention was held in the Twin Towns.

Lin Valentine secured the highest number of votes with 555, followed by Abdel Cowo with 429, Tosh Lanza with 411, Illiana Moreno with 379, and Kim Price with 349.

The five emerged victorious from eight candidates vying for spots on the party’s municipal slate.

The elected councillor candidates will now join mayoral candidate Earl Trapp and Councillor Leader Bernadette Fernandez to complete the UDP’s ticket for the upcoming municipal elections.

Following the convention, the UDP expressed gratitude to its candidates, delegates, volunteers.

World.title: Belize City Council hosts successful Ebo Town Festival 2026
World.content:
Belize City Council hosts successful Ebo Town Festival 2026

By Zoila Palma: On August 1, 2026, in celebration of Emancipation Day, the Belize City Council and partners hosted Ebo Town fest 2026.

It was a day filled with cultural entertainment, education, and community spirit, celebrating our heritage, reflecting on our history, and strengthening the bonds that define Belize City.

The festival featured beloved Belizean dishes and proudly showcased the African traditions deeply woven into our cultural identity.

The Belize City Council extended gratitude to the National Celebrations Commission and the National Institute of Culture and History for their invaluable collaboration and support in making this event possible.

The Council says that it remains committed to supporting events that preserve our culture, educate future generations, and provide meaningful opportunities for residents to connect.

World.title: Beach, rainforest or culture? In Belize the answer is yes
World.content:
Beach, rainforest or culture? In Belize the answer is yes

By Breaking Belize News Staff (HP): Every vacation begins with the same argument. The beach people want salt and sun. The adventure people want jungle and adrenaline. The culture people want food, music, and history you can touch. In most of the world, somebody loses that argument. In Belize, nobody does, because this small country delivers all three, often in the same week, sometimes in the same day.

Start with the beach, because the Caribbean here makes an unanswerable opening statement. The Belize Barrier Reef, second largest on Earth, runs the length of the coast, turning the sea into a living aquarium for snorkelers, divers, and fly-fishers. On the Placencia Peninsula, the beach vacation reaches its finest form at Chabil Mar Villas, the award-winning, guest-exclusive resort where the water begins where the veranda ends, and the hardest decision of the day is hammock or pool.

Then turn inland, where the second Belize waits under the canopy. The west is rainforest country, rivers, caves, waterfalls, and the ancient Maya sites that crown it all. Base yourself at Villa Massis Resort on the banks of the Mopan River near San Ignacio, and the jungle chapter organizes itself: Xunantunich and its towering El Castillo one day, Cahal Pech the next, the legendary ATM Cave for the brave, and the river itself for the lazy golden afternoons in between. Good food, good vibes, and howler monkeys for an alarm clock.

And through it all runs the third Belize, the one that lives in people rather than places. This is a nation of cultures side by side: Garifuna drumming and hudut on the southern coast, Maya villages where chocolate is still made from bean to bar, Mestizo towns fragrant with escabeche and corn, Creole rice and beans perfected in every kitchen, and market mornings in San Ignacio where the whole tapestry shops together. Cultural immersion here is not a scheduled excursion. It is simply what happens when you talk to people.

The practicalities seal the case. Belize speaks English, pegs its dollar two to one to the US dollar, and has never been easier to reach, with a record 1.4 million visitors, new nonstop routes connecting five more American cities this winter, and Canadian service growing from three cities. The world is discovering what a single small country can hold.

The only real challenge is logistics, stitching reef, rainforest, and culture into one seamless trip, and that is a solved problem too: Barefoot Services in Placencia, local travel experts who live the destination daily, build the whole route, transfers, tours, and hidden gems included.

So bring the beach people, the adventure people, and the culture people on the same plane. Belize ends the argument the only way worth ending it: everybody wins.

World.title: ‘Kimmy Boo’, in this trimester of pregnancy, found dead in advanced state of decomposition
World.content:
‘Kimmy Boo’, in this trimester of pregnancy, found dead in advanced state of decomposition

By Breaking Belize News Staff: Police are investigating the sudden death of 22-year-old Kimane Rosita Ashanti Garbutt, a pregnant woman also publicly known as “Kimmy Boo,” whose body was discovered inside an upstairs room in Belize City on Sunday morning.

Police were called to a building at the corner of Vernon Street and Amandala Drive at about 9:30 a.m. on August 2. Upon arriving, officers met a 44-year-old man, who escorted them to a room on the upper floor.

Inside, police found Garbutt’s motionless body in a seated position in a corner of the room. Her body was reportedly already in an advanced state of decomposition.

Moore told investigators that he went to check on Garbutt at about 9:00 that morning but found the door to the upstairs room locked. He forced the door open, found her motionless and immediately contacted police.

According to the police report, Garbutt had suffered from epileptic seizures for several years. She was also in the third trimester of pregnancy and had reportedly been experiencing complications. She had visited the Karl Heusner Memorial Hospital for a prenatal check-up approximately two weeks before her death.

Garbutt was last seen alive at about 7:00 a.m. on Saturday, August 1. At the time, she told him that she was not feeling well.

Garbutt had previously received public attention under the name “Kimmy Boo” through several Magistrate’s Court appearances. In October 2025, she pleaded guilty to a theft charge and was fined, and in December 2025, she was fined after pleading guilty to common assault.

Her body was transported to the National Forensic Science Service laboratory, where it awaits a post-mortem examination. The cause of death has not yet been determined, and police investigations continue.

World.title: Pregnant young woman found dead in Belize City room
World.content:
Pregnant young woman found dead in Belize City room

By Breaking Belize News Staff (HP): A death investigation is underway in Belize City after a 21-year-old woman, in the third trimester of pregnancy, was found lifeless in an upstairs room, with a post mortem examination expected to determine how she died.

According to the Belize Police Department, information of a sudden death was received at about 9:30 a.m. on Sunday, August 2, 2026, directing police to a location at the corner of Vernon Street and Amandala Drive.

On arrival, officers met a 44-year-old man who escorted them to a room on the upper floor of a building, where they observed the motionless body of a young woman seated at a corner of the room. She appeared to have passed some time before she was found. The deceased was identified as a 21-year-old domestic of the area.

The man reported that at about 9:00 a.m. that morning, he went to check on the young woman and found the door to the upstairs room locked. He forced the door open to gain entry, and upon seeing her motionless, immediately called the police.

The circumstances of her health add layers of sorrow to the investigation. The young woman had been suffering from epileptic seizures for several years, and was in the third trimester of pregnancy with complications, having last been seen by medical personnel at the Karl Heusner Memorial Hospital about two weeks earlier for a prenatal checkup.

She was last seen alive at about 7:00 a.m. on Saturday, August 1, when she informed the man that she was not feeling well.

Her body has been transported to the National Forensic Science Service laboratory, where it awaits a post mortem examination. Police have given no indication of foul play, and the matter remains under investigation, with the examination expected to establish the cause of death.

World.title: Sunny week opens for Belize while the south catches showers
World.content:
Sunny week opens for Belize while the south catches showers

By Breaking Belize News Staff (HP): The new work week begins under mostly sunny skies for Belize, with the familiar August heat reaching 95 degrees inland, though the south stands as the exception, catching a few more shower and thunderstorm outbreaks through the morning and again late at night.

According to the National Meteorological Service, a light to moderate easterly airflow prevails. Skies will be sunny today with a few cloudy spells, turning partly cloudy tonight and becoming cloudy at times, especially over the south. Showers or thunderstorms will be isolated, except for the south, where a few more outbreaks can be expected during the morning hours and late at night.

Temperatures along the coast will reach a high of 89 degrees Fahrenheit (32 Celsius) and a low of 82 (28 Celsius). Inland areas will be the hottest, climbing to 95 degrees Fahrenheit (35 Celsius) before dropping to 74 (23 Celsius). In the hills, expect a high of 83 degrees Fahrenheit (28 Celsius) and a low of 68 (20 Celsius). With the mercury holding at 95 inland, hydration and shade breaks remain the order of the working day.

At sea, conditions stay gentle, with easterly winds of 10 to 15 knots, a light chop, and waves of 2 to 4 feet.

On the tropical front, the calm continues. Tropical cyclone formation is not expected in the region over the next 48 hours.

Looking ahead to Tuesday and Tuesday night, skies will be partly cloudy to cloudy at times, with showers and thunderstorms staying isolated, except over the south, where a few more can be expected.

Today’s low tides are at 7:08 AM and 7:17 PM, with a high tide at 1:02 PM and another high at 1:18 AM tomorrow. The sun rose at 5:32 AM and will set at 6:24 PM. The forecast was issued by forecaster Catherine Cumberbatch.

World.title: ‘War With Me And The Mother-In-Law’: Man charged with trying to light mother-in-law’s house on fire with her in it
World.content:
‘War With Me And The Mother-In-Law’: Man charged with trying to light mother-in-law’s house on fire with her in it

By Breaking Belize News Staff: A 22-year-old construction worker accused of deliberately setting fires inside his former mother-in-law’s Belize City home has pleaded not guilty to two counts of arson in the High Court.

Sir Hugh Anthony Andrewin appeared unrepresented before Justice Nigel Pilgrim this week, where he was formally indicted on the two charges.

Justice Pilgrim strongly advised Andrewin to obtain an attorney, telling him that the allegations against him were “very serious offences.” The judge gave him approximately three months to seek legal representation and adjourned the matter until November 13, 2026.

Andrewin was further remanded to the Belize Central Prison, as he also has other pending matters before the Belize City Magistrate’s Court for which he remains on remand.

The charges arise from two alleged incidents at a home on Flamboyant Street on June 11 and June 12, 2025.

Police allege that at about 10:00 p.m. on June 11, Andrewin arrived at the residence of his now former mother-in-law, pulled out a blue lighter and set fire to a sheet covering a grey loveseat valued at $400. The woman reportedly extinguished the fire before it could spread further.

Several hours later, at about 4:00 a.m. on June 12, the woman and her daughter were reportedly awakened by smoke and found a curtain and a green loveseat valued at $750 engulfed in flames. The fire also damaged aluminium louvre windows valued at $495.

The prosecution alleges that the second fire was set with the intention of endangering both women. Andrewin initially faced one arson charge in the Magistrate’s Court but was indicted on two counts when the matter reached the High Court.

World.title: Wheatley granted injunction barring IC charges until judicial review
World.content:
Andrew Wheatley

The Supreme Court has granted an injunction preventing the Integrity Commission (IC) from charging Cabinet Minister Dr Andrew Wheatley until the hearing and determination of an application by his lawyers for judicial review.

Wheatley had applied for leave to pursue judicial review against the IC’s recommendation that he be charged with illicit enrichment.

Observer Online understands that the Supreme Court on Friday granted Wheatley’s application, recommending that the judicial review be heard by a panel of three judges.

Before granting the injunction, presiding Judge Justice David Batts had suggested that the IC consider an undertaking not to charge Dr Wheatley until the hearing and determination of the judicial review.

The commission said it could not give an undertaking at this time. The judge then granted the injunction.

It is understood that the IC’s application for leave to appeal the ruling was denied.

The Integrity Commission had alleged that there is a disproportionality in Wheatley’s assets when compared to his income to the tune of $164 million.

Wheatley rejected the allegation and accused the IC of failing to take into consideration $168 million in rental income accumulated over a decade.

He is being represented by a high powered legal team including King’s Counsel Ransford Braham, Abe Dabdoub and Neco Pagon.

The Integrity Commission is being represented by King’s Counsel Kevin Powell.

World.title: DROUGHT ALERT!
World.content:
Principal Director of the Meteorological Service of Jamaica, Evan Thompson gives the forecast for the island over the next few months during a press briefing Thursday afternoon.(Photo: Karl McLarty)

With projections from the Meteorological Service of Jamaica showing prolonged dry conditions stretching into October this year, Water, Environment and Climate Change Minister Matthew Samuda has put Jamaicans on alert for full prohibition orders for water usage, which he says will take effect on August 10 if the forecast remains unchanged or worsens.

The warning comes following a Thursday morning meeting of the Integrated Water Resources Management Council — a Cabinet subcommittee comprising all stakeholders in the water sector; academia; municipalities; and the ministries of agriculture, health and national security. That report was complemented by forecasts of the Met Service and assessments of the Water Resources Authority, according to Samuda.

Since earlier this year, nightly water restrictions and scheduled supply cuts have been implemented in vulnerable Corporate Area networks, such as Kingston 20, given the drought conditions.

Speaking during a media briefing at the Half-Way-Tree Road offices of his ministry to discuss the rainfall and drought conditions, Samuda said given the indications that there will be “a dry August, a dry September, and a dry October…it is clear and should be clear to all Jamaicans that conservation is indeed imperative at this stage”.

“We are first encouraging conservation, but being very clear that as at August 10th…if the situation has not changed — meaning if the Met Services evaluation of rainfall in July is as we suspect — that we will have continued declines in rainfall, and if the rolling three-month forecast has not changed, or has worsened, prohibition orders will come into effect,” Samuda said.

The water minister said those orders will be targeted at “irrigation and watering of gardens, lawns, grounds, and farms, filling or supplying of pools, and other things for domestic services”.

“Washing of cars, watering and washing of roadways, and any purpose that would require unusual or non-essential use of water would be prohibited,” Samuda added.

He emphasised that the announcement was not to be interpreted to mean “that the systems and the storage are at critical levels today, but the rainfall that would normally come at the end of August is not projected to be experienced”.

Pointing to the learning loss that has already resulted from the COVID-19 pandemic as well as weather events such as Hurricane Beryl, Tropical Storm Raphael, and Hurricane Melissa, the minister said every effort will be made to ensure that schools receive the support needed.

“We simply cannot afford water to contribute to learning loss in September. So we will take the measures that we absolutely need to ensure that we’re able to safeguard the opening of schools in September and not contribute to learning loss. So that needs to be understood. We do hope that the situation will change, but with the information that we have, this is the best decision that we can make at this stage,” Samuda stressed.

“We do hope that the situation will change, but with the information that we have, this is the best decision that we can make at this stage,” he added.

Speaking during the briefing, principal director of the Meteorological Service of Jamaica Evan Thompson said as at the end of June the parishes of St Elizabeth, St James, St Ann, and St Mary “were determined to be experiencing drought conditions”. He said the parishes of Manchester and St Catherine “were both basically on the borderline, in that they were just about moving toward drought conditions”.

“It’s most likely that having not experienced significant rainfall during the month of July, that situation would have been worsened. We should be seeing that drought conditions at least would have extended to these two parishes. That’s what we’re expecting to pick up after the month of July has ended, as we begin to gather and collate and compare our data,” Thompson told members of the media.

He noted that the projections did not mean there would be “no rainfall” at all for the island, but that “the number of incidents of rainfall will be fewer”, influenced by the El Nino phenomenon which has caused “lesser than normal amounts of rainfall and higher than normal temperatures” over the past few months.

“However, we could have a bulk of rainfall that is intense, and so we could have very small areas that experience maybe even flooding events in small areas as these systems develop and as they continue to affect us, but generally we will experience dry conditions,” Thompson explained further.

He cautioned that with the forecast for August showing “higher-than-normal temperatures right through the month” and “lower-than-normal rainfall”, Jamaicans should be on the lookout for “climate-induced bushfires”.

World.title: More for MSMEs
World.content:
WILLIAMS... it is a catalyst for the next era of public procurement in Jamaica.

ONLY about one per cent of the Government’s annual procurement spending currently reaches micro, small, and medium-sized enterprises (MSMEs), a disparity Finance Minister Fayval Williams says the upgraded Government of Jamaica Electronic Procurement portal (GOJEP 2.0) is intended to address. The platform will increase MSME access to public contracts.

Speaking during Thursday’s launch of the updated digital procurement portal, Williams said the modernised system eliminates outdated technical requirements, and creates more opportunities for local businesses to access a share of the Government’s roughly $470-billion annual procurement spend.

“Let me put the scale in perspective. Each year, the Government of Jamaica spends roughly US$3 billion — translated into Jamaican dollars, that’s about $470 billion, depending on the currency at any point in time – and this procures goods, services, and works from the private sector. This is close to, I think, about 13 per cent of our GDP (gross domestic product). And yet, of that enormous sum, only about one per cent reaches our micro, small, and medium-sized enterprises,” the minister pointed out.

“That imbalance is exactly what we are determined to correct so that more Jamaican businesses can share in the billions that Government spends each year, particularly as we rebuild in the wake of Hurricane Melissa. So every procurement decision carries real responsibility. It must inspire public confidence, deliver value for money, create economic opportunity, and make certain that every dollar entrusted to Government works harder for the people we serve,” she said during the event held at AC Hotel Kingston.

According to Williams, GOJEP 2.0 is an upgraded version of the Government’s online system for buying goods, works and services from the private sector. She explained that the remodelling of the digital portal will see the removal of outdated barriers, put in place stronger record keeping aimed at making the process faster and more transparent.

“It’s easier to use. You no longer need to install extra software just to submit a bid. You log in from any ordinary web browser on any device, including your phone. It’s better connected. The system now talks to other government systems, so the same information doesn’t have to be entered twice, it keeps a proper record digitally,” explained the minister.

“Every key decision made during evaluation is captured and tracked automatically instead of living in a paper file or in someone’s memory. It cuts duplicate paperwork for government staff, and it collects far better data on how long procurements take, how much competition is there, and how well our small business set-asides are working,” Williams added.

She also pointed out that bidders and buyers will now be able to follow opportunities that the government brings to market, and see who ultimately wins the work. Furthermore, she assured that GOJEP 2.0 was not the finished product, noting that upgrades will continue overtime.

“It is a catalyst for the next era of public procurement in Jamaica. And, over the next years, we will build a fully integrated end-to-end digital procurement system, one that connects planning, tendering, evaluation, contract management, supplier performance, and payment.

“Imagine in a year or two being able to open GOJEP and see the goods, works, and services that government intends to buy over the coming years. A business could then prepare, assess its capacity, build partnerships, secure certification, arrange financing, and position itself to compete. For our MSMEs especially, that advanced visibility can be the difference between watching from the sidelines and winning the work,” said the finance minister.

Meanwhile, Chief Public Procurement Policy Officer Jovell Barrett also highlighted the gap that exists for MSMEs, pointing out that of the 300,000 active businesses registered with the Companies Office of Jamaica, less than 10,000 unique people and entities are awarded government contracts each year.

“Government is one of the largest purchasers of goods, works and services. And so, the question that we have asked ourselves at the Office of Public Procurement Policy is how many Jamaican businesses see government as a potential customer? How many entrepreneurs look to the public procurement system as an opportunity? And perhaps most importantly, how many do not see public procurement as an opportunity — and if they don’t, why?” said Barrett.

He hailed Thursday’s launch of GOJEP 2.0 as an opportunity to ensure that every taxpaying Jamaican has a fair chance to participate in the public procurement process.

“That’s the vision that I have and that’s what I want to see as a Jamaican. Why? I want to see more Jamaicans participating in public procurement. When public procurement operates as I want to see it happen… small businesses, hundreds and thousands of them in each community, [will] become a mechanism through which public procurement will work best and will be able to develop our economy more. It becomes the instrument of change that Government really wants it to be. That is the power of public procurement,” he said.

World.title: Dexta Daps stays true
World.content:
Dexta Daps.

As thousands of patrons prepare to descend on Montego Bay for Dream Wknd, few performers arrive with the kind of anticipation that surrounds Dexta Daps.

Over the past decade the dancehall star has built one of the genre’s most devoted followings by staying true to the soulful, emotionally driven sound that first set him apart.

“Staying true to the vibe that started my career and keeping the music honest and relatable,” he says when asked about the secret to his longevity. “I evolve with the production sounds, but I don’t chase trends; solid melodies, real emotion, and a performance that connects with the audience is always the goal.”

In a genre that constantly reinvents itself, Dexta Daps has remained relevant by refining his craft rather than reinventing his identity. As production styles and audience tastes have evolved, he has focused on strengthening the qualities that first resonated with listeners.

His creative process, however, has never stood still.

“It’s ever-evolving,” he explains. “I’ve continued to sharpen my sense of arrangement and storytelling while balancing intimate, soulful moments with the dancehall energy.”

That balance has become one of his defining trademarks. Whether delivering emotionally charged ballads or high-energy dancehall records, he has demonstrated an ability to connect with audiences on multiple levels, creating music that feels both deeply personal and widely relatable.

As with any artiste whose career has spanned several years, thoughts inevitably turn to legacy. For Dexta Daps, the impact he leaves extends far beyond chart success or hit records.

“If fans only remembered one thing about my career years from now,” he says, “I’d want it to be that I gave people real, heartfelt music that resonated beyond the dance songs, music that felt honest and performances that stayed with them.”

That same commitment to delivering memorable performances is what fans can expect when he takes the stage at Dream Wknd, one of the Caribbean’s premier entertainment festivals, which runs from July 30-August 3 this year.

Sharing the stage with Dexta Daps at Dream’s Montego Bay debut are some of the biggest names in dancehall, including Alkaline, Tommy Lee, Govana, Shaneil Muir, Tifa, Elephant Man, General B, Jamal, Skeng, and Armanii, alongside a number of international acts.

“It’s always great to share the stage with so much talent,” he says. “It’s about representing the culture well and keeping the energy high for the crowd. I don’t take that for granted.”

While he remains tight-lipped about exactly what fans can expect, he hints that patrons should be prepared for something special.

“Always a few surprises,” he says with a laugh. “However, I can’t reveal them because then it wouldn’t be a surprise.”

Looking beyond the summer, Dexta Daps’s focus remains firmly on creating new music while continuing to expand his reach internationally.

“More music, working on an album,” he responds.

So, with new music, an album in the works, and another Dream Wknd appearance on the horizon, Dexta Daps is continuing to build a career rooted in authenticity, one heartfelt performance at a time.

World.title: DOLPHIN COVE’S US$2.5-M LIFT
World.content:
Visitors interact with dolphins at one of Dolphin Cove Limited’s Jamaican attractions. The company has added approximately US$2.53 million to its net book value following a revaluation of its Jamaican properties

DOLPHIN Cove Limited has added approximately US$2.533 million to its net book value after revaluing its Jamaican properties, an adjustment disclosed while its majority shareholder has agreed to sell its controlling stake and is seeking to add four directors.

Property Consultants Limited valued the group’s Jamaican land and buildings as at March 31, but its report reached Dolphin Cove’s board after the company had published its first-quarter financial statements.

The appraisal increases the carrying value of property, plant and equipment by approximately US$2.576 million. After adjustments to deferred taxation, the net increase in Dolphin Cove’s book value is approximately US$2.533 million.

Applied to the previously reported March figures, the adjustment would lift property, plant and equipment from approximately US$26.65 million to US$29.23 million and shareholders’ equity from US$27.39 million to approximately US$29.92 million, before any other second-quarter movements.

The increase is equivalent to approximately nine per cent of the equity Dolphin Cove reported at the end of March.

It is an accounting adjustment rather than new income or cash. Dolphin Cove said the revaluation has no effect on revenue, operating results or cash flow for the period.

The revised values will be reflected in the company’s financial statements for the six months ended June 30.

Dolphin Cove did not identify the individual Jamaican properties covered by the appraisal, disclose their separate values or say whether the updated figures were considered in the proposed sale of the company’s controlling stake.

The transaction under way is a sale of shares in Dolphin Cove rather than a direct sale of the properties.

World of Dolphins Inc agreed on July 9 to sell all 313,901,858 Dolphin Cove shares it owns to Global Attractions Limited, a Saint Lucia company incorporated in March. The shares represent 79.99 per cent of Dolphin Cove.

Neither the purchase price nor the expected completion date has been disclosed. Completion is subject to conditions, including arrangements for the refinancing and discharge of Dolphin Cove’s existing credit facility with Sagicor Bank Jamaica Limited. The beneficial owners of Global Attractions, its financing arrangements and its plans for Dolphin Cove also remain unknown.

The property adjustment has now been announced as World of Dolphins seeks to add four directors to the listed company’s board.

The majority shareholder has nominated Colin Kerr, Darys Estrella, Alberto Bergés González and Sylvain Dominici for election, according to a notice signed by World of Dolphins representative and Dolphin Cove director Steven Strom.

Dolphin Cove has not published biographies of the nominees, explained their connections to World of Dolphins or said whether any of them is associated with Global Attractions.

It also has not explained why the selling shareholder is seeking to expand the board before the ownership transaction is completed.

The nominations were scheduled for consideration at Dolphin Cove’s annual general meeting on Thursday, July 30, at The Courtleigh Hotel & Suites.

However, the chairman was expected to seek shareholders’ consent to adjourn the meeting to allow investors at least 14 days’ notice of the proposed appointments. The outcome was unavailable at press time.

If shareholders approve the adjournment, the resumed meeting would be held between August 13 and August 28. The exact date has not been announced.

Based on Dolphin Cove’s latest public disclosures, electing all four nominees would expand its five-member board to nine if the present directors remain in office.

World of Dolphins currently holds enough shares to determine the outcome of the elections if it votes its 79.99 per cent stake. That could change if the sale is completed or the voting rights are transferred before the adjourned meeting.

Once completed, the acquisition will trigger a mandatory offer allowing minority shareholders to sell their shares to the new controlling owner. The price and other terms have not been published.

Dolphin Cove said its properties in Saint Lucia and the Turks and Caicos Islands will also be revalued. It did not say when those appraisals would be completed or whether it expects them to increase or reduce the assets’ carrying values.

World.title: ‘He who has the gold’
World.content:
FIFA President Gianni Infantino (centre) addresses a round table press briefing at the end of the FIFA Executive Summit at the Montego Bay Convention Centre in St James in January 2018. Also pictured are Jamaica Football Federation (JFF) President Michael Ricketts (left) and Concacaf President Victor Montagliani.

Veteran administrator Tony James says FIFA President Gianni Infantino’s proposal to privatise world football is “underhanded”, but cautions that developing nations under severe financial stress will find the promised US$40-million payout nearly impossible to resist.

James, who led the Jamaica Football Federation (JFF) from 1985 to 1992 and has spent over 50 years working in football, offered a sharp critique of Infantino’s proposed FIFA Forward Enterprise (FFE). Under the plan, FIFA aims to create a private commercial entity valued at US$20 billion (over $3 billion) to handle broadcasting, ticketing, sponsorship, and hospitality rights for competitions like the World Cup. Developed alongside JP Morgan, the strategy involves selling up to 21 per cent to private equity investors — led by Joshua Kushner’s firm, Thrive Eternal — to raise US$4.2 billion (roughly $665 billion) in upfront capital. Kushner is the brother of US President Donald Trump’s son-in-law, Jared Kushner.

To win over member nations, FIFA offered a substantial payout of increasing baseline development funding from US$10 million (over $1.5 billion) to US$20 million (over $3 billion) per nation for the 2027-2030 cycle. Associations could also access an additional US$20 million upfront through a new FIFA Fast Forward Programme for infrastructure, putting up to US$40 million on the table per country ahead of a September 19 deadline. Infantino, however, warned that member nations declining support would continue to receive the baseline.

While continental governing bodies have moved to block the move, James says that for smaller member associations, the financial reality takes precedence.

“It is underhanded, and the cynical view is being reinforced by the way it is being proposed now,” James told the Jamaica Observer on Thursday. “He who has the gold makes the rule. That’s how people perceive of it; that it’s the current way of the world. You’re trumping (pardon the pun) institutionalised good governance structures, integrity, etcetera. That’s what’s being put out in the public now.”

Despite the governance concerns, James says smaller associations operate in a vastly different financial reality than European giants.

“This US$40 million for each affiliate will have traction in all the poorer and developing countries,” he said. “The focus will be on CAF [Confederation of African Football], and Concacaf, which includes the Caribbean, but it’s also the poorer countries in Asia and UEFA.

“UEFA’s principled position is understandable, but it’s fortunate in having three financial platforms. One is the World Cup, like everybody else, and their teams are the top of the heap. Let us call them Category A teams because they’re the ones who are going to get most of the money. All of the rest of us are Category B and C teams that should get money, but not like the A teams.”

James’s comments come as global opposition to Infantino’s scheme reaches a boiling point. After an emergency meeting, Concacaf — the governing body for North America, Central America, and the Caribbean — unanimously voted down the proposed enterprise plan, joining European governing body UEFA in open revolt. Concacaf made its announcement moments after the Observer’s interview with James.

In its official statement, Concacaf mentioned severe procedural failures surrounding the proposal.

“During the meeting, the membership expressed deep concerns about the lack of due process surrounding the proposal, the artificially short deadline imposed, and the absence of any review or approval by the relevant FIFA governance bodies,” Concacaf said on its website. “In addition, the need for private equity investment to fund new and existing FIFA Forward programmes following the most profitable FIFA World Cup in history was questioned.”

Concacaf confirmed all 41 member associations rejected the deal after UEFA’s warning that it would pull its teams from FIFA competitions entirely.

“As a result of today’s discussion, no UEFA national teams will participate in any FIFA competition for so long as these proposals remain alive, unless this proposal has been abandoned in its entirety and binding assurances have been given that FIFA will never again open its governance or competitions to private ownership,” UEFA said on its website on Thursday.

Despite Concacaf’s joint rejection, local sentiments reflect exactly what James described.

JFF President Michael Ricketts rejected all of the Observer’s calls to him seeking a comment, and declined to respond to questions posed on WhatsApp.

However, while speaking to Nationwide Sports, he struck a far more open tone regarding the commercial structure.

“I have not discussed it with my directors, but my personal feeling is that, on the face of it, I really don’t think that anything is wrong with it,” Ricketts said. “It’s workable. But the big problem I’m having is the — for want of a better word — non-transparent way in which it was done. We would’ve spent so much time together with the leadership of FIFA before, during, and after the World Cup, and we were never apprised of these discussions, and this would bring to the fore some level of non-transparency.”

Ricketts’s pragmatic view is tied directly to local circumstances. He told the Observer in an interview on July 14 that the JFF is strapped for cash after a costly, unsuccessful World Cup qualifying campaign. He also said in that interview that he would fully support Infantino’s plan to expand the World Cup to 64 teams as early as the 2030 tournament as it would provide a greater chance of qualification for Jamaica.

A US$40-million windfall would completely alter local operations. Furthermore, with Jamaica actively bidding to co-host the 2031 Women’s World Cup with the US, Mexico, and Costa Rica, maintaining good relations with FIFA ahead of Infantino’s re-election bid in March remains a practical priority.

While acknowledging the lifelines that FIFA funds provide, James warned that dumping millions into unprepared administrative set-ups brings serious risks.

“Regrettably, I don’t think most developing countries have an administrative structure to deal with this kind of money. They don’t,” he said. “You also have to ask, given our system, how much of this US$40 million would actually reach football development, because human nature says when you have money, it’s about a source of power, greed, corruption, football politics, and that syphons off the money.”

And on whether Infantino’s tactics amount to using FIFA’s massive wealth to secure political survival ahead of the upcoming presidential vote, James gave a blunt assessment of how the global game operates.

“He has been a disgrace,” James said. “But in a new world where the golden rule applies, when he hits FIFA and hits the politics, what do you think they’re going to say to him? When he tells them how much he has earned off this World Cup, that the vision was his, the planning was his, what he has had to do, ‘Listen, we had problems here and there, but at the end of the day, look at what I have done for you. Look at what FIFA has done for you. Who are you going to vote for?’ What do you think is going to be the response? It’s all about performance. Let’s face it, he has performed.”

World.title: 2026 Isuzu D-MAX: Built to last
World.content:
The durability, reliability, and ability shown through the history of the Isuzu D-MAX pickup continues in 2026. (Photo: Rory Daley)

Isuzu has long been one of the darlings of the commercial vehicle sector, having built a reputation for durability, reliability, and longevity over its long history.

The D-MAX pickup is endowed with these characteristics, and for 2026 continues to be so.

EXTERIOR

The four-door cab pickup is based mostly on function rather than form. Redesigned from the ground up, Isuzu calls it their ‘Spirit of Truck’ DNA, giving the D-MAX a masculine and no-nonsense look from its wide stance and wedge-shaped body lines. However, function over form still rules, and the D-MAX uses aerodynamic integration of the lower body to boost fuel efficiency and reduce wind noise. For those wanting style, up to 18-inch wheels can be had.

INTERIOR

Inside the new spacious cabin it reflects the working nature of the D-MAX. There’s a quality impression and the presence of durability to the cabin. There’s a mixture of hard-wearing plastics, with soft-touch materials at the main points of user contact. Ergonomics is a key word, with simple large buttons for the main functions to be accessed with ease under all conditions, and feel like they’ll be working for years to come.

Storage is plentiful for those who have to work. The deep centre console will swallow important gear, as will the dual gloveboxes. Cup holders and door pockets that all can hold a 1.5-litre bottle further contribute to the ability to hold personal cargo. The D-MAX has redesigned seats with improved internal materials for higher comfort, and better lateral support to increase occupant, especially driver, comfort.

The infotainment is similarly focused, using USB-C for smartphone-run connectivity and services.

ON THE ROAD

Powered by a 3-litre turbodiesel, the D-MAX is not lacking in this area. With 190bhp and 332lb/ft of torque, it manages to be both frugal and powerful. This is because there is tons of low-end torque to effortlessly pull the D-MAX along in the situations it’s built to operate in.

Boost response is good, and it rarely has to be taken into the higher rpms for more power. On road, this keeps engine noise and vibration low so as not to upset passengers in the cabin, meaning a strong case for prolonged on-road use.

But the D-MAX didn’t get its reputation for its on-road manners. Off-road, it has the ability to match the class leaders, because it’s all under the skin with a chassis boasting greater torsional and longitudinal rigidity. The same suspension that smooths out rough roads and can deal with highway travel can easily handle tough terrain with or without payload.

Rookie or professional, the D-MAX gives confidence in challenging situations, delivering up to 800 millimetres of wading depth, 30 degrees of approach angle, 22.9 degrees of breakover, and 24.2 degrees of departure angle. Being equipped with 2WD, 4WD, and 4WD Low, plus a rear differential, few things can slow, even stop, the D-MAX on a trail.

VERDICT

The D-MAX retains the ethos of the Isuzu brand. There’s a reason the company is a commercial equipment manufacturing powerhouse, and that all is installed into their flagship pickup. The durability, reliability, and ability shown through the history of the D-MAX pickup continue without question. 2026 adds some key updates and refinements to keep it a top contender.

World.title: Poland appeals €1.3B Pfizer vaccine ruling
World.content:
Warsaw says the end of the pandemic and Russia’s invasion of Ukraine upended the deal.

Poland on Monday appealed a Brussels court judgment ordering it to take delivery of roughly 64 million unwanted Covid-19 doses and pay Pfizer about €1.3 billion. Warsaw also asked judges to freeze the ruling’s provisional enforcement while the challenge is heard.

“The decision of the court of first instance does not take into account all the relevant factual and legal circumstances of the case,” the Health Ministry said in a statement. It added that Poland would use “all legal means of defense,” but declined to disclose its arguments or evidence, citing the need to protect the state’s interests.

The ruling which Poland appealed relates to a 2021 agreement the European Commission negotiated with Pfizer on behalf of EU countries. Poland stopped accepting vaccine deliveries in 2022, citing collapsing demand and the impact of Russia's war against Ukraine. Pfizer sued Poland and Romania the following year. In April 2026, a Brussels court ruled that Warsaw remained bound by the contract and ordered it to pay roughly €1.3 billion, plus interest and legal costs, for the undelivered doses.

Pfizer defended the Belgian judgment, which it told POLITICO reflected “the importance of the contractual obligations that underpinned a successful European pandemic response, built on the principle of solidarity between Member States.” The company said it was taking “appropriate steps” to ensure compliance through “established legal enforcement mechanisms,” adding that those efforts followed “years of discussions and significant flexibility to accommodate Member States' circumstances.”

World.title: Farage needs the border to be the battle of the summer
World.content:
Under its proposals, an “integrated surveillance command” to track boats using drones, space satellites and infrared feeds would be established using the Royal Navy, Royal Air Force, Royal Marines and British Army.

Small boats would be intercepted at sea with their occupants detained, medically-assessed and given food and water before being returned on military inflatable boats to the country they came from, most likely France.

“I am entirely confident that under a Reform government, within a fortnight, there would be no more boats,” Farage — who took questions at a press conference for the first time since early May — told reporters.

“If the Royal Navy is not there to protect this country from invasion, then, frankly, I can’t see what its purpose is,” he added.

Seizing the agenda

The Reform announcement comes as the ruling Labour Party enjoys a modest bounce in opinion polls two weeks after swapping out Keir Starmer as prime minister for former Greater Manchester Mayor Andy Burnham.

Burnham has seized the agenda, announcing a flurry of spending commitments in his first fortnight in charge, and struck a more optimistic tone than his predecessor.

World.title: Zelenskyy appoints chief negotiator as head of foreign intelligence
World.content:
Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy has appointed Kyiv’s chief negotiator and former Defense Minister Rustem Umerov as head of the country’s Foreign Intelligence Service, according to a decree published by the presidential office on Monday.

Umerov’s current position as secretary of the National Security and Defense Council will be taken over by Ihor Klymenko, who was serving as minister of internal affairs, as announced in a separate presidential decree. Klymenko had been considered by lawmakers the leading candidate to replace ousted Defense Minister Mykhailo Fedorov.

Umerov’s appointment comes as part of a broader reshuffle of Ukraine’s security leadership that Zelenskyy announced in July. The overhaul included the dismissals of Fedorov, Commander-in-Chief Gen. Oleksandr Syrskyi and others. Ukraine needed “more strength” in its wartime leadership, said Zelenskyy.

Umerov will now be in charge of a broader portfolio including “diplomacy, defense, negotiations with the U.S. and other designated partners, as well as talks on ending the war,” according to Zelenskyy’s announcement. A key participant in Ukraine-Russia negotiations, Umerov will also continue overseeing work on the EU–Ukraine Drone Deal.

World.title: Paris court rejects pro-Kremlin TV star’s appeal against expulsion
World.content:
A Paris court on Monday rejected Russian television star Xenia Fedorova’s appeal against a ruling that she must leave the country, a week after French authorities accused her of acting as “a conduit for disinformation campaigns” orchestrated by Moscow to “destabilize public order.”

The former head of Kremlin-backed RT France, who has been under house arrest in Paris since Wednesday, challenged three government measures: the expulsion order, a requirement that she remain in Paris and report to police daily, and a six-month asset freeze. But an administrative court ruled she had failed to demonstrate any of these measures caused her immediate and serious harm.

The former RT France chief was a regular commentator on media platforms owned by conservative French billionaire Vincent Bolloré — including CNews and Europe 1 — where her Russia-friendly views on Ukraine, NATO and European security had come under growing scrutiny ahead of the country’s 2027 presidential election.

World.title: Von der Leyen rallies to support Spain after Ceuta crisis
World.content:
Around 50,000 people crossed into Ceuta from Morocco last week, with dozens dying in the attempt. Almost all those who entered have since returned to Morocco.

Von der Leyen on Monday praised the “swift handling” of returns by Spanish and Moroccan authorities, saying they had “successfully prevent[ed] illegal movement onwards to mainland Spain and Europe.”

The exchange followed a joint letter from 22 EU leaders at the weekend calling for an emergency meeting of interior ministers and a tougher, coordinated response to the crisis. That meeting will take place on Tuesday, with EU ambassadors discussing the situation on Monday afternoon.

The intervention by EU leaders opened a new political fight over Spain’s migration policy, including Madrid’s plan to regularize more than 1 million undocumented migrants. Some governments argued that the measure created a “pull factor” by encouraging people to believe that irregular entry could eventually lead to legal residency.

Sánchez rejected that criticism in his letter, accusing some EU countries of responding in a “selfish,” “polarizing” and unlawful manner. He argued that Spain needed European solidarity rather than blame after the deaths and the strain placed on Ceuta’s authorities. The Spanish government refused to comment for this article.

Von der Leyen’s letter offered that solidarity while making clear that the crisis would also have to prompt stronger EU action.

World.title: Spain’s politicians point finger at Morocco over Ceuta crisis
World.content:
That led many to suspect that such a large flow of people could hardly be masterminded without the acquiescence of Morocco, which claims the Spanish cities of Ceuta and Melilla as occupied territories.

Diplomatic speculation has also centered on whether Rabat could be flexing its muscles over Spain’s recent rapprochement with Algeria, which supports self-determination in Western Sahara — a territory claimed by Morocco.

“Let’s call things by their name: Morocco is using human beings to attack our sovereignty,” said Eduardo Rubiño, lawmaker with the Sánchez-allied, left-wing Más Madrid party.

Ceuta Mayor Juan Jesús Vivas from the conservative People’s Party on Monday said the situation could not be characterized as “a migration crisis” because “people have the perception that this, if not orchestrated, was encouraged or permitted” by Moroccan authorities.

Vivas conceded that Madrid had to do its utmost to continue working with Rabat, but also told Spanish newspaper El País that “Morocco has shown us that it is not reliable.”

Since the outset of the crisis, Spain’s Socialist-led government has prioritized smooth relations with Morocco, which will prove critical to resolving the crisis, rather than pinning the blame on Rabat.

World.title: France bolsters checks on ‘sensitive’ foreign investments
World.content:
Earlier this year, Lecornu asked three parliamentarians from his center-right coalition to report on France’s economic security. Obtained by POLITICO, the document called for a “radical change in posture” and urged the government to take “a holistic approach” to protecting strategic assets, securing critical supply chains, reducing dependencies and strengthening technological sovereignty.

In a press release on the threshold change, Lecornu’s office said the government would give its response on any proposed foreign investments within 10 days of notification to “avoid placing an undue burden on companies’ ability to raise capital in financial markets.”

The move is intended to “guard against opportunistic acquisitions by non-EU investors in French companies listed outside the EU that could pose risks to national security,” the statement noted.

France had previously set up a screening process for planned acquisitions of over 10 percent of shares in French companies listed on European markets during Covid-19, with the stated aim of “protecting strategic companies” in a time of crisis. The measure was later made permanent and is now being extended to French companies listed outside the EU.

The new rules will come into effect in the coming days.

Other EU countries, such as Germany and Spain, have similar foreign investment screening regimes that apply a 10 percent threshold to acquisitions in certain strategic sectors.

Paul de Villepin contributed to this report.

World.title: Iran signals no immediate U.S. talks after Trump says negotiations to resume
World.content:
U.S. President Donald Trump said negotiations with Iran would resume Monday, after scrapping a planned military strike over the weekend. Speaking on Sunday, the American leader also refused to set a deadline for reaching a broader deal with Tehran.

“They knew the extent of the attack because they saw it forming. Now what we’re doing is we’re talking to them in the form of a negotiation. It begins tomorrow afternoon, and we’ll see,” said Trump, talking to reporters aboard Air Force One.

Asked whether he had imposed a deadline, the U.S. president responded: “Would I rather make a deal? I’m not looking to kill people because people die, a lot of people die, and we don’t want that.”

Trump’s remarks came on the heels of his early Sunday announcement on Truth Social that the U.S. was shelving a “massive attack,” after Iran and several Middle Eastern countries asked Washington to pause military action while negotiators worked toward an agreement. He said the framework under discussion included the “Immediate, Complete, and Total OPENING OF THE HORMUZ STRAIT” and an end to Iran’s nuclear threat, adding that Israel had also agreed to pause strikes.

Baghaei stated there would be “no significant change” in the situation in the Strait of Hormuz as long as Iran remained under what he described as U.S. military pressure.
