World.title: Military-civil integration key to robust def ecosystem to tackle challenges: Rajnath
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Defence minister Rajnath Singh on Monday underlined the need to deepen integration between the military and civil components of the defence ministry to foster greater synergy within the defence ecosystem to tackle evolving security and technological challenges, while ensuring institutional memory, stability and the effective application of rules and regulations.

Addressing the 85th Armed Forces Headquarters (AFHQ) Civilian Services Day celebrations in Delhi on Aug 3, he emphasised that both uniformed and civil services share the same commitment of âNation Firstâ, and when the objective is singular, every element of the system transforms into national strength.

Rajnath underlined that military and administrative integration cannot proceed along separate paths, adding that, as joint and integrated structures develop, there will be a need for continuity and expertise across all areas â policy, administration, human resource management, financial processes, logistics, and institutional knowledge.

He highlighted the importance of further enhancing structured cross-exposure between civilian and military officers, suggesting joint training programmes and developmental assignments for both sides to learn from each otherâs experiences.

âMilitary officers bring operational experience, a command perspective, and an understanding of warfare, while civilian officers contribute through administrative continuity, policy experience, an understanding of government processes, and institutional memory.





When these strengths combine, decision-making becomes more informed, balanced, and effective,â Rajnath said.

Explaining with the example of âcyber warfareâ, the minister stated that if officers of the AFHQ civilian services develop defence-specific common cyber tools leveraging their expertise, it could prove beneficial to the defence forces. He said a forum could be developed for the study of Indian military history, examining it from a civilian perspective, thereby fostering fresh ideas and new perspectives.

He expressed confidence that, by leveraging expertise in such areas, AFHQ civilian services will be able to make more meaningful contributions to the defence sector.

Rajnath called upon the AFHQ civilian services to evolve into the âstrategic brainâ of Indiaâs defence management architecture by developing a comprehensive understanding of the defence sector, functioning effectively in a joint environment, and continuously enhancing its expertise to face the emerging challenges.

While he acknowledged the AFHQ civilian services for moving ahead in sync with changing times, he asserted that, at a time when modern warfare is driven by technological dynamism, the cadre must move beyond its specific mandate of proper implementation of service rules, regulations & orders.

âA military derives its strength not merely from weapons and ammunition, but also from the thousands of unseen hands that always stand in their support. AFHQ Civilian Services is one of these unseen yet decisive forces. It must focus on strengthening the security architecture through research, geo-strategic thinking & innovative ideas. Its active participation in core defence matters is essential as, being a permanent cadre of the Ministry of Defence, it possesses deep domain knowledge,â Rajnath said.

World.title: Bankipur bypoll: BJP chief Nitin Nabin vows introspection after Kishor ends party's 30-yr hold
World.content:
NEW DELHI: BJP national president Nitin Nabin on Monday said the party would undertake a "thorough introspection" after losing the Bankipur Assembly bypoll in Bihar, where Jan Suraaj founder Prashant Kishor defeated BJP candidate Neeraj Kumar to end the party's three-decade dominance in the constituency.

Kishor won the bypoll by 19,324 votes, polling 64,151 votes against Neeraj Kumar's 44,827 votes. The victory marked Kishor's first electoral win since launching the Jan Suraaj Party and came less than a year after the party failed to win a single seat in the 2025 Bihar Assembly elections.

Reacting to the bypoll results, Nabin accepted the verdict and said the BJP would analyse the reasons behind its defeats.

In a post on X, Nabin said, "We accept the mandate received in today's three assembly by-elections.

We express our heartfelt gratitude to the people of Manjalpur assembly constituency in Gujarat for expressing their faith in the Bharatiya Janata Party. We extend our warm congratulations to all the dedicated workers and office-bearers of the BJP for this victory.

In Bapni Pur and Datia, we did not receive the expected mandate. We will conduct a thorough introspection of the election results in both these areas with complete seriousness, and with renewed energy and determination, we will continue to go among the people and work tirelessly to further strengthen their trust."





Bankipur had been one of the BJP's strongest urban bastions since 1995. The seat was represented first by BJP leader Navin Kishore Prasad Sinha and later by his son, Nitin Nabin, who held it for five consecutive terms before vacating it after his election to the Rajya Sabha, triggering the bypoll.

In the 2025 Bihar Assembly election, Nabin had retained the seat by a margin of more than 50,000 votes, making Kishor's victory one of the biggest political upsets in the state ahead of the Assembly elections.

The bypoll also marked Prashant Kishor's electoral debut. After years as a political strategist, he launched the Jan Suraaj Party with a campaign centred on education, employment and governance reforms. His victory gives the fledgling party its first electoral success.

Earlier in the day, Kishor said the result carried a message beyond Bankipur.

"It was an attempt by the people of Bihar to send a message to the BJP's central leadership that they should appoint a good person as the Chief Minister of Bihar," he told reporters.

Following the result, the Jan Suraaj Party posted on X, "In democracy, the fortress belongs only to the people. Thank you, Bankipur--this is your victory."

Bihar chief minister Samrat Choudhary also congratulated Kishor on his victory.

"In the grand festival of democracy, the people have chosen Jan Suraaj in the Bankipur Assembly by-election. I extend my heartfelt congratulations to Shri Prashant Kishor ji on his victory, while respecting the people's decision," he said in a post on X.

According to the Election Commission, the Bankipur bypoll recorded a voter turnout of 34.24 per cent.

World.title: Indians trafficked to cybercrime hubs in Golden Triangle tortured with electric shock
World.content:
NEW DELHI: The Asia pacific Group on money laundering in its latest report on cybercrime hubs in Myanmar, Lao PDR and Cambodia has revealed that Indian nationals are among victims of several countries trafficked to these cyber hubs and kept as slaves, trained to operate various scams like investment, romance, impersonation, social media and gaming.

These cybercrime hubs are controlled by Chinese nationals who also tortured these âslavesâ through coercion methods, including electric shock, dark room and isolation room confinement, physical abuse, fines and mental torture.

Cyber scam hubs are mainly located in the Golden Triangle region along border areas between Thailand, Myanmar, Lao PDR and Cambodia, besides the northern border of Myanmar with China and the Philippines.

Some of them operated from special economic zones.

An inter-governmental body like the Financial Action Task Force, the Sydney-based APG initiated this study led by Indonesia and UN Office on Drugs and Crime with a team comprised of 24 experts from the govts of Australia, Bangladesh, China, India, Indonesia, Malaysia, Myanmar, Solomon Islands, Singapore, Vietnam and UAE.

The study examined the emerging nexus between human trafficking and cyber-enabled financial crime, drawing upon the debriefings of 15 Indian nationals repatriated from Myanmar, Lao PDR, and Cambodia between 2023 and 2024.





The individuals were recruited under the pretext of high-paying customer-service or IT jobs, transported through Thailand, and then coerced to work in criminal âscam compoundsâ operated by transnational syndicates, it said.

âVictims were mostly young men (20-35 age group) from nine Indian states, recruited via social media or personal networks, who paid upfront fees (Rs 50-70,000). Compounds were run by Chinese-speaking syndicates, with multi-national workforces and strict control (passport confiscation, physical/psychological abuse),â the report has said.

The report further revealed that these slave workers were sold between scam compounds, where they were subjected to confinement, violence and debt bondage. âInterception operations and large-scale rescues have revealed victims from a variety of nationalities and regions, suggesting that recruitment practices have expanded beyond solely regional contexts. Workers are forced to conduct investment fraud, impersonation schemes, romance scams, and illegal online gambling platforms, with performance enforced through physical abuse and threats,â it added.

Crypto-based financial systems served as core enabling mechanisms.

Other examples cited by the agency related to large-scale use of mule accounts and SIM cards from India, which exploited the âvulnerable populationâ, which were unemployed youth and drug addicts. In one case, muule bank accounts and SIM cards from Punjab were supplied to cyber fraudsters in the Philippines, facilitating scams totalling over Rs 40 crore. The unemployed youth were lured with fake jobs, asked to open accounts and provide their SIMs, which were couriered to the Philippines.

World.title: India gets 101st 'Ramsar' site as Arunachal Pradesh's Glaw Lake joins elite global list of protected wetlands
World.content:
Glaw Lake in Himachal Pradesh

NEW DELHI: Indiaâs one more wetland, Glaw Lake of Arunachal Pradesh, has entered the global list of protected wetlands as a Ramsar site. It is the countryâs 101st such site and the stateâs first to join the elite club for additional care and conservation.Located within the Kamlang Tiger Reserve and Wildlife Sanctuary, Glaw Lake is a pristine freshwater lake in the Eastern Himalayas and a biodiversity hotspot. The lake is fed by perennial mountain streams and is surrounded by lush vegetation, supporting rich floral diversity.âEvery new Ramsar site strengthens our resolve to protect nature while securing the future of communities that depend on these invaluable ecosystems,â said Union environment minister Bhupender Yadav while announcing the development on X on Monday.The Glaw Lake wetland has over 150 tree species and 49 orchid species recorded within the site and its catchment, underscoring its ecological significance and surrounding landscape.âFrom 26 Ramsar sites in 2014 to 101 today, this remarkable journey reflects our unwavering commitment to environmental protection, biodiversity conservation, and sustainable development,â said Yadav.Globally, there are nearly 2,600 such designated wetlands under the Ramsar Convention.India has the highest number of such wetlands in Asia and third highest in the world after the UK (176) and Mexico (144).Wetlands are land areas covered by water, either temporarily/ seasonally or permanently. These are critical ecosystems that play a significant role in supporting biodiversity, and providing various ecosystem services such as flood control, water supply, food, fibre and raw materials.

World.title: SKM announces farmers' protests at 100 locations, including Delhi, from November 26
World.content:
November 26 also marks the sixth anniversary of the year-long farmersâ protest, which culminated in the repeal of the three farm laws in December 2021.

NEW DELHI: Emboldened by the success of the studentsâ protests here at Jantar Mantar, the Samyukt Kisan Morcha (SKM)âthe umbrella organisation of farmer groups involved in the anti-farm laws agitation five years agoâon Monday announced that it would restart protests at 100 locations, including Delhi, across India from November 26 - the day which will mark the sixth anniversary of the year-long farmersâ protest, which culminated in the repeal of the three farm laws in December 2021.The protests will demand a law guaranteeing minimum support price (MSP), repeal of all free trade agreements and no India-US FTA, and a comprehensive loan waiver to address rural indebtedness.The SKMâs demand list also includes four other demands such as scrapping of four labour codes; minimum wage of Rs. 31,000 payable to all workers as well as restoration of the previous rural job guarantee scheme; withdrawal of Electricity Privatisation Bill 2025, the Seed Bill 2025, and the NFSA Amendment Bill; and no forceful land acquisition.âThe protest will not be called off until all seven principal demands are achieved,â said P Krishnaprasad of the All India Kisan Sabha (AIKS), a constituent of SKM.âThe decisive mass struggle, coordinated with joint platforms and organisations of workers, farmers, agricultural workers, students, youth, women and all other social sections facing the brunt of corporate attack under the NDA regime will advance based on worker-peasant unity to end the prolonged agrarian crisis and labour exploitation, and to build a modern democratic, federal, secular India,â he said while announcing the overall protest plan of the SKM.

World.title: NDA states acted firmly against recruitment scams; opposition failed to curb irregularities: CM Dhami
World.content:
on Monday said that NDA-ruled states have taken firm action against recruitment scams and examination-related irregularities, while alleging that opposition-ruled states failed to curb such malpractices and were marked by widespread irregularities in recruitment processes.

Speaking to reporters here, Dhami said that the Uttarakhand government had acted decisively against the "cheating mafia" by arresting and jailing over 100 people and enacting a stringent anti-cheating law.

"In all NDA-ruled states, wherever instances of cheating occurred, action was taken against the perpetrators. In Uttarakhand, we took action against a hundred members of the 'cheating mafia,' jailed them, and enacted a law specifically to curb cheating.

Furthermore, recruitment drives were conducted and fully completed in strict accordance with the scheduled calendar," Dhami said.

The Chief Minister contrasted this with states such as Jharkhand and Punjab and also referred to the previous Samajwadi Party government in Uttar Pradesh, alleging that recruitment processes between 2012 and 2017 were marred by irregularities.

"In contrast, consider states like Jharkhand, Punjab, or others.





Previously, between 2012 and 2017, Uttar Pradesh witnessed massive irregularities in recruitment and widespread cheating," he said.

Targeting opposition parties, Dhami alleged that the Congress, Samajwadi Party, Aam Aadmi Party (AAP), and their alliance partners were responsible for such irregularities.

"Be it the Congress Party, the Samajwadi Party, the AAP, or any of their alliance partners--they are the ones who committed all these wrongs, and the youth of the country understands this," he said.

Referring to the Prime Minister's approach towards young people allegedly involved in such incidents, Dhami said the focus was on taking action against the masterminds rather than punishing those who may have been influenced.

"The PM chose not to subject these young people, who may have been misled or misguided for whatever reason, to legal hassles or punishment; instead, he forgave them," Dhami said.

Launching a sharp attack on Opposition leaders following the registration of an FIR against Congress MP Rahul Gandhi, Independent MP Pappu Yadav, and Samajwadi Party MP Awadhesh Prasad over an alleged insult to Sanatan Dharma, Uttarakhand Chief Minister Pushkar Singh Dhami on Monday stated that defaming saints represents the "lowest form of conduct imaginable."

Addressing reporters in Dehradun, CM Dhami condemned the actions of the leaders, alleging that Pappu Yadav and his associates have consistently worked to malign Sanatan Dharma.

"To defame the saints is the lowest form of conduct imaginable. I had stated earlier as well that Pappu Yadav and the 'Pappu gang' have been working in tandem to continuously malign Sanatan Dharma," CM Dhami said.

Taking a dig at the Opposition leaders over their stance on religious events, the Chief Minister pointed out that despite being extended invitations to the historic Ram Mandir Pran Pratishtha ceremony, none of them attended.

"When the Ram Mandir was being built, they were invited to the event, yet none of them attended; and today, they are engaging in this manner to defame our community of saints. I believe this reveals their true mindset regarding Sanatan Dharma," Dhami added.

Highlighting his state administration's public outreach programs, Chief Minister Dhami also elaborated on the progress of the state government's 'Jan-Jan ki Sarkar' initiative.

He emphasised that the drive is designed to bridge the gap between governance and citizens, especially those residing in remote regions.

"The objective of the 'Jan-Jan ki Sarkar' initiative is to bring the entire government administrative machinery to the people to resolve their issues," CM Dhami said. "This includes issuing certificates to those who lacked them and ensuring that people receive the benefits of various Central and State government schemes...

"So far, over 6.5 lakh people have participated across both phases, and more than 60,000 individuals have received on-the-spot resolutions to their grievances," he stated.

World.title: A seat for JSP's 'school bag': Why Prashant Kishor's Bankipur win is a warning for both BJP and RJD
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Jan Suraaj Party (JSP) founder

has finally found a seat for his âschool bagâ in Bihar. The election strategist-turned-politician has flipped the Bankipur assembly seat, an unassailable bastion of the BJP for the last 30 years.

Before todayâs shock defeat, the BJP had registered 8 consecutive victories in Bankipur since 1995, when it won the seat for the first time.

By-election in Bankipur was necessitated after

resigned as BJP MLA from the seat in April after his election to Rajya Sabha. This followed Nitin Nabinâs elevation as BJP national president in January this year.

To gauge the enormity of Prashant Kishorâs victory, look at these facts:

BJP has held Bankipur assembly seat from 1995 (Till 2005, the seat was known as Patna West)

BJP chief Nitin Nabin won from the Bankipur assembly seat four times in a row

Nitin Nabin won from Bankipur for first time in 2010 with a margin of 56%

From 1995 to 2010, the seat (known as Patna West) was represented by Navin Kishore Prasad Sinha (Nitin Nabinâs father)

Father-son duo has won the seat 8 consecutive times

For PK, as Prashant Kishor is popularly known, contesting the Bankipur byelection was a huge political gamble.

PK, who made a high-pitched entry into Bihar politics with a padyatra spanning months ahead of the 2025 assembly elections, cut a sorry figure when his Jan Suraj Party failed to win even one seat less than a year ago. Such dismal was his first electoral show that JSP lost deposit in 236 of the 238 seats it contested.

Prashant Kishor did not contest the election himself and instead led a high-voltage campaign for his party across the state.





Little wonder his decision to contest the Bankipur bypoll was fraught with the danger of becoming a make-or-break political move. But the gamble has paid off and Prashant Kishor with his debut win has propelled into the centrestage of Bihar politics.

âBankipurâs message to BJP central leadershipâ

Prashant Kishor polled over 64,151 votes and won the key electoral battle by a margin of 19,324 votes over BJPâs Neeraj Kumar. Prashant Kishorâs resounding success, nine months after his partyâs humiliating defeat, marks a remarkable turnaround.

And making the most of his victory, Prashant Kishor immediately trained his guns at Bihar chief minister Samrat Choudhary.

"This is the victory of the people of Bankipur. As we stated during the election campaign, this was not just an election to choose an MLA. It was an attempt by the people of Bihar to send a message to the BJP's central leadership that they should appoint a good person as the chief minister of Bihar. They do not want a person with a criminal background or questionable conduct, character, or reputation to lead Bihar.

They want a good chief minister who can improve education, create employment opportunities for the youth, and ensure that the children of Bihar do not have to migrate elsewhere for work," Kishor told reporters as his supporters celebrated his maiden electoral victory.

Prashant Kishor hits out at Bihar CM

Prashant Kishorâs use of his victory to target Samrat Choudhary did not come as a surprise. Ksihor been unrelenting in his attacks against the BJP leader ever since the election strategist became a full-time politician.

He has targeted Samrat Choudhary over the chief ministerâs educational qualification and his alleged criminal past.

Kishor's development pitch or disappointment against BJP?

The Jan Suraaj chief also called upon the BJP's central leadership to focus on governance ahead of the next Lok Sabha elections, stating, "Before the Lok Sabha elections, Prime Minister Modi, the BJP, and Amit Shah should focus on improving Bihar, creating jobs for its youth, and stopping migration.

That is our only objective. We do not want to become MLAs merely to award contracts. Our sole objective is the development of Bihar.

"

These are the very themes on which Prashant Kishor fought the 2025 assembly elections and lost. Clearly, while he keeps focus on these issues, his victory in bankipur may less be about endorsement of his development focus and more about peopleâs disappointment with the BJP. The result is also perhaps a fallout of the studentsâ agitation against NEET-UG paper leak, which saw huge protests in Bihar.

In Siwan, a police constable was suspended after a video purportedly showing him using an AK-47 rifle during a student protest on July 25 went viral on social media.

Leader of opposition in Bihar assembly,

, slammed Chief Minister Samrat Choudhary for the incident. He posted a video of the purported incident on X and, along with it, said, "During the protest in Siwan, police resorted to direct firing with an AK-47 on students.

When a criminal becomes chief minister, then police fire bullets at innocent students.â

âVerdict by Bihar's youth against BJPâ

CPI(ML) Liberation general secretary Dipankar Bhattacharya in his message to Prashant Kishor described his victory as a significant verdict by Bihar's youth against the BJP-led state government.

In a post on X, Bhattacharya termed Kishor's victory a "well-earned debut victory" and said the bypoll result reflected public anger against the ruling dispensation.

"Congratulations to Prashant Kishor on his well-earned debut victory in Bankipur bypoll. Kudos to the youth of Bihar for delivering such a telling blow to the supremely arrogant, incompetent and tyrannical BJP government of Bihar," he said.

Shock verdict for BJP

The BJP was quick to accept the verdict of the people. State BJP president Sanjay Saraogi said in a statement, "We bow before the will of the people. We shall draw lessons from the debacle, unlike our opponents who tend to blame every electoral loss of theirs on EVMs and the Election Commission".

But for the BJP, this defeat comes as an embarrassment for both its national president Nitin Nabin and the partyâs first chief minister in the state Samrat Choudhary. Bankipur seat was literally a personal fiefdom of Nitin Nabinâs family which represented the constituency for 30 long years. A defeat in the backyard will surely embarrass the BJP chief.

For Samrat Choudhary, this was the first electoral test of his government which was formed after the BJP took over the reins of the state from JD(U) chief Nitish Kumar.

It was Nitish Kumar who had led the NDA to an emphatic triumph in the 2025 assembly elections. And the BJP would have hoped that Samrat Choudhary would have given it a winning start. But that was not to be.

Lalu's RJD pushed to fringes

The Bankipur bypoll result also has a worrying message for the main opposition party RJD. Tejashwi Yadavâs party seems to have learnt no lessons from the 2025 electoral drubbing. The party which has been reduced to 25 seats in the assembly did little to show intent on the ground.

Join conversation Commentsâ Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

Its candidate Rekha Kumari polled just 14,273 votes. This was over 32,000 votes less than the figure of 46,363, which she had polled in the 2025 assembly elections as the runnerup in the seat.

Ironically, for the greater part of the campaign, RJDâs star campaigner Tejashwi Yadav was missing in action.

Time to pause, review

It may not be prudent to overexaggerate the outcome of one bypoll. The result of one seat, even though high-profile, may not be indicative of any larger trend. But for the BJP and the RJD to brush aside the defeat as a one-off setback would be doing harm to their cause. The BJP should remember that it rules Bihar but is still dependent on its allies for survival. The RJD, meanwhile, remains the main opposition party but seems to have lost the plot to factionalism and family feuds after its dismal 2025 show.

Both need to pause and review what went wrong in Bankipur. MLA Prashant Kishor, on the other hand, will perhaps be now preparing for another bout with his political bete noir Samrat Choudhary - this time on the floor of Bihar assembly.

World.title: 679th Foundation Day of Bahmani Empire observed in Kalaburagi
World.content:
The 679th Foundation Day of Bahmani Empire was observed at the tomb of Alauddin Hasan Bahman Shah, the founder and first ruler of the Sultanate, in Kalaburagi city on Monday.

The event, organised by the Bahmani Foundation, brought together historians, artists, intellectuals and social activists, who recalled the contributions of the Bahmani Sultanate to the cultural and architectural heritage of the region during its nearly two-century rule from 1347 to 1527 AD.

Speaking on the occasion, advocate Jabbar Gola said the Bahmani rulers played an important role in promoting art, culture and architecture, leaving behind a rich legacy reflected in the monuments and traditions of the region.

Bahmani Foundation president Qazi Rizwan-Ur-Rahman Siddique said the organisation has been commemorating the Foundation Day for several years through seminars, cultural programmes and competitions aimed at creating awareness among students about the history and heritage of the Bahmani period.

Artists Mohammed Ayazuddin Patel and Rehaman Patel, Numismatist Mohammad Ismail and others were present.

World.title: Police seize ganja on train in Salem
World.content: The Salem Railway Police seized 10 kg of ganja smuggled on a train on Monday. Acting on a tip-off, the police searched the Sabari Express at Salem Junction. When they checked the unreserved compartment, they found two unclaimed bags near the toilet. The bags contained 10 kg of ganja. The police registered a case and are on the lookout for the smugglers.

World.title: Trump claims Iran talks will start August 3, and other developments in West Asia
World.content:
After calling off a fresh round of strikes against Iran, U.S. President Donald Trump announced that new talks to wind down the war would start Monday (August 3, 2026), even as Iranian officials claimed their diplomatic efforts were focused on neighbouring nations.

Aslo Read: West Asia updates on August 3, 2026

Talks between the U.S. and Iran are critical to ending the monthslong conflict and reviving stalled cargo traffic through the Strait of Hormuz, a crucial waterway through which about a fifth of all traded oil and natural gas passed before the war.

But Iran’s Foreign Ministry said it’s focused on negotiations with Oman, not the U.S., prompting Mr. Trump to criticise the country’s leadership, which has grown increasingly divided over the war’s endgame.

Mr. Trump, who has made a habit of threatening strikes on Iran only to dangle the prospect of a last-minute diplomatic reprieve, said Monday (August 3) that whether “Iran wants to admit it or not, we are, in fact, talking.”

Elsewhere, Israel struck the Gaza Strip over the weekend, days after the U.S. and Hamas said a deal was reached for the militant group to disarm, a potential step toward ending the war in Gaza.

Hospitals in Gaza said at least 17 people were killed in the weekend strikes, including children. A strike on a residential apartment in southern Gaza killed three family members, including a 4-year-old child, according to Nasser Hospital, where the bodies arrived.

The Israeli military said the strikes targeted militants.

World.title: Officials inspect sago factory in Salem after fire incident
World.content:
Following a fire incident at an sago factory at Sathasivapuram in Attur on Sunday, officials on Monday ordered suspension of its operation. The fire broke out at the factory, reportedly owing to short-circuit, on Sunday evening and spread to a room where chlorine had been dumped. When workers tried to extinguish the fire in the room, they experienced breathing difficulty and some fainted.

The Attur Fire and Rescue Service personnel rescued nine workers and extinguished the fire. During the operation, a firefighter, too, suffered breathing difficulty. In total, 10 people were hospitalised. The Attur rural police also registered a case.

On Monday, officials from the Revenue Department, Directorate of Industrial Safety and Health; Fire and Rescue Services; and the Tamil Nadu Pollution Control Board visited the factory.

The officials instructed the management not to operate the factory until further orders. The officials also gave it three hours to clean the factory.

World.title: Public urged to support enumeration exercise
World.content:
Two days after the house listing operations for Census 2027 began in the district, enumerators and supervisors are making door-to-door visits to collate information on the data sets.

According to the district administration, 2,660 enumerators and 418 supervisors are making door-to-door visits to collate information that would go on to inform the population data sets. District Collector C. Dinesh Kumar inaugurated the house listing operations on Saturday.

The enumerators and supervisors will visit houses with their identification cards. People are requested to verify their identity and provide the information sought. The information collated shall be used only for the purposes of Census and shall not be used for any other purposes, the administration said.

Households have been requested to support the exercise and provide the information. The Census, which began on August 1, will end on August 30.

In Dharmapuri

House listing operations in Dharmapuri is being undertaken with the support of 2,376 enumerators and 399 supervisors. District Collector V. Saravanan urged the public to receive the household census enumerators with respect and, upon verification of their identity, answer the 33 questions. The replies would help form the data set that would inform the status of the population and go on to help in policy formulation.

World.title: Sudan army drone attack on Darfur court kills 35
World.content:
The Sudanese army on Sunday (August 2, 2026) struck a traditional court in western Darfur with drones, killing 35 people and wounding others, a rights group said.

The Emergency Lawyers, which has documented abuses by both the army and its rival paramilitaries throughout the three-year conflict, said the strike hit the court in the village of Garra al-Zawaya in North Darfur state at around 1:00 p.m., as civilians had "gathered to attend hearings on local cases and disputes".

The village is under the control of the Paramilitary Rapid Support Forces (RSF), which have been locked in a brutal conflict with the army since April 2023.

"The court session was being held under a tree with the participation of local community leaders," a witness from the area told AFP on condition of anonymity for safety reasons.

Among those killed were "four tribal leaders and two RSF commanders", the witness added.

There was no immediate response from the army. The RSF's self-declared government condemned the attack as "a horrific crime", saying 37 people had been killed and 50 others wounded.

Drone warfare

Garra al-Zawaya lies near the town of Kabkabiya in North Darfur, about 150 kilometres (93 miles) west of El-Fasher, the army's last stronghold in Darfur before it was captured by the RSF in a bloody offensive last October.

UN investigators have said violence linked to the RSF's siege and capture of El-Fasher bears "the hallmarks of genocide".

Following its takeover of the city, the RSF, which emerged from the Janjaweed militia accused of atrocities in Darfur in the early 2000s, consolidated control over much of the region.

Since El-Fasher campaign, both sides have increasingly relied on drone warfare. According to the United Nations, more than 1,000 civilians were killed in drone strikes during the first five months of this year.

Last week, after losing control of a key highway linking the capital Khartoum and the city of El-Obeid, RSF commander Mohamed Hamdan Daglo released a video message in which he told his fighters to consider themselves "unleashed" in their war against the army.

El-Obeid, the largest city in the southern Kordofan region, has come under intense drone attacks in recent weeks, prompting the UN to issue a "red alert" over the unfolding "catastrophe" there, where the RSF has sought to reimpose a blockade and is feared to be preparing a ground offensive.

The UN has repeatedly warned that RSF advances in El-Obeid and the wider Kordofan region could lead to mass atrocities.

The war between Daglo and his former ally, army chief Abdel Fattah al-Burhan, has killed tens of thousands of people, displaced millions and created what the United Nations describes as the world's largest hunger and displacement crises.

Both sides have been accused of committing war crimes, including indiscriminate attacks on civilians, but the RSF has been particularly accused of systematic sexual violence, looting and mass atrocities.

World.title: Prashant Kishor breaks BJP’s five-term Bankipur run with decisive bypoll victory
World.content:
Jan Suraaj Party (JSP) founder Prashant Kishor scripted a major political upset in Bihar by defeating the Bharatiya Janata Party candidate in the Bankipur Assembly byelection, a constituency represented for five consecutive terms by the BJP’s national president Nitin Nabin. The BJP retained Manjalpur in Gujarat while the Congress held on to Madhya Pradesh’s Datia in other Assembly byelections.

Mr. Kishor dedicated the victory to the people of Bankipur and appealed to the BJP’s central leadership to change the Chief Minister of Bihar. The Bankipur Assembly seat had fallen vacant after Mr. Nabin vacated the seat upon his election to the Rajya Sabha and elevation as BJP chief.

The political strategist-turned-politician clinched victory over BJP candidate Neeraj Kumar Sinha by a margin of 19,324 votes. He bagged 64,151 votes while Mr. Sinha finished with 44,827 votes. Rashtriya Janata Dal nominee Rekha Kumari secured the third position with 14,273 votes. A total of 25 candidates contested the election, with 646 voters choosing the NOTA option.

In the 2025 Assembly election, Mr. Nabin had defeated Ms. Kumari by a margin of 51,936 votes. He had secured 98,299 votes while Ms. Kumari polled 46,363 votes. The JSP’s Vandana Kumari had received 7,717 votes.

Prashant Kishor: From election backrooms to Bihar Assembly

Throughout the 32 rounds of counting on Monday, Mr. Kishor, contesting an election for the first time, remained ahead in every round and held on to his lead until the final tally. Celebrations broke out at the JSP office in Patliputra Colony after the 10th round, when Mr. Kishor had established a lead of over 6,000 votes.

A JSP worker, celebrating the victory while dancing to Bhojpuri songs, said: “Bankipur is just a trailer; the whole of Bihar is still to come.”

After the 22nd round of counting, when Mr. Kishor was leading by a margin of around 13,000 votes, he and his wife Jahanvi Das walked to the counting centre at A.N. College to join the party workers and supporters in celebrations.

“The people have not only elected an MLA, but the people of Bankipur have given a message to the central leadership of the BJP to replace Samrat Choudhary with a better person. I expect that the BJP leadership will seriously think about it,” Mr. Kishor said.

He added that the time had come for Prime Minister Narendra Modi to not only care about the people of Gujarat but also pay attention to the people of Bihar.

“My only concern is that the young people of Bihar need to go to other States in search of jobs. Migration from Bihar should be stopped,” he said.

Read updates from the vote counting for Manjalpur Assembly bypoll in Gujarat

The Bihar Chief Minister congratulated Mr. Kishor on his victory on his X handle. “In the grand festival of democracy, the people have chosen Jan Suraaj in the Bankipur Assembly by-election. I extend my heartfelt congratulations to Prashant Kishor ji on his victory, while respecting the people’s decision,” said Mr. Choudhary.

In his statement, Bihar BJP State president Sanjay Saraogi said, “The Bharatiya Janata Party humbly accepts the mandate of the Bankipur by-election and respects the decision of the people. In a democratic process, the verdict of the people is above everything! We will seriously analyse why we did not secure the votes; we will identify our shortcomings and work diligently to rectify them.”

He added, “Unlike Opposition parties, we do not blame constitutional institutions, EVMs, or the Election Commission for our defeat. The Bharatiya Janata Party has complete faith in democracy and constitutional systems, and believes in addressing its shortcomings through introspection and review.”

BJP wins in Manjalpur

In Gujarat, the BJP retained the Manjalpur Assembly seat in Vadodara district, with its candidate Satish Govindbhai Patel defeating Congress nominee and former Minister Bhikhabhai Rabari by 30,630 votes. According to the Election Commission, Mr. Patel secured 55,481 votes against Mr. Rabari’s 24,851 after 20 rounds of counting at Bhavan’s School in Makarpura. The byelection, necessitated by the death of senior BJP MLA and former Minister Yogesh Patel, recorded a voter turnout of 37.5%.

With the victory, the BJP’s strength in the 182-member Gujarat Assembly has increased to 162 seats, while the Congress has 12 MLAs.

The Congress defended Madhya Pradesh’s Datia Assembly constituency, with its candidate Ghanshyam Singh winning against BJP’s Ashutosh Tiwari by 6,016 votes. Mr. Singh, a member of Datia’s erstwhile royal family, polled 66,757 votes against Mr. Tiwari’s 60,741. Mr. Tiwari was picked to contest the bypoll over former State Home Minister Narottam Mishra. Aazad Samaj Party candidate Damodar Yadav ‘Mandal’ finished third with 22,527 votes.

World.title: Stone pelting in Hubballi as protesters demanded ministerial berth to three-time MLA Prasad Abbayya
World.content:
Hubballi witnessed a snap protest demanding ministerial berth to three-time MLA Prasad Abbayya on Monday. As the protest turned violent resulting in damages to a public transport bus, the police detained over 40 persons.

The demonstrators had gathered at Indi Pump in Hubballi to register their protest against their leader not being included in the State Cabinet.

As they tried to torch old tyres as mark of their protest, the police personnel present at the protest site tried to prevent them, leading to altercation. Protesting the police action, some of them lied down on the road and refused to move.

Meanwhile, stones were pelted at a public transport bus leading to damages. As the situation seemed to go out of control, the police swung into action and took several of them into custody and dispersed the crowd.

Police Commissioner N. Shashikumar told reporters that over 40 persons had been taken into custody and action would also be taken in connection with the stone-pelting.

As the protests were likely to continue in the twin cities, they had deployed additional forces at strategic points, he said.

World.title: Death toll from suicide bombing near police station in Swat rises to 17
World.content:
SWAT: The death toll from Sunday’s suicide bombing near a police station in Swat rose to 17 on Monday, including several policemen.

The suicide bombing had taken place near the Kabal Police Station while a protest against lawlessness was under way at the adjoining public square. Police said that the suicide bomber had detonated his explosives after police personnel atte­mpted to stop and search him at the entrance to the police station.

According to a list of casualties shared by Swat police spokesperson Nasir Iqbal Karimi, seven policemen and 10 civilians have lost their lives in the incident while 18 policemen and nine civilians have been injured.

Police have revised down the death toll from an earlier tally of 19, which they shared in a statement earlier in the day.

Karimi said in the statement that a large-scale rescue operation had been launched immediately after the attack, in which more than 50 Rescue 1122 personnel participated.

“Rescue teams provided first aid at the scene before shifting the injured to various hospitals for further treatment. Authorities are continuing relief efforts as investigations into the suicide attack remain under way,” it said.

In a separate statement, Swat police said the funeral prayers of two policemen martyred in the suicide attack were held at Javed Iqbal Shaheed Police Lines on Monday.

A smartly turned-out police contingent presented a guard of honour to Constable Mukarram Khan and Constable Hussain Khan, and floral wreaths were laid on their coffins.

The ceremony was attended by Malakand Regional Police Officer (RPO) Syed Fida Hassan Shah, Swat District Police Officer (DPO) Muhammad Umar Khan, Superintendent of Police (operations) Ghulam Sadiq Khan, Superintendent of Police (headquarters) Ataullah, and other senior police officers.

Security personnel and law enforcers have been coming under attack in KP, which continues to face terrorism.

According to the Pakistan Institute for Conflict and Security Studies’ (PICSS) monthly security assessment released on Saturday, Security personnel deaths in terrorism incidents in KP, excluding merged districts, increased from 12 in June to 38 in July and terrorist deaths from 37 to 108, reflecting a rise by 192pc. But civilian deaths fell from 26 to seven, a decline by 73pc. One peace committee member was also killed.

Security personnel deaths in merged districts rose from six to 11 and terrorist deaths fell from 72 to 55. Civilian deaths, meanwhile, rose by 86pc, increasing from seven to 13.

CM visits Swat

Khyber Pakhtunkhwa Chief Minister Sohail Afridi reached Swat on Monday to meet with the martyrs’ families. He was accompanied by Special Assistant for Home Affairs Tariq Saeed, Chief Secretary Shahab Ali Shah and the KP inspector general (IG) of police, according to a statement issued by the CM office.

In Swat, he visited Sheikh Zayed Al Nahyan Hospital in Saidu Sharif and inquired about the health of those injured in the suicide attack.

The chief minister directed the hospital administration to ensure the provision of the best possible medical treatment to all the injured, the statement said.

It added that the CM also chaired a high-level meeting at the Jirga Hall in Saidu Sharif. At the meeting, which was also attended by senior officials, the CM was briefed on the overall law and order situation in Malakand Division and its Swat district.

Reaffirming the government’s commitment to restoring peace, the chief minister said there would be no compromise on law and order in Swat and Malakand. He directed the relevant authorities to launch a full-scale operation against terrorists and ensure that peace and stability were restored.

Meanwhile, KP Inspector General of Police (IG) Zulfikar Hameed visited the injured personnel and civilians in the hospital, according to a post on the KP Police’s X account.

“Our police personnel have high morale. The cowardly attacks of terrorists will be given a befitting response,” he is quoted as saying.

Lawyers, traders observe strike

Lawyers across Swat and Upper Swat observed a complete strike on Monday to condemn Sunday’s suicide bombing. Court proceedings remained suspended as members of the legal fraternity expressed solidarity with the victims and called for stronger measures for eliminating terrorism.

A shutter-down strike was also observed across Kabal tehsil, where markets remained closed.

Separately, elders of the Swat Qaumi Jirga, traders, lawyers, and youth representatives have announced a protest demonstration at Nishat Chowk in Swat’s Mingora on August 7 to condemn the recent wave of terrorism in the region.

The organisers said the planned demonstration was aimed at expressing solidarity with the victims of terrorist attacks. It was being organised to demand lasting peace and urge the government to take decisive action against terrorist groups operating in the area, they said.

World.title: PM Shehbaz congratulates PML-N after party maintains lead in second phase of AJK polls
World.content:
Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif congratulated the PML-N’s leadership and successful candidates on Monday after unofficial results of the second phase of elections in Azad Jammu and Kashmir (AJK) showed it had won 14 of 18 seats up for grabs the previous day.

The PML-N’s main rival in the contest and also its ally in the Centre, the PPP, has accused the PML-N of electoral malpractices, rigging and violence during Sunday polls — as it had during the first phase of the elections in Mirpur division on July 27. The PML-N secured nine of the 13 seats in the first phase while the PPP won the remaining four.

Elections in AJK are being held in three phases over security concerns, with polling having been held on seven seats of Muzaffarabad division and 12 refugee seats — reserved seats for refugees from India-occupied Kashmir — on Sunday. In the third phase, elections will be held in 11 constituencies of Poonch division on August 10.

‘Results reflect people’s confidence in PML-N’s policies’

A statement released by the PM’s Office on Monday said the premier congratulated PML-N’s leadership and successful candidates after their win in the second phase.

“The continuity of this success is a result of the hard work of PML-N President Nawaz Sharif and the entire PML-N team,” the statement quoted PM Shehbaz as saying

According to the statement, the premier noted that Nawaz and the PML-N team had conducted a successful electoral campaign in AJK and the party’s success “reflects the confidence of the people of AJK in PML-N’s policies”.

He said the development and prosperity of AJK and the welfare of its people remained PML-N’s top priority.

PM Shehbaz added that political parties had actively participated in the second phase of the AJK elections, which he said would further strengthen the democratic process.

Results breakdown

Earlier in the day, state broadcaster Radio Pakistan reported the unofficial results of Sunday’s elections, citing AJK Chief Election Commissioner Justice (retd) Ghulam Mustafa Mughal’s press talk in Muzaffarabad.

During the press briefing, he announced that the PML-N had won 14 seats and the PPP four, the report said.

Unofficial results

LA-25 bagged by PML-N’s Ghulam Qadir

LA-26 bagged by PPP’s Mian Abdul Waheed Khan

LA-29 bagged by PPP’s Sardar Mukhtar Ahmad Khan

LA-30 bagged by PML-N’s Mustafa Bashir Abbasi

LA-31 bagged by PML-N’s Saqib Majeed Khan

LA-32 bagged by PML-N’s Raja Farooq Haider Khan

LA-34 (Jammu-I) — PML-N’s Nasir Hussain Dar

LA-35 (Jammu-II) —PML-N’s Chaudhry Muhammad Ismael

LA-36 (Jammu-III) — PML-N’s Muhammad Ahsan Raza

LA-37 (Jammu-IV) — PML-N’s Maryam Javed

LA-38 (Jammu-V) — PML-N’s Zeeshan Ali

LA-39 (Jammu-VI) — PML-N’s Raja Muhammad Siddique Khan

LA-40 (Kashmir Valley-I) — PPP’s Amir Abdul Ghaffar Khan

LA-41 (Kashmir Valley-II) — PML-N’s Muhammad Amir Shah

LA-42 (Kashmir Valley-III) — PML-N’s Syed Shoukat Ali Shah

LA-43 (Kashmir Valley-IV) — PML-N’s Muhammad Yasin Lone

LA-44 (Kashmir Valley-V) — PML-N’s Ahmad Raza Qadri

LA-45 (Kashmir Valley-VI) — PPP’s Abdul Majid Khan

Polling was postponed until Tuesday in LA-27 Muzaffarabad-I (Kutla) and at 71 of the 174 polling stations in LA-28 Muzaffarabad-II (Lachhrat) as polling staff and election material could not reach the constituency because of landslides and bad weather that resulted in blocked roads.

According to preliminary results issued by the AJK Election Commission, the refugee seat of LA-37 saw a tough contest between PML-N’s Maryam Javed and Jammu & Kashmir United Movement’s (JKUM) Usman Aleem.

Javed emerged as the winner with 28,547 votes, while Aleem was the runner-up with 22,937 votes.

According to a document showing results for constituencies LA-34 through LA-45, PPP candidates were the runner-ups to PML-N in LA-36, LA-39, LA-42 and LA-43.

All Jammu and Kashmir Muslim Conference was the runner-up in LA-44 and LA-45, while independents placed second in LA-34, LA-35 and LA-41.

CEC hints at no polling in Rawalakot, Tharor on Aug 10

For the third phase of the AJK elections, the CEC said that considering the situation in Poonch division, the commission would conduct polling on August 10 in three constituencies in Bagh, one in Haveli and one in Abbaspur.

However, the constituencies of Baloch and Palandri (in Sudhnoti district) were also under consideration, he said.

“If we receive positive reports from there and the way people in Muzaffarabad rejected all pressures and tactics, came out of their homes and cast their votes, people in Poonch also extend the same cooperation, God-willing, we are ready to hold elections in all constituencies except for Rawalakot city and Thorar.”

“Our preparation is complete for all constituencies. However, the law and order situation and the demands of the safety of voters play an important role in holding elections.”

Responding to a question, he said that under the AJK constitution, the current Legislative Assembly ceases to exist after August 4.

“Even if elections cannot be held in two or a few more constituencies, one cannot say that the house is not complete or those who have returned cannot take oath or perform their functions,” he explained.

He said the new assembly would still take oath after the completion of the August 10 polls.

For LA-27, where the election had been postponed across the constituency, he said polling will be held at all 197 polling stations tomorrow (Tuesday).

Polling would be held on Tuesday from 8am to 5pm at 54 polling stations in three union councils (UCs) of LA-28 Muzaffarabad-II (Lachhrat).

Polling staff and election material could not reach these areas in time due to road blockades. At two of these polling stations, supporters of a candidate had set ballot boxes on fire.

The CEC affirmed that adequate arrangements had been made to reopen the roads following bad weather.

After security personnel returned from other areas, additional forces had been deployed in view of the sensitivity of these constituencies to ensure the electoral process was completed peacefully. He added that polling staff had already been dispatched to their respective stations under security escort.

AJK Election Commissioner retd Justice Ghulam Mustafa Mughal addresses the media on Aug 3, 2026. — Photo provided by Tariq Naqash

Speaking on yesterday’s elections, the AJK CEC said voter turnout in the seven constituencies stood at 53 per cent.

“This was certainly a difficult election, and given the circumstances that were created, this is by no means a low turnout,” retired Justice Mughal noted.

“I congratulate the people for making the right decision. They rejected the path of violence and chose the power of the vote instead — a path of positive change that will produce beneficial results.”

Expressing regret over allegations levelled against the Election Commission, CEC Mughal said the electoral watchdog was a constitutional and autonomous institution whose responsibility was to conduct free, fair and impartial elections without favouring any party.

He said it was the state’s responsibility to provide full security and assist the Election Commission.

“We perform our duties in accordance with the Constitution and the law, and our conscience is clear.”

In view of Tuesday’s polling, the Muzaffarabad deputy commissioner has declared a public holiday across the district.

PML-N now has ‘simple majority’ to form govt: Rana Sana

As the unofficial results were released, Adviser to the Prime Minister on Political Affairs and PML-N leader Rana Sanaullah said his party had now gained the “simple majority” needed to form a government in AJK.

He was addressing a press conference alongside Minister for Kashmir Affairs and Gilgit-Baltistan Amir Muqam.

“We have the government-forming number,” he said, adding that “there are a total of 45 seats […] and out of 45, PML-N has so far secured 23 seats”.

The PML-N leader said his party had won in four of the seven territorial constituencies in Muzaffarabad while the PPP, which had been “attempting to build a rigging narrative since 10:30am yesterday”, had secured three.

Sanaullah demanded that the PPP must tell the people how they managed to secure three seats despite the alleged rigging.

“Did they succeed because of rigging or because of a free and fair election?”

Sanaullah further stated that the PML-N had also secured 10 out of 12 refugee seats while the PPP had won two.

“A democratic government, which has the people’s mandate, will now be formed in AJK, and it will work on ideological, economic, and political affairs of the region,” he said.

He added that a parliamentary party session of the PML-N would be called after the conclusion of the third phase of the elections for future decisions.

Speaking about PPP’s rigging allegations, the PML-N leader dismissed them and accused PPP of colluding with the proscribed Joint Awami Action Committee (JAAC) to disrupt the election process in Muzaffarabad.

“Anticipating PML-N’s win, PPP along with the action committee planned riots and [..] fired at the police personnel when they got there,” Sanaullah alleged.

He claimed that the incident created an atmosphere of fear in the area, which led to a lower turnout.

“We received at least 3,000 to 4,000 fewer votes due to this,” he claimed.

On PPP’s allegations that an attempt had been made on its candidate AJK Legislative Assembly Speaker Chaudhry Latif Akbar’s life, he accused the party of staging a “drama”. He also claimed that the PPP had refused to get Akbar’s medicolegal examination done.

Sanaullah accused the PPP of employing “dirty tricks” to sabotage the electoral process, saying that the PPP’s actions violated the Charter of Democracy, in which the party leadership had agreed that they would not “malign each other’s mandate with such dirty tricks”.

Replying to a question, he said the PPP had raised doubts over “high turnout” in constituencies where the PML-N’s candidate had won.

“With the kind of societal system in place in AJK, it is certainly possible that if there are 300 people in a village, 290 might show up to vote,” he said.

He asked the PPP to follow due process in case of complaints rather than “building a narrative and disrupting democracy and the election process”.

Federal govt’s last days have begun: Sharjeel

On the other hand, PPP’s Sharjeel Inam Memon said his party would continue to contest until the last phase of the AJK elections for the rights of Kashmiris despite what he described as “historical rigging”.

Addressing a press conference in Islamabad alongside PPP’s AJK chapter president Chaudhry Muhammad Yasin, Memon said, “PPP will fight for our Kashmiri brothers until the last moment.”

The Sindh senior minister accused the AJK CEC of being a PML-N supporter, alleging that the elections were being rigged in favour of the federal ruling party.

Referring to Sanaullah and Muqam’s press conference earlier in the day, Memon said they did not show any signs of guilt; rather, “they were proud of themselves for having stolen AJK’s mandate”.

He said that PPP would not resort to bad language and ridicule the way PML-N did.

Sharjeel claimed that in the Mirpur polls, PML-N candidates “stamped” ballot papers in LA-1, LA-5, LA-9, LA-11 and LA-12. He added that PPP had filed applications before the Election Commission against the alleged action but received no response.

“When the entire country knows that they won the 2024 elections through a donated mandate and rigging, but they have not accepted that to date, so how would they accept the rigging in AJK?” Memon claimed.

“I believe that the federal government’s last days have begun,” the PPP leader remarked.

Memon said that polling in LA-27 was postponed yesterday citing rainfall, despite there being no showers on Sunday in the area.

He contended that the Election Commission did not have the required capacity and could not arrange ballot materials on time.

In LA-28, only seven out of 10 union councils (UCs) were equipped for balloting, according to the Sindh minister. He said elections in the other three UCs would be held on Tuesday.

Memon also reiterated the PPP’s claim that acting AJK President Chaudhry Latif Akbar was attacked by PML-N workers while he was on his way to cast his vote.

He added that a PPP MNA was also fired upon and suffered a bullet injury on his hand when he went to a polling station in the same constituency.

“Kashmiris’ rights have been robbed for PML-N’s personal benefits,” the PPP leader said.

Meanwhile, Yasin noted that at 40 polling stations, voter turnout was between 85 and 99 per cent, adding that, on average, this figure was “no more than 40 to 45pc”.

Yasin also took exception to the phase-wise elections, saying that when the decision was announced, PPP workers had alerted their party chairman Bilawal that it was an “attempt to intensify rigging”.

Reports of violence

During the polling on Sunday, attempts were reportedly made to disrupt polling in some neighbourhoods of Muzaffarabad, but voting continued in most areas. In LA-31, Muzaffa­rabad-V (Khawra), clashes between workers of the PML-N and PPP were reported in Union Council Katkair.

The PPP alleged that one of its workers, Syed Mushtaq Shah, was killed in an attack by PML-N supporters. The PML-N rejected the allegation, claiming the man suffered a cardiac arrest following a scuffle between two groups. There was no independent confirmation of either claim.

PPP candidate and Legislative Assembly Speaker Akbar also wrote to the AJK chief election commissioner, alleging security lapses, firing incidents, interference in polling, prevention of polling agents from entering polling stations and denial of voting rights.

He also claimed there had been an attempt on his life in which Advocate Syed Mumtaz Hussain Naqvi was injured, and called for an investigation and legal action against those responsible. There was no immediate response from the Election Commission.

Clashes between workers of the two major parties, some involving the use of firearms, were also reported from other areas, though no casualties were immediately reported.

Low turnout outside AJK

Outside AJK, Kashmiris voted for their candidates vying for refugee seats at polling stations set up in Chakwal, Jhelum, Rawalpindi, Islamabad, Sialkot, Narowal, Sargodha, Attock, Nawabshah, Hyderabad, Mohmand, Mansehra, Quetta, Dera Ghazi Khan, Peshawar, Sanghar, and Naushahro Feroze.

Polling in these areas largely remained peaceful and recorded a low turnout. In Mohmand, not a single voter turned up at a station set up for the AJK polls. In Dera Ghazi Khan, a single registered female voter cast her ballot at the Govt Elementary School in Maumori, where a polling station had been established just for her.

Out of 12 refugee seats, seven seats are in Punjab, one seat is in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, one seat (Jammu-VI) is divided between Pun­jab, Islamabad, and Khyber Pakhtun­khwa, one seat is divided between Sindh and Balo­chistan (Valley-I), and one seat (Jammu-I) is shared among refugees living in Balochistan, Punjab, and Sindh. Valley-V seat is divided between Punjab and Islamabad.

World.title: Religious scholar killed in explosion at supermarket in South Waziristan's Wana
World.content:
LOWER SOUTH WAZIRISTAN: A religious scholar was killed in an explosion, suspected to have been caused by a pressure bomb, at a supermarket in Lower South Waziristan’s Wana on Monday, police said.

Wana Circle Deputy Superintendent of Police (DSP) Asghar Ali Shah told Dawn that the explosion occurred on the ground floor of a supermarket located in Rustam Bazaar.

He said Mufti Jana Mir Masti Khel sustained critical injuries in the explosion and was immediately shifted to Wana district headquarters hospital, where he succumbed to his injuries.

The DSP added that he and Wana City Police Station House Officer Usman Wazir, along with a large contingent of police, reached the site of the incident after the explosion, and the area was cordoned off while investigators collected forensic evidence.

The DSP said preliminary findings suggested that the pressure bomb had been planted in advance with the apparent intention of targeting the cleric.

He said police had filed an initial complaint and further investigation was under way to identify the perpetrators and determine the motive behind the attack.

In addition to his religious services, Mufti Jana Mir played a significant role in various national peace jirgas held after the 2004 military operations in Wana’s different areas.

Most recently, he participated in the Waziristan Peace Jirga, where he presented key recommendations aimed at restoring law and order and achieving sustainable peace in the area.

He was widely regarded as a respected religious and social figure who consistently advocated for regional and national interests and worked to promote lasting peace in the region.

Monday’s incident comes just three days after unidentified gunmen shot dead Maulana Ismail, a cleric affiliated with Jamiat Ulema-i-Islam-Fazl (JUI-F), in Azam Warsak Bazaar of Lower South Waziristan’s Birmal tehsil.

On July 28, a local cleric was killed and two other people were injured in a suspected quadcopter attack near a mosque in the Landi Doag area of Birmal.

World.title: AJK information secretary says 7 law enforcement personnel martyred in recent unrest
World.content:
Azad Jammu and Kashmir (AJK) Information Secretary Muhammad Rashid Hanif on Monday said that seven law enforcement personnel, including those of police and Rangers, were martyred during recent unrest in the region.

The now-proscribed Joint Awami Action Committee (JAAC), which has been demanding the abolishment of 12 seats in the local legislature reserved for refugees from Indian-held Kashmir, has been holding protests in the region for several weeks now.

Clashes took place between protesters and law enforcement personnel in Rawalakot and Mirpur last week, which reportedly resulted in several casualties. Amid the tensions, elections are being held across the region in three phases , with those in Mirpur (July 27) and Muzaffarabad divisions (Aug 2) marred by rigging allegations by the PPP.

In a televised address on Monday, Hanif recalled a press conference held on July 27 where a police official presented weapons allegedly recovered from JAAC members.

Hanif said that seven personnel were martyred from the “same weapons”, while 45 personnel suffered serious injuries and “numerous” others sustained minor injuries. He further said that police and Rangers vehicles were also burned.

“This confirms that the blacklisted JAAC is sheltering a large number of armed elements and is attempting to undermine peace and the writ of the state,” the information secretary asserted.

Addressing allegations by JAAC regarding incidents in Rawalakot and surrounding areas between July 27 and July 31, he said they were not only false but “part of a misinformation and propaganda campaign”, which in itself was part of a broader effort to “undermine public order and the writ of the state”.

He went on to stress that “security institutions of the AJK government have demonstrated the utmost restraint and professionalism while maintaining law and order”.

The information secretary rejected allegations of unprovoked firing by security forces and withholding bodies, stating that the government had no bodies presently in its custody.

“Propaganda being circulated by this banned organisation on social media is misleading and part of an effort to further aggravate the situation,” he added, alleging that JAAC members were involved in blocking or burning vehicles carrying essential supplies and food.

Hanif also provided the casualty figures for law enforcement personnel resulting from JAAC’s “violent actions” in recent years, noting one police official was martyred in 2024 and three personnel in October 2025.

“Two armed operatives from this organisation recently admitted in their confession that they were promised Rs10 million to kill one Rangers personnel, which raises serious concerns about the source of this group’s funding,” the AJK official claimed.

AJK govt calls BBC report ‘biased’; Al Jazeera’s coverage termed ‘selective’

Hanif also termed a BBC report on the Rawalakot clashes as “angled, biased and contrary to the facts”, saying that the AJK government “rejected” it.

“The facts and figures presented in this report are not only incorrect, but they were published without verification or confirmation from the government, police or the civil administration,” he stated, describing the report as “contrary to the ethics of journalism and professionalism”.

Contending that videos and press releases from the AJK administration had provided evidence of JAAC possessing modern weapons, he noted that the BBC “should have at least taken the verified evidence into account and published a report based on facts”.

Similarly, the Ministry of Information and Broadcasting criticised Al Jazeera’s coverage of the AJK elections, accusing the Qatar-based broadcaster of “selective reporting from handpicked polling stations” in Muzaffarabad.

In a post on X on Sunday night, the ministry alleged that the media outlet had “sought to misrepresent the AJK elections and the voting process” through “carefully chosen timings and scripted statements from selected individuals”.

“Such yellow journalism only confirms the agenda of external actors with vested interests who are attempting to delegitimise this electoral exercise and undermine the popular will of the people of Muzaffarabad and AJK,” it alleged.

The publication had reported that the residents of Muzaffarabad were observing a boycott of the polls following unrest in the region, where the proscribed JAAC has been protesting for several weeks.

Over the past two months, the regional administration and the JAAC have been at odds over various issues, most notably the committee’s demand to abolish the 12 seats in the region’s Legislative Assembly, which has resulted in protests across the region.

The government has accused militant elements “pu­r­­s­u­ing a foreign age­nda and backed by Indian funding” of fomenting the recent unrest in AJK.

On June 5, following the announcement of the JAAC’s June 9 strike, the AJK government declared the committee a proscribed organisation and placed it under the First Schedule of the region’s anti-terrorism act (ATA).

The next day, AJK authorities launched a crackdown on the JAAC, arresting scores of its leaders and later placing 147 of its activists on the Fourth Schedule of the ATA.

World.title: Islamabad ATC hands Mushtaq Ahmad to police on 3-day physical remand in protest case
World.content:
ISLAMABAD: An anti-terrorism court (ATC) has handed over former senator Mushtaq Ahmad Khan and other suspects to police on a three-day physical remand in a case registered in connection with a protest.

The police produced the former senator and another person named Daniyal before Duty Judge Rukhsanda Shaheen in the ATC.

During the hearing, the prosecution requested a 30-day physical remand of the suspects, stating that the police needed to recover a vehicle and weapons allegedly connected with the case.

After hearing the arguments, the court granted the police three-day physical remand of Mushtaq and the other suspects and directed that they be produced before the court again upon completion of the remand period.

The first information report (FIR) was registered at Islamabad’s Shalimar Police Station on July 31, on the complaint of Sub-inspector Ghulam Murtaza.

The FIR said Mushtaq and dozens of others had led a crowd of about 400-500 people and gathered in the capital’s F-10.

It accused the former senator of making “incendiary” speeches on loudspeakers, forcing shops to shut down, and chanting slogans against “current government institutions”.

According to the FIR, Mushtaq then led the protesters to Sambal Road with the intention of marching to the Main Jinnah Avenue Road and blocking roads.

The FIR said the district administration told Mushtaq through a loudspeaker to end the gathering as it was being held without a no-objection certificate (NOC), but the former senator and others blocked a main road near Shalimar Plaza at around 7:10pm.

It accused the protesters of vandalising a media DSNG vehicle and other private cars passing by, along with pelting stones and “attacking” police officials. It further claimed that some protesters snatched away anti-riot helmets from personnel and threatened them.

Last Wednesday, Mushtaq’s Pakistan Rights Movement (PRM) alleged that he had been detained by Punjab police on July 28 from Kahuta Bazaar while he was returning from Azad Pattan Bridge after allegedly being denied entry into AJK.

Senior police officers in Punjab had not responded to calls and messages at the time. Police officials in Rawalpindi approached by Dawn for comment spoke off the record and denied that Mushtaq was in their custody.

Mushtaq’s X account said the next day that he had been released. Following this, he had announced a gathering on July 31 in Islamabad’s F-10 to “express condolences, solidarity with Kashmir and for peace and reconciliation”.

Last week, activists in Lahore were detained while holding a peaceful demonstration outside the press club to show solidarity with the proscribed JAAC.

Additional input by Mohammad Asghar

World.title: PM Shehbaz directs completion of privatisation programmes according to agreed timelines
World.content:
ISLAMABAD: Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif on Monday directed officials to complete all stages of the government’s privatisation programme within the prescribed timelines.

Presiding over a meeting in Islamabad reviewing the privatisation of state-owned enterprises, the prime minister instructed relevant ministries and institutions to work in close coordination to ensure that all targets and deadlines under the privatisation programme were met, according to a statement issued by the Prime Minister’s Office (PMO).

The meeting was attended by Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Senator Muhammad Ishaq Dar, Federal Ministers Khawaja Muhammad Asif, Jam Kamal Khan, Ahad Khan Cheema, Sardar Awais Khan Leghari and other senior officials, the PMO said.

PM Shehbaz said the privatisation structure for the Zarai Taraqiati Bank Limited (ZBTL) should be designed in a way that safeguards the bank’s primary role in agricultural financing.

“It must be ensured that even after privatisation, the Zarai Taraqiati Bank’s focus on providing agricultural loans and financial resources to small and medium-scale farmers remains intact,” he was quoted as saying by the statement.

The premier noted that improving farmers’ access to financial resources was “essential” for increasing per-acre agricultural productivity, especially for small and medium-scale cultivators, adding that agricultural development remained critical to Pakistan’s economic growth and food security.

Officials from the privatisation ministry briefed the meeting on progress under the government’s privatisation programme and future targets. The meeting was told that 27 state-owned enterprises were included in the programme, which was being implemented in three phases.

According to the briefing, the financial closing process for the privatisation of Pakistan International Airlines (PIA) and First Women Bank has been completed. Officials said the first financial closing and transfer of management control of PIA were completed on June 29.

The meeting also reviewed progress on the planned privatisation of Islamabad Electric Supply Company (Iesco), Faisalabad Electric Supply Company (Fesco) and Gujranwala Electric Power Company (Gepco).

Officials said expressions of interest (EOIs) had been advertised for these companies, with submission deadlines set for Aug 7 for Fesco, Aug 21 for Gepco and Sep 7 for Iesco.

The meeting was also told that international companies have expressed interest in these distribution companies, while roadshows with investors are also underway, according to the PMO.

Fesco, Gepco and Iesco collectively serve more than 14 million consumers across major industrial, commercial and urban centres of Punjab, the Islamabad region, and parts of Azad Jammu and Kashmir.

The transaction offers investors an opportunity to acquire between 51 per cent and 100pc shareholding, along with management control, in each of the three distribution companies.

Officials also updated the prime minister on progress on the privatisation of ZTBL, stating that the transaction structure was being designed to protect the bank’s agricultural lending mandate.

The meeting further reviewed progress on the planned privatisation of Islamabad International Airport, Jinnah International Airport in Karachi and Allama Iqbal International Airport in Lahore.

The PM directed officials to maintain close oversight of all ongoing privatisation transactions and ensure their completion according to the agreed timelines.

The premier issued these instructions three days after Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi’s statement saying that the system had “collapsed”, and that things would not get fixed as long as “the present system is not reset”.

Presiding over a separate meeting on private investment, PM Shehbaz directed officials to prepare, at the earliest, a roadmap for establishing a private equity fund to promote investment, support small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) and encourage sustainable economic growth, according to his office.

He asked officials to submit a comprehensive plan for developing both Pakistan’s public equity market and a private equity fund to improve access to investment capital and help attract foreign investment.

“The promotion of private investment is essential for the country’s economic growth,” the premier said according to another statement issued by the PMO.

He said that private equity funds could serve as an effective catalyst for investment, business expansion and job creation, adding that sectors including mining, agriculture, livestock, energy and information technology had the potential to become key drivers of Pakistan’s economic growth.

PM Shehbaz said a stronger public equity market could provide an important financing avenue for investment in these sectors. He noted that the banking sector’s contribution to investment financing remained limited, making the development of alternative sources of capital increasingly important.

The premier noted that the government was prioritising policies aimed at strengthening the economy on a sustainable basis through private sector-led investment, industrial growth and export promotion.

DPM Dar, Minister of State Bilal Azhar Kayani, Special Assistant to the Prime Minister Haroon Akhtar, and senior government officials attended the meeting, the PMO said.

World.title: Bulls in charge as PSX opens week by gaining 2,100 points
World.content:
The Pakistan Stock Exchange (PSX) opened the week in the green on Monday, gaining more than 2,100 points to close above the 178,000 mark.

The development came as global oil prices tumbled on Monday, after United States President Donald Trump said fresh talks with Iran would begin later in the day.

At 11am, the benchmark KSE-100 index had gained 2273.78 points, from the previous close of 176,094.11 points. By 2:18pm, the index’s gains had dropped to 1781.72 points.

However, after an intraday low of 177,759.88 points, it staged a recovery after 2pm to close at 178,200.02 points — up by 2,105.91 (1.20 per cent) from the previous close.

Topline Securities Ltd. said that the rally reflected “renewed risk appetite as investors welcomed signs of easing regional tensions and softer energy prices”.

On the index contribution front, FFC, MEBL, LUCK, PPL, and ENGROH emerged as the top contributors, collectively adding approximately 699 points to the benchmark index, according to the firm.

Market activity also strengthened: the total traded volume rose to 785 million shares, while traded value stood at Rs33bn, it added.

Mettis Global, a web-based financial portal, said the positive momentum at PSX came as “investors took cues from easing geopolitical tensions after Trump called off a planned strike on Iran, reducing immediate concerns over a wider regional conflict”.

Awais Ashraf, director of research at AKD Securities, said investor optimism extended the positive momentum from the previous week, driven by expectations of a swift agreement between the US and Iran.

“Sentiment improved after the US president announced that talks with Iran would resume on Monday, without setting a deadline for reaching an agreement following the cessation of hostilities,” he said.

Ashraf added that “the return of inflation to single digits in July, with the data due to be released today, would provide an additional catalyst for the market by strengthening expectations of monetary easing and further boosting investor confidence”.

The KSE-100 index ended the first month of the current fiscal year lower. According to Topline Securities Ltd, the index closed July down 4,208 points or 2.3 per cent month-on-month as escalating US-Iran tensions pushed global crude oil prices higher, weighing on investor sentiment.

Average daily traded volume during the month stood at 845 million shares, while average daily traded value was Rs37.5bn.

Additional input from AFP

World.title: Iran denies negotiations with US after Trump announces talks
World.content:
